blocks.caption: The number of levels each kind of step of [[sem-labels]] consumes in the deadlock-free relation. \inmode{lf}{A cost table $\kappa$ assigns these numbers subject to four conditions. The lock-free relation uses $\kappa_L$, in which $\beta$ steps, creations, spawns and links are free.} A force costs one level\inmode{lf}{ in each table}. The [[e-rel|term relation]], the [[e-obl|obligations]] and the [[p-obls|process obligations]] read the cost of a step.
blocks.why: The costs fix how far the level drops at a step. In $\kappa_{DF}$ a send costs nothing, so the payload is passed on at the level of the continuation. A receive costs one, so the received value is read one level lower, where the relation is already defined. A force costs one, so a box reads its body one level lower, where its own variable is already in $V$. \inmode{lf}{A step of cost $0$ is read at the same level, so a thread cannot take infinitely many of them.}

blocks.title: The value relation
blocks.caption: Each rule is one clause of $V$ at a type of [[ty-grammar]], by recursion on the ordinal index and, within a level, on the type, the measure $\sym{rel.vsize}{(\alpha, \sym{sr.size}{\mathsf{size}}\,T)}$. $\Theta$ maps exactly the ends the [[syn-values|value]] owns, $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$ of [[syn-fends]]. An end is related at a session type [[ty-equiv|up to $\approx$]]. A closure is safe when its body is safe in each larger world of [[w-ext]], at each lower level, for each argument $w$ and each future of the caller above $u$. This is the semantic form of [[r-fun|E-Abs]]. A thunk, the closure that [[r-threads|$\mathsf{spawn}$]] runs, is read at the empty future. A box owns no end, and it is safe when its unrolled body $e[!e]$ is safe at each instance, as [[r-boxes|E-Force]] may pick, at each level a force below. An existential value is a value of the body at witness points whose facts hold, as [[r-ex|E-Pack]] states.
blocks.why: The clauses for closures and boxes quantify over larger worlds and lower levels. This quantification makes the relation compositional. A closure received from another component is safe in the joined world because it was safe in each extension of its own.

blocks.title: The term relation
blocks.caption: A term in $E$ is a [[syn-values|value]] in [[v-rel|$V$]] when it is irreducible and [[rd|ready]] when it is reducible. Each of its steps meets its [[e-obl|obligation]]. This holds at each index, $0$ included, and in each larger world of [[w-ext]]. After a step of cost $c > 0$ from [[ct-costs]] at the ordinal index $\alpha$ the successor is read at each $\beta$ with $\beta + c \leq \alpha$, and after a free step at $\alpha$ itself. At a limit index this is each smaller index. The three rows of [[sr-reading]] say the same in words.
blocks.why: The term relation is the center of the logical relation. Values, obligations and readiness are its three clauses. A free step is read inside the least fixpoint at the same level, so a term may take only finitely many free steps in a row before a step of positive cost.

blocks.title: Obligations of term steps
blocks.caption: Each step $e \xrightarrow{\ell} e'$ of a term holding $\Theta$ must meet $\mathsf{Obl}_\ell(e')$, and the successor is read at the lower indices the cost of [[ct-costs]] allows, as [[e-rel]] states. A $\beta$ step keeps the ends. A [[r-threads|spawn]] gives the child exactly the ends of its thunk, by $\mathsf{fends}$ of [[syn-fends]], and a [[r-new|creation]] adds two dual ends at a fresh base or at a field. A send gives away exactly the ends of its payload, instantiated as in [[ty-payload]], and a receive is safe for each value that may arrive. A close removes the end, a choice moves it to the field of the branch, and a link removes two dual ends. These are the semantic counterparts of the [[r-act|action rules]]. A creation places $c^{+}$ at a position $\pi$, and a message has a payload value $w$.
blocks.why: The obligations say how each step changes ownership and points. The relation reads step labels only here. O-New chooses the position and the facts of the new channel inside the relation, so the semantics never reads a type, and the fundamental theorem supplies the choice of E-New.

blocks.title: Readiness
blocks.caption: A stuck term offers below everything it keeps and below its future. A stuck process has an offer below each end it keeps. $\mathsf{offered}\,t$ is the set of ends on which $t$ can act. $\Theta|_A$ is the set of points of the ends of $\Theta$ in $A$, $\Theta \setminus A$ the set of points of the other ends of $\Theta$, and the bar takes dual points. $A \prec_W B$ holds when $W \vdash x \prec y$ for each $x \in A$ and $y \in B$, in the order of [[w-order]]. Internal channels have no points. The [[e-rel|term relation]] and the [[p-rel|process relation]] ask readiness of each reducible term and process.
blocks.why: In a strict order some stuck thread waits at a minimal point, and the thread holding the dual end can act with that thread. Adequacy uses this argument to derive deadlock freedom from readiness. This is the semantic form of the [[t-side|side conditions]] of typing.
blocks.example: A thread that offers $\mathsf{close}\,c$ at $x$ while it holds $d$ at $y$ is ready iff $W \vdash x \prec \overline{y}$. The thread with $\overline{d}$ that offers its close at $\overline{y}$ while it holds $\overline{c}$ at $\overline{x}$ needs $\overline{y} \prec x$. A strict order cannot hold both facts, so one of the two threads is not ready, and the pair is in no process relation.

blocks.title: The process relation
blocks.formula:
\begin{array}{c}\begin{array}{l}
\sym{P.zero}{\forall p.\ p \in \sym{th.Prel}{P^{W}_{0}\llbracket \Sigma \vdash T \rrbracket}} \\

blocks.caption: Internal steps, including messages between two threads of $p$, keep the interface and read the successor at the lower indices the cost of the event in [[ct-costs]] allows. A message with the outside moves ends across the interface. A send gives away its payload ends, including the ends $\Theta_e$ of internal channels, and a receive must be safe for each value that may arrive at each lower level. The [[p-rel|process relation]] asks these at each step, and they mirror the [[e-rel|term obligations]] with the interface $\Sigma$ in place of $\Theta$.
blocks.why: Each case says how the interface changes at a step and where the successor must be safe.

blocks.title: Relation and fuel side by side
blocks.caption: Fuel is a second predicate on a thread, separate from the relation and with the same shape, a value clause and one obligation per step. The relation gives each end a point, $S_x$, and [[fu|fuel]] gives it a counter and tickets, $S^{f,m}$. The [[soup|lock-free process relation]] requires both of each thread. The relation makes a stuck thread ready, and fuel bounds how often the thread holding a dual end acts on other ends first. \inmode{lf}{Fuel holds ends $\Phi$ and returns within $d$ actions.}
blocks.why: The table compares what the relation and fuel read and guarantee. The lock-free process relation requires both.

cells.text: a stuck wait, and at $\kappa_L$ a loop of free steps

blocks.title: Fuel
blocks.caption: Fuel has the shape of the term relation $E$ without the ready clause. $e \in F^N_\alpha\llbracket \Phi \vdash \sigma\ !\ d\rrbracket$ says that the thread $e$, which holds the ends $\Phi$ with their counters and tickets, has fuel at the index $\alpha$. When $e$ is a value it is in $FV$ of [[fv]] at $\sigma$. Otherwise each step meets its [[fu-obls|fuel obligation]] one level lower. The frame $d$ bounds the actions before the thread returns, and $g$ renames the held ends. [[fu-vs]] sets fuel beside the relation.
blocks.why: Fuel bounds how often a thread acts on other ends before it acts on an end it holds. Lock-free adequacy measures waits with these counters and tickets. Fuel is separate from the relation because it reads no point and no world. It is the run-time form of the [[t-lf-counters|counters]] of typing.

blocks.title: Fuel obligations
blocks.caption: An action on $o$ requires $o$ held and not idle, and a positive counter on the other ends that are not idle and on the frame. It uses one unit of the frame, advances the protocol of $o$, resets the counter of $o$ to its tickets $m$ and decrements the other counters, written $\Phi{\downarrow}[o \mapsto S^{m,m}]$. A force is an action on no end. It asks a positive counter on each held end that is not idle and on the frame, and it decrements each of these counters. The free steps decrement no counter, and a spawn hands the ends of its thunk on at their counters. A new channel starts each end at its tickets. A send hands the ends of its payload on with their counters minus one, read in [[fv]]. A link lowers no counter and asks the counter of each linked end to exceed $N - m$ for the tickets $m$ of the other. A send has a payload value $w$, and $d$ is the frame. [[fu]] asks these obligations at each step.
blocks.why: Each kind of step changes the held ends, counters and tickets in one way, the same at each level. The rules of the [[t-lf-counters|counters block]] are their static images, credit for the counter and the same resets, decrements and link condition.

blocks.title: Values with fuel
blocks.caption: Values with fuel by recursion on the type. The counter of an end is at least its [[t-lf-counters|credit]]. A closure keeps the counters of its captured ends that are not idle at least at its credit $a$. Its body has fuel at each call whose counters are at least the counters at creation minus $a$. A box holds no end, and its body has fuel at each force. The [[fu-obls|fuel obligations]] read $FV$ at payloads and thunks.
blocks.why: Values with fuel connect credits in types with counters at run time.

blocks.title: The lock-free process relation
blocks.caption: An annotated configuration $a = (q, K, W_a)$ is a configuration $q$ with an ownership map $K$ and the ranked world $W_a$ of its run so far. $K$ gives each held end the thread that holds it, its point, its counter and its tickets. The configuration is in the lock-free process relation at the ordinal index $\alpha$ when each thread is in $E[\kappa_L]$ at the ends it owns and has [[fu|fuel]] at their counters, the two columns of [[fu-vs]]. $A$ and $\Phi$ describe the held ends for the relation and for fuel, and $\mathsf{consistent}$ requires $A$, $\Phi$ and $K$ to agree. It also bounds each counter by its tickets and the tickets of the two ends of an internal channel by $N$, the bound of the [[t-lf-counters|counters block]]. Fuel occurs only in this definition.
blocks.why: The lock-free process relation combines the relation and the fuel of each thread over one ownership map. Lock-free adequacy reads the points and counters that $K$ records, and the invariant on tickets makes the measure fall at a link.

blocks.title: Semantic judgments
blocks.caption: The semantic judgments quantify over ordinal indices, larger worlds and substitutions, and read the static future at each of its denotations. A term is in the [[e-rel|term relation]] under each grounding $\gamma$ of its variables, and a process in the [[p-rel|process relation]] at each index. The process judgment at a world $W$ holds at each consistent extension of $W$\inmode{lf}{, a strict one for deadlock freedom}. A grounding $\gamma$ in the relation $G$ on contexts substitutes values for the variables of $\Delta$, and the set $Y$ denotes the rest of a future. \inmode{lf}{The lock-free judgment at the bound $N$ holds at each ranked extension of $W$ and chooses the annotated configuration of the [[soup|lock-free process relation]] at each index. The creation choice of each channel is an existential inside O-New.}
blocks.why: The fundamental theorems conclude the semantic judgments, and adequacy takes a semantic judgment as its premise. The judgment at a world is what makes a component reusable. It holds at each consistent extension of the world, so a component composed with another is read at an extension of the join.

sections.title: Theorems
sections.intro: Typed closed processes are deadlock free, and the proof goes through the logical relation. The section opens with the chain of results and then states each of them for processes. The lemmas about terms come last. The deadlock-free results, binary and n-ary, take no classical hypothesis. \inmode{lf}{The lock-free results stand next to their deadlock-free counterparts and take excluded middle and functional choice as explicit hypotheses.}

blocks.title: How the results fit together
blocks.caption: Typing gives the semantic judgment at the world $W$ of the derivation, and that judgment gives deadlock freedom. Both steps use the relation $(V, E, P)$ at the step costs $\kappa_{DF}$ over consistent worlds, and neither needs a classical hypothesis. The arrows are proved in [[th-fund-proc]], [[th-adeq]] and [[th-terms]]. \inmode{lf}{Lock freedom uses the same relation at $\kappa_L$, which excludes divergence by free steps, together with fuel, over ranked worlds, the two columns of [[fu-vs]]. The lock-free process relation combines both for each thread. Lock-free adequacy measures a wait on $o$ by $\mu(t) = (\varrho(x), f)$. The ownership map $K$ of [[soup]] records the point $x$ of $o$ and the counter $f$ of the dual end $\overline{o}$. A step of the thread holding $\overline{o}$ on another end decreases $f$, which F-Count keeps at $1$ or more. A force of that thread decreases $f$ as well, by F-Force. A link gives the waiting end a dual end with a lower counter, by the premise of E-Link and the bound on tickets. So the thread holding $\overline{o}$ acts on $\overline{o}$ after finitely many steps. Excluded middle enters at the creations under $\mathsf{gen\_new}$ and at the existential property of ordinal indices.}
blocks.why: Each arrow is one theorem of this section. \inmode{lf}{The lock-free rows show what lock freedom adds to the deadlock-free proof.}

blocks.caption: A closed typed process is deadlock free, the property of [[sem-props]], and so is a closed n-ary composite whose component worlds have a consistent join by [[w-wf]]. No classical hypothesis enters. The proof combines [[th-fund-proc]] and [[th-adeq]] for the rules of [[p-typing]]. \inmode{lf}{At $\kappa_L$ it also has no divergence by free steps. Under excluded middle, dependent choice and functional choice, a closed process typed at a finite bound $N$ over a well-founded world of [[t-lf-wf]] is lock free. A weakly fair maximal run of the process exists under the same hypotheses, so the statement is not vacuous. Dependent choice serves the run alone, and lock freedom follows without dependent choice. For each reachable configuration in which a thread is pending, some configuration reachable from it has a step in which that thread takes part.}
blocks.why: These are the main results. The n-ary form handles rings, such as the [[ex-ring3|three-thread ring]]. Three components that are consistent two at a time and inconsistent together are rejected, because the check reads the joined order.

The [[ex-flag|self-computed flag]] uses this to combine a thread proved safe by its reductions with typed threads.

blocks.title: Fundamental theorem
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{l}\sym{th.fundamental-proc}{\begin{array}{l}\Sigma \sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash\inmode{lf}{^{\infty}}_W} p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Sigma \mathrel{\sym{sj.sw}{\vDash}}_{W} p : T\end{array}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.live-fundamental-proc}{\begin{array}{l}\Sigma \sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash\inmode{lf}{^{\infty}}_W} p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Sigma \mathrel{\sym{sj.sw}{\vDash[\kappa_L]}}_{W} p : T\end{array}}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-fundamental}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.em}{\mathsf{EM}} \land \Sigma \sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_W} p : T \land N \in \mathbb{N} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Sigma \mathrel{\sym{sp.lfsem}{\Vvdash}}^{N}_{W} p : T\end{array}}} \\[1.5ex] \sym{th.ptyped-apart}{\begin{array}{l}\Sigma_1 \sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_1}} p_1 : T_1 \land \Sigma_2 \sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_2}} p_2 : T_2 \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \exists \pi_1, \pi_2.\ \Sigma_i \mathrel{\sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash}}\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{\pi_i W_i} p_i : T_i \land A'_1 \cap A'_2 \subseteq \sym{tp.iface}{\mathsf{I}(\Sigma_1, T_1)} \cap \mathsf{I}(\Sigma_2, T_2)\end{array}} \\[1.5ex] \sym{th.ptyped-ren}{\begin{array}{l}\Sigma \sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_W} p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \pi\Sigma \mathrel{\sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash}}\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{\pi W} p : \pi T\end{array}} \\[1.5ex] \sym{th.typed-ren}{\begin{array}{l}\Gamma ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W} e : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \pi\Gamma ; \pi\Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{\pi F}_{\pi W} e : \pi T\end{array}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: A typed process is in the semantic judgment of [[sj-all]] at the world $W$ of its derivation. The proof is one induction on the derivation. The case of P-Term is the fundamental theorem for terms of [[th-terms]], and the case of P-Connect composes the two components at the join of their worlds. \inmode{lf}{Under excluded middle the same holds at a finite bound, with the lock-free judgment.} Its cases are the rules of [[p-typing]] and the composition rules of [[th-compose]]. A bijection $\pi$ on constants renames a derivation to one at $\pi W$. Two derivations renamed by bijections $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ that fix their interfaces share only interface constants. The bases $A^{\prime}_1$ of $\pi_1 W_1$ and $A^{\prime}_2$ of $\pi_2 W_2$ meet inside both interfaces.
blocks.why: The fundamental theorem connects typing with the relation.

blocks.title: Adequacy
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{c}\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.adequacy}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.acyc}{\mathsf{cons}}\,W \land \sym{sj.proc}{\forall \alpha.\ p \in \sym{th.Prel}{P^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \varnothing \vdash T \rrbracket}} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.df}{\mathsf{deadlock\_free}}\,p\end{array}} \\[1.5ex] \sym{th.adequacy-h}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.acyc}{\mathsf{cons}}\,W \land \varnothing \mathrel{\sym{sj.sw}{\vDash}}_W p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.df}{\mathsf{deadlock\_free}}\,p\end{array}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.live-sub-df}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.em}{\mathsf{EM}} \land \sym{th.ac}{\mathsf{FC}} \land \sym{ty.tfree}{\mathsf{tfree}}\,T \land \sym{th.boxfree}{\mathsf{boxfree}}\,T \land \forall \alpha.\ p \in \sym{th.Prel}{P[\kappa_L]^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \varnothing \vdash T \rrbracket} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \forall \alpha.\ p \in \sym{th.Prel}{P[\kappa_{DF}]^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \varnothing \vdash T \rrbracket}\end{array}}}\end{array}\inmodeplain{lf}{\\[3ex]}\inmode{lf}{\begin{array}{l}\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-adequacy}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.kind}{\mathsf{ranked}}\,W \land \forall \alpha.\ \exists a.\ \sym{proc.erase}{\mathsf{erase}}(\sym{th.qa}{q_a}) = p \land a \in \sym{th.soup}{S^{N,W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \varnothing \vdash T \rrbracket} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.lf}{\mathsf{lock\_free}}\,p\end{array}}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-thread-progress}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.kind}{\mathsf{ranked}}\,W \land \forall \alpha.\ \exists a.\ \sym{proc.erase}{\mathsf{erase}}(\sym{th.qa}{q_a}) = p \land a \in \sym{th.soup}{S^{N,W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \varnothing \vdash T \rrbracket} \land \sym{prop.notau}{\mathsf{no\_tau\_divergence}}\,p \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \begin{array}{l}\forall (r, l).\ \sym{proc.erase}{\mathsf{erase}}\,(\sym{se.run}{r\,0}) = p \land \sym{prop.maximal}{\mathsf{maximal}}\,(r, l) \land \sym{prop.wfair}{\mathsf{wfair}}\,(r, l) \\ \quad \Longrightarrow\ \sym{th.tpr}{\mathsf{thread\_progress\_run}}\,(r, l)\end{array}\end{array}}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-sems-adequacy}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.em}{\mathsf{EM}} \land \sym{th.ac}{\mathsf{FC}} \land \sym{w.lfworld}{\mathsf{wf}}\,W \land \varnothing \sym{sp.lfsem}{\Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}}_W p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.lf}{\mathsf{lock\_free}}\,p\end{array}}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-tp-gen}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{prop.lf}{\mathsf{lock\_free}}\,p \land \sym{prop.notau}{\mathsf{no\_tau\_divergence}}\,p \land \sym{th.linksr}{\mathsf{links\_restricted}}\,p \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \begin{array}{l}\forall (r, l).\ \sym{proc.erase}{\mathsf{erase}}\,(\sym{se.run}{r\,0}) = p \land \sym{prop.maximal}{\mathsf{maximal}}\,(r, l) \land \sym{prop.wfair}{\mathsf{wfair}}\,(r, l) \\ \quad \Longrightarrow\ \sym{th.tpr}{\mathsf{thread\_progress\_run}}\,(r, l)\end{array}\end{array}}}\end{array}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: A closed process in the process relation at each index at a consistent world is deadlock free. So is a closed process in the semantic judgment of [[sj-all]] at a well-formed consistent world, which is its own consistent extension by [[w-ext]]. The proof reads the readiness of [[rd]]. \inmode{lf}{A closed process in the lock-free judgment at a [[t-lf-wf|ranked world]] is lock free, as [[sem-props]] defines over the [[sem-events|events]] of a run. When $p$ has no internal divergence, each thread progresses on each weakly fair maximal run. The measure is the rank of the awaited point and the counter that the [[soup|lock-free process relation]] records. At a well-founded world of typing this needs excluded middle and functional choice. Under excluded middle and functional choice, a closed process in the semantic judgment at $\kappa_L$ is in the one at $\kappa_{DF}$ when its result type holds no end and no box.}
blocks.why: Adequacy connects the relation with the safety property. In a stuck configuration each thread is ready, so each offered end lies below the dual points of the ends its thread keeps. A minimal offered point then has its dual end offered too, and the two threads can step.

blocks.title: Conservativity
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{l}\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.conservative}{\begin{array}{l}(\exists \varepsilon.\ \Gamma;\sym{th.df}{\Delta_{df}} \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,\infty}} e : T_{df}\ !\ \varepsilon) \\ \quad\iff\ \Gamma ; \Delta_{df} \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W} e : T_{df}\end{array}}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.typed-dftyped}{\begin{array}{l}\Gamma ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} e : T\ !\ \varepsilon \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Gamma ; \Delta_{df} \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_W e : T_{df}\end{array}}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: The annotated judgment at $N = \infty$, with the annotations of [[ty-ann]] at $\infty$, types the same terms as deadlock-free typing, and erasing the annotations of a lock-free typing gives a deadlock-free typing.
blocks.why: Lock-free typing therefore rejects no deadlock-free program.

blocks.title: Lemmas about terms

\Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W} \sym{syn.letu}{\mathsf{let}}\ \ast = \sym{prim.close}{\mathsf{close}}\,a\ \sym{syn.letu}{\mathsf{in}}\ \sym{prim.close}{\mathsf{close}}\,b : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Gamma \mathrel{\sym{ctx.slt}{\vdash}} x \prec \overline{y}\end{array}}\\[3ex]\sym{th.Erel-bind}{\begin{array}{l}\begin{array}{l}e \in \sym{th.Erel}{E^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \Theta_1 \vdash T\rrbracket^{F \cup \sym{ty.heads}{\mathsf{ap}}\,\Theta_2}} \\ \land\ \forall W' \sym{w.ext}{\sqsupseteq} W,\ \beta \leq \alpha,\ v \in \sym{th.Vrel}{V^{W'}_{\beta}\llbracket\Theta_v \vdash T\rrbracket}. \\ \qquad \sym{se.frame}{f[v]} \in \sym{th.Erel}{E^{W'}_{\beta}\llbracket \Theta_v \cup \Theta_2 \vdash U\rrbracket^{F}}\end{array} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{se.frame}{f[e]} \in \sym{th.Erel}{E^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \Theta_1 \cup \Theta_2 \vdash U\rrbracket^{F}}\end{array}}\inmodeplain{lf}{\\[3ex]}\inmode{lf}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.cost-fundamental}{\begin{array}{l}\Gamma ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} e : T\ !\ \varepsilon \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{cs.csem}{\Delta \mathrel{\sym{sj.term}{\vDash}}^{N} e : T\ !\ \varepsilon}\end{array}} \\[1.5ex] \sym{th.fsem-of-cost}{\begin{array}{l}\varnothing ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{\varnothing}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} e : T\ !\ c \land \sym{ty.tfree}{\mathsf{tfree}}\,T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{fu.fsem}{\mathsf{fsem}\,N\,\sym{th.styof}{\Delta\inmode{lf}{^{N}}}\,e}\end{array}}\end{array}}\\[3ex]\sym{th.let-var}{\begin{array}{l}\Gamma ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W} e : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Gamma ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W} \sym{syn.let}{\mathsf{let}}\ x = e\ \sym{syn.let}{\mathsf{in}}\ x : T \\[1.5ex]f : \sym{ty.box}{\Box}\,\sym{ty.ex}{\exists}\iota.\,\sym{ty.unit}{\ast} \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}} \sym{syn.let}{\mathsf{let}}\ x = \sym{prim.force}{\mathsf{force}}\,f\ \sym{syn.let}{\mathsf{in}}\ x : \ast \\ \quad\land\ f : \Box\,\exists\iota.\,\ast \mathrel{\not\vdash} \mathsf{force}\,f : \ast\end{array}}\\[3ex]\sym{th.pinst}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.wf}{\mathsf{world\_wf}}\,W \land \sym{th.hinst}{\Gamma' \vdash \sigma(\Gamma)} \ \land\ \Gamma ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W} e : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Gamma' ; \sigma(\Delta) \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{\sigma(F)}_{W} e : \sigma(T)\end{array}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: A closed program is sound as a one-thread process over a consistent world. Typing a term implies the semantic term judgment of [[sj-all]] at each consistent extension of its world. $E$ is closed under the evaluation frames of [[sem-ctx]], which the case of [[r-fun|E-App]] and the other rules with subterms use. Two closes in sequence need the point of the first below the dual point of the second, which the rejections of the [[ex-flag|self-computed flag]] and of the [[ex-gennew|creations with exits]] use. A term bound to $x$ and returned types wherever the term itself types, and the converse fails for a forced box of an existential. A derivation stays a derivation when a substitution $\sigma$ instantiates its point variables, over each context $\Gamma'$ that derives the instantiated facts. \inmode{lf}{The rejection of [[ex-forkjoin|recursive fork-join]] at a finite bound uses the same lemma. A typed term is in the relation at $\kappa_L$. At a finite bound and under excluded middle this holds at each consistent extension, ranked ones included. A typed term at a finite bound with the annotations of [[ty-ann]] has [[fu|fuel]], with its values in [[fv]].}
blocks.why: The proofs of the process results use these lemmas, each proved rule by rule. Each typing rule has one compatibility lemma, and the fundamental theorem is the induction over the derivation.

syn.var.title: Variable
syn.var.meaning: A de Bruijn index $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of binders between the occurrence and its binder.
syn.var.why: A plain term former. With de Bruijn indices, substitution $e[v]$ and renaming need no side condition on fresh names. Examples write named binders, such as $\lambda x.\,x$ for $\lambda\,0$.
syn.var.example: In $\lambda e$ the variable $0$ of $e$ is the argument.

args.name: i
args.meaning: A de Bruijn index $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of binders between the occurrence and its binder.

syn.unit.title: Unit value $\ast$
syn.unit.meaning: The unit value $\ast$, with $V\llbracket\Theta \vdash \ast\rrbracket$ only at $\Theta = \varnothing$.
syn.unit.why: A plain term former. $\mathsf{close}$, $\mathsf{link}$ and $\mathsf{spawn}$ return $\ast$, and in a terminated process each thread but the main thread is $\ast$.

syn.end.title: End value $o$
syn.end.meaning: The value $o$ names one end of a channel, the only channel name in terms.
syn.end.why: Each end has its own name $c^{+}$ or $c^{-}$, and $\mathsf{select}_i\,o$ and $\mathsf{branch}\,o$ return the same name $o$. Hence no step of the semantics reads a point.
syn.end.example: $\mathsf{new} \xrightarrow{\mathsf{new}\,c} \langle c^{+}, c^{-}\rangle$ returns the two end values of $c$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: An end $o \in \mathsf{End}$, one of $c^{+}, c^{-}$ for a channel $c$.

syn.lam.title: $\lambda$-abstraction
syn.lam.meaning: A one-argument closure $\lambda e$, a value for each $e$ because no frame has its hole under $\lambda$.
syn.lam.why: A plain term former and the value form of a user function.
syn.lam.example: $\lambda x.\,\mathsf{send}\,x$ is $\mathsf{send}$ as a function value.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The body, $e \in \mathsf{Expr}$, with the argument as index $0$.

syn.app.title: Application
syn.app.meaning: Application, left to right, with $(\lambda e)\,v \xrightarrow{\beta} e[v]$.
syn.app.why: A plain term former. It is the only way to run a closure, received or built.

args.name: e_2
args.meaning: The argument, evaluated once $e_1$ is a value.

syn.pair.title: Pair
syn.pair.meaning: A pair $\langle e_1, e_2\rangle$, evaluated left to right, a value iff both components are values.
syn.pair.why: A plain term former. $\mathsf{send}$ takes a pair $\langle v, o\rangle$ and $\mathsf{recv}$ returns one.

syn.letu.title: Unit elimination
syn.letu.meaning: $\mathsf{let}\ \ast = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$ evaluates $e_1$ to $\ast$ and then steps to $e_2$ by $\beta$.
syn.letu.why: A plain term former. It sequences $e_1$ before $e_2$ when $e_1$ returns $\ast$, and the derived $\mathsf{let}$ uses it to discard its unit component.

args.name: e_1
args.meaning: A term of type $\ast$, evaluated first.

syn.letp.title: Pair elimination
syn.letp.meaning: $\mathsf{let}\ \langle a, b\rangle = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$ evaluates $e_1$ to $\langle v_1, v_2\rangle$ and steps to $e_2[v_1, v_2]$ by $\beta$.
syn.letp.why: A plain term former and the only eliminator of $\otimes$. A $\mathsf{recv}$ returns $\langle v, o\rangle$, and the continuation reads $v$ and $o$ through the pair elimination.

args.name: e_1
args.meaning: A term that returns a pair $\langle v_1, v_2\rangle$.

args.name: a, b
args.meaning: The bound variables, $a$ at index $1$ for $v_1$ and $b$ at index $0$ for $v_2$.

args.name: e_2
args.meaning: The body, in scope of $a$ and $b$.

syn.let.title: Derived let
syn.let.meaning: $\mathsf{let}\ a = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2 := \mathsf{let}\ \langle a, u\rangle = \langle e_1, \ast\rangle\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{let}\ \ast = u\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$ with $u$ fresh.
syn.let.why: The abbreviation binds one variable without a $\lambda$, so its body keeps the ends of the context and the typing needs no lower point $l$ for these ends. It uses only $\otimes$ and $\ast$.
syn.let.breaks: Written as $(\lambda a.\,e_2)\,e_1$ instead, the $\lambda$ must bound the dual points of the ends it captures by one lower point $l$. After $\mathsf{let}\ \langle a, a'\rangle = \mathsf{new}$ at a fresh base the ends $a, a'$ are at $\rho$ and $\overline{\rho}$, which have no common lower bound, and the body does not type.
syn.let.example: $\mathsf{let}\ p = \mathsf{force}\,mk\,\ast\ \mathsf{in}\ e$ keeps the ends of the context in $e$.

args.name: a
args.meaning: The bound variable, standing for the value of $e_1$.

args.name: u
args.meaning: A variable not free in $e_2$, bound to the unit component.

syn.inj.title: Injection
syn.inj.meaning: $\mathsf{inj}_i\,e$ for $i \in \{1, 2\}$, a value when $e$ is a value.
syn.inj.why: A plain term former. $\mathsf{branch}\,o$ returns $\mathsf{inj}_i\,o$, and $i$ records which choice arrived.

syn.case.title: Case
syn.case.meaning: $\mathsf{case}\ e\,(a.e_1)\,(a.e_2)$ evaluates $e$ to $\mathsf{inj}_i\,v$ and steps to $e_i[v]$ by $\beta$.
syn.case.why: A plain term former and the only eliminator of $\oplus$. It consumes the result of $\mathsf{branch}$.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The scrutinee, a term that returns $\mathsf{inj}_i\,v$.

args.name: a
args.meaning: The variable bound to $v$ in each branch, index $0$.

syn.box.title: Box $!e$
syn.box.meaning: A recursive thunk value whose body binds the box at index $0$, $\mathsf{force}\,(!e) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{force}} e[!e]$.
syn.box.why: One former gives recursion and replication. The value relation asks $\Theta = \varnothing$ and $\mathsf{fends}(e) = \varnothing$ of a box, so copying a box duplicates no end.
syn.box.example: $!(f = \lambda x.\,\mathsf{let}\ \langle v, x'\rangle = \mathsf{recv}\,x\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{force}\,f\,x')$ is a server loop.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The body, with the box itself as index $0$.

syn.new.title: $\mathsf{new}$
syn.new.meaning: $\mathsf{new} \xrightarrow{\mathsf{new}\,c} \langle c^{+}, c^{-}\rangle$ for a fresh channel $c$. The typing places $c^{+}$ at a fresh base $\rho$ and $c^{-}$ at $\overline{\rho}$ under an existential with a constraint $C$, or at a field $x\cdot\kappa$ and its dual with no constraint.
syn.new.why: The term names no point. The position and the constraint are part of the type of $\mathsf{new}$, which the typing derivation chooses. Each ordering of a new channel is therefore available without program syntax.
syn.new.breaks: With the position or the facts in the term, each held end that the facts mention is an argument that $\mathsf{new}$ takes and returns, because ends are linear.

args.name: \rho
args.meaning: The fresh base of $c^{+}$, bound by the existential.

args.name: C
args.meaning: The facts of the creation at a fresh base.

args.name: x\cdot\kappa
args.meaning: A field, the other position E-New-Field allows.

syn.op.title: Constant application $k\,e$
syn.op.meaning: The term $k\,e$ applies the constant $k$ to its argument $e$. It evaluates $e$ to a value $v$ and then takes the head step of $k$ on $v$. A constant never occurs without its argument, so $k\,e$ is never a value.
syn.op.why: The constants are the operations on channels, boxes and threads, and one term former covers each constant. Each constant has its own typing rule. A constant passed as a function is written as its eta-expansion $\lambda x.\,k\,x$.

prim.send.title: $\mathsf{send}$
prim.send.why: The label contains the payload $v$. The value relation is exact, $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$ for $v$ in $V$ at $\Theta$, so the ends that leave the thread are determined by $v$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S, S'
args.meaning: The session type of the end before the action and its continuation.

args.name: T, m
args.meaning: The payload type and the number $m$ of point variables it binds, instantiated at the fields $x\cdot i$.

prim.recv.title: $\mathsf{recv}$
prim.recv.why: A receive has a step for each value, so it can match the send on the dual end whatever value is sent. The session type of $o$ restricts the $v$ the relation considers.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S, S'
args.meaning: The session type of the end before the action and its continuation.

args.name: T, m
args.meaning: The payload type and the number $m$ of point variables it binds, instantiated at the fields $x\cdot i$.

prim.close.title: $\mathsf{close}$
prim.close.meaning: $\mathsf{close}\,o \xrightarrow{o\,\mathsf{end}} \ast$. The process step pairs it with $\mathsf{close}\,\overline{o}$ and removes $\mathsf{ech}\,o$ from $C$.
prim.close.why: A plain constant. A session type ends in $\mathsf{Close}$, and after both closes no thread holds an end of the channel.
prim.close.example: $\mathsf{close}\,c^{+}$ in one thread and $\mathsf{close}\,c^{-}$ in another.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S, S'
args.meaning: The session type of the end before the action and its continuation.

prim.select.title: $\mathsf{select}_i$
prim.select.meaning: $\mathsf{select}_i\,o \xrightarrow{o \lhd i} o$ for $i \in \{\mathsf{false}, \mathsf{true}\}$, where $\mathsf{false}$ selects the first branch.
prim.select.why: The end continues at $\overline{x\cdot\kappa_i}$, a point that depends on $i$. Hence the two branches are ordered independently.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S, S', S''
args.meaning: The session type before the action, and its two continuations, $S'$ for $\mathsf{false}$ and $S''$ for $\mathsf{true}$.

prim.branch.title: $\mathsf{branch}$
prim.branch.why: A plain constant that receives the choice of $\mathsf{select}_i$ on the dual end. The injection $\mathsf{inj}_i$ passes the chosen $i$ to the program.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S, S', S''
args.meaning: The session type before the action and the two continuations.

prim.link.title: $\mathsf{link}$
prim.link.meaning: $\mathsf{link}\,\langle o_1, o_2\rangle \xrightarrow{\leftrightarrow\{o_1, o_2\}} \ast$. The process step removes $\mathsf{ech}\,o_1$ and renames each thread by $\mathsf{csub}\,o_1\,o_2$.
prim.link.why: A link forwards a conversation without relaying messages. \inmode{lf}{It acts on no protocol, so it costs $0$ in both cost tables, and in the fuel layer it lowers no counter.}

args.name: \overline{S}_{\overline{x}}
args.meaning: The second, at the dual type and the dual point.

prim.spawn.title: $\mathsf{spawn}$
prim.spawn.meaning: $\mathsf{spawn}\,v \xrightarrow{\mathsf{spawn}\,v} \ast$, and the process starts a thread running $v\,\ast$.
prim.spawn.why: The label contains the thunk $v$. The value relation is exact, so the child holds exactly the ends $\mathsf{fends}(v)$ and the parent keeps the rest.
prim.spawn.example: $\mathsf{spawn}\,(\lambda u.\,\mathsf{let}\ \ast = u\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{close}\,d')$ transfers $d'$ to the child.

args.name: u, l
args.meaning: The upper and lower point of the thunk, arbitrary.

prim.force.title: $\mathsf{force}$
prim.force.why: A plain constant. It is the only use of a box, and a loop calls itself by $\mathsf{force}$ of its own box variable.
prim.force.example: $\mathsf{force}\,f\,\langle a, b\rangle$ runs the loop $f$ again.
prim.force.signature: \mathsf{force} : \Box(\forall\bar\iota\,\bar\alpha.\ C.\ \ast\multimap^{u} U) \multimap^{u[\bar x]} U[\bar s][\bar x]

args.name: \bar\iota, \bar\alpha
args.meaning: The point and session variables of the box.

args.name: u
args.meaning: The upper point of the body, instantiated as the upper point of the call.

args.name: U
args.meaning: The result type of the body.

syn.values.title: Values
syn.values.why: The results of evaluation. A thread that is a value has finished.
syn.values.example: $\langle \ast, c^{+}\rangle$ and $\lambda x.\,\mathsf{close}\,x$ are values, $\mathsf{close}\,c^{+}$ is not.

deviations.reason: The Rocq writes the injections as `Inj`, shown as $\mathsf{inj}_i$, and `is_val` decides which terms are values.

end.cend.title: End
end.cend.meaning: An end $o \in \{c^{+}, c^{-}\}$ of a channel $c$, with one entry per end in an environment.
end.cend.why: The two ends have independent names, and $\mathsf{select}$ and $\mathsf{branch}$ return the name they received. Hence an environment entry is determined by the end alone.

end.dual.title: Dual end $\overline{o}$
end.dual.why: A message on $o$ synchronizes with an action on $\overline{o}$. Each two-thread process step pairs an end with its dual end.
end.dual.example: A send on $c^{+}$ meets a receive on $c^{-}$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: An end, $\overline{o}$ is the other end of $\mathsf{ech}\,o$.

end.ech.title: Channel of an end
end.ech.why: Restricted sets $C$ and the subjects of an offer are sets of channels, so the rules map ends to channels by $\mathsf{ech}$.

syn.fends.title: $\mathsf{fends}$
syn.fends.meaning: $\mathsf{fends}(e)$ is the finite set of ends that occur in $e$.
syn.fends.why: The value relation asks $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(\lambda e)$ of a closure and $\mathsf{fends}(e) = \varnothing$ of a box. Hence for $v$ in $V$ at $\Theta$ the ends a send or spawn of $v$ moves are $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, and ownership follows the syntax of values.

args.name: e
args.meaning: A term, $\mathsf{fends}(e)$ is the set of ends occurring in $e$.

syn.fchans.title: $\mathsf{fchans}$
syn.fchans.why: A created channel $c$ must satisfy $c \notin \mathsf{fchans}(e)$ for each thread $e$, or two channels share a name.

proc.proc.title: Process $(C, E)$
proc.proc.meaning: A process is a pair of a finite set $C$ of restricted channels and a finite multiset $E$ of threads.
proc.proc.why: A channel $c \in C$ has both ends inside the process. An end $o$ with $\mathsf{ech}\,o \notin C$ belongs to the interface with the environment.

args.name: E
args.meaning: The threads, a finite multiset of terms.

proc.config.title: Configuration
proc.config.meaning: A configuration $q = (C, M)$ has a finite partial map $M : \mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup e$ from thread identifiers to terms.
proc.config.why: \inmode{lf}{Weak fairness and lock freedom speak about one thread $t$ across a run, so threads have identifiers.}

args.name: M
args.meaning: The thread map, $M(i)$ the term of thread $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

deviations.reason: The Rocq type `gmap nat expr` of the thread map is shown as $\mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathsf{Expr}$, with $\mathsf{Expr}$ for the type `expr` of terms.

proc.erase.title: $\mathsf{erase}$
proc.erase.meaning: $\mathsf{erase}(C, M) = (C, \{\!|\, M(i) \mid i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M \,|\!\})$ forgets the identifiers.
proc.erase.why: Steps are defined once, on configurations. A process $p$ steps to $p'$ when some $q$ with $\mathsf{erase}(q) = p$ steps to some $q'$ with $\mathsf{erase}(q') = p'$.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: A configuration, $\mathsf{erase}(C, M)$ keeps $C$ and the multiset of the terms $M(i)$.

pt.const.title: Constant $a$
pt.const.meaning: A constant base $a \in A$ of the world $W$, shared with the environment through an interface or added when $\mathsf{new}$ creates a fresh base.
pt.const.why: Each point of a held end has a base in $A$. The facts $\prec_A$ mention only such points.

args.name: a
args.meaning: A constant, $a \in A$ for the world $W$ in use.

pt.var.title: Point variable $\iota$
pt.var.meaning: A de Bruijn point variable, bound by $\Box\forall\bar\iota$, by a payload $!(\bar\iota.\,T)$ or by the existential of $\mathsf{new}$, and absent from terms.
pt.var.why: No term mentions a point. Types quantify over points instead.
pt.var.example: $\Box\forall \iota\,\kappa\,\zeta.\ C.\ \ast \multimap U$ binds three point variables.

args.name: \iota
args.meaning: A de Bruijn index over points, bound by $\Box\forall\bar\iota$, by a payload $!(\bar\iota.\,T)$ or by the existential of $\mathsf{new}$.

pt.shift.title: Shift $x^{+}$
pt.shift.meaning: $x^{+}$ raises the offset of $x$ by $1$, so an action on an end at $x$ moves it to $x^{+}$.
pt.shift.why: For each $W$ and $x$, $x \prec_W x^{+}$. Hence the actions of one end are ordered in program order.
pt.shift.example: After $\mathsf{send}$ at $x$ the end is at $x^{+}$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: A point, $x^{+}$ has the offset of $x$ plus $1$.

pt.field.title: Field $x\cdot\kappa$
pt.field.meaning: $x\cdot\kappa$ is a name below $x$ with offset $0$ and positive polarity, where payloads, branch continuations and channels created at a field are.
pt.field.why: The $j$-th payload end of a message at $x$ is at $x\cdot j$, and the continuation of choice $i$ at $x\cdot\kappa_i$. $\mathsf{new}$ may place a channel at the same fields, so a channel created to be sent is at the field where the message delivers its payload.
pt.field.breaks: With a separate sort of point for created channels, a reply channel created to be sent is away from the payload field, and request and reply programs do not type.
pt.field.example: $\mathsf{new}$ at the position $\rho\cdot 0$ places $d^{+}$ at $\rho\cdot 0$ and $d^{-}$ at $\overline{\rho\cdot 0}$.

pt.dual.title: Dual point $\overline{x}$
pt.dual.meaning: $\overline{x}$ flips the polarity of $x$, and the two ends of a channel are at $x$ and $\overline{x}$.
pt.dual.why: A thread blocked at $u$ that holds an end at $v$ must satisfy $u \prec \overline{v}$, the point of the dual end.

args.name: x
args.meaning: A point, $\overline{x}$ has the opposite polarity.

pt.laws.title: Point laws
pt.laws.meaning: For each $x$ and $\kappa$, $\overline{\overline{x}} = x$, $\overline{x}\cdot\kappa = x\cdot\kappa$ and $\overline{x^{+}} = \overline{x}^{+}$.
pt.laws.why: $\overline{x}\cdot\kappa = x\cdot\kappa$ makes the payload points $x\cdot j$ of sender and receiver equal, although the two ends are at $x$ and $\overline{x}$.
pt.laws.breaks: If $\overline{x}\cdot\kappa \neq x\cdot\kappa$, the ends of a message are at different points for sender and receiver, and the received value is not in the value relation at its type.

sx.kappai.title: Field of a choice $\kappa_i$
sx.kappai.why: The two continuations of a choice are at distinct fields $x\cdot 0 \neq x\cdot 1$, so facts order them independently.

deviations.reason: `bfield false` is $0$ and `bfield true` is $1$, shown as the fields $\kappa_{\mathsf{false}}$ and $\kappa_{\mathsf{true}}$.

pt.sel.title: Select continuation
pt.sel.meaning: $\mathsf{sel\_pt}\,x\,i = \overline{x\cdot\kappa_i}$, the point of the end after $\mathsf{select}_i$ at $x$.
pt.sel.why: Selecting end and branching end continue at the two sides $\overline{x\cdot\kappa_i}$ and $x\cdot\kappa_i$ of one field.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the selecting end before the step.

pt.bra.title: Branch continuation
pt.bra.meaning: $\mathsf{bra\_pt}\,x\,i = x\cdot\kappa_i$, the point of the end after $\mathsf{branch}$ at $\overline{x}$ receives $i$.
pt.bra.why: It is $\overline{\mathsf{sel\_pt}\,x\,i}$, the dual point of the selecting side.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the selecting end, the branching end is at $\overline{x}$.

pt.payload.title: Payload fields
pt.payload.meaning: The $j$-th end of a message sent at $x$ is at $x\cdot j$.
pt.payload.why: $\overline{x}\cdot j = x\cdot j$, so sender at $x$ and receiver at $\overline{x}$ compute the same points for the delivered ends.
pt.payload.example: A message on $y$ at $Y$ delivers its end at $Y\cdot 0$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the carrier end at the send.

args.name: m
args.meaning: The number of point variables the payload binds.

lbl.field.title: Field label $\kappa$
lbl.field.meaning: $\kappa \in \mathbb{N}$ selects the field $x\cdot\kappa$ of a point $x$.
lbl.field.why: Payloads, choices and the position of a new channel use fields. $x\cdot\kappa = x\cdot\kappa'$ iff $\kappa = \kappa'$.
lbl.field.breaks: Two channels created at one field $x\cdot\kappa$ are at the same points $x\cdot\kappa$ and $\overline{x\cdot\kappa}$, so no fact orders one before the other.

link.csub.title: $\mathsf{csub}$
link.csub.meaning: $\mathsf{csub}\,o_1\,o_2 = \{\overline{o_1} \mapsto o_2,\ o_1 \mapsto \overline{o_2}\}$, the identity elsewhere, applied to each thread after a link.
link.csub.why: After the link, the thread holding $\overline{o_1}$ communicates with the thread holding $\overline{o_2}$, so it holds $o_2$. The map identifies $\overline{o_1}$ with $o_2$, so it is no bijection.
link.csub.example: After $\mathsf{link}\,\langle c^{+}, d^{-}\rangle$ the thread holding $c^{-}$ holds $d^{-}$.

args.name: o_1, o_2
args.meaning: The linked ends, the channel of $o_1$ disappears.

se.slabel.title: Session label $\sigma$
se.slabel.meaning: A label $\sigma$ of a step that acts on an end and synchronizes with another thread or with the environment.
se.slabel.why: Session labels are exactly the steps a thread can wait on. Readiness and the obligations of the relation are stated over session labels.
se.slabel.example: $o?v$ and $o\,\mathsf{end}$ are session labels, $\beta$ is none.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

args.name: v
args.meaning: The value sent or received, where present.

se.subst.title: Substitution $e[v]$
se.subst.meaning: $e[v]$ is $e$ with the value $v$ for the variable of index $0$, and the other indices lowered by one.
se.subst.why: A plain definition. Application, the two lets, case and force step by substitution.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The body, with a free index $0$.

se.frame.title: Frame filling $f[e]$
se.frame.meaning: An evaluation frame $f$ is a term with one hole in evaluation position, and $f[e]$ fills the hole with $e$.
se.frame.why: A plain definition. The frames fix where the next step of a term happens.

args.name: f
args.meaning: An evaluation frame, a term with one hole $\square$ in evaluation position.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The term placed in the hole.

se.upd.title: Map update $M[i \mapsto e]$
se.upd.meaning: $M[i \mapsto e]$ maps $i$ to $e$ and each $j \neq i$ to $M(j)$.

se.echans.title: $\mathsf{echans}(M)$
se.echans.why: A created channel $c$ satisfies $c \notin \mathsf{echans}(M)$, so it differs from each channel a thread mentions.

se.subj.title: Subjects $\mathsf{subj}\,\sigma$
se.subj.meaning: $\mathsf{subj}\,\sigma$ is the set of channels $\sigma$ acts on, $\{\mathsf{ech}\,o\}$ for an action on $o$ and $\{\mathsf{ech}\,o_1, \mathsf{ech}\,o_2\}$ for a link.
se.subj.why: An offer to the environment requires $\mathsf{subj}\,\sigma \cap C = \varnothing$, so it uses only interface channels.

se.parts.title: Participants $\mathsf{parts}(ev)$
se.parts.meaning: $\mathsf{parts}(\mathsf{sync}_{i,j}\,\sigma) = \{i, j\}$, $\mathsf{parts}(\mathsf{solo}_i\,\alpha\,k) = \mathsf{parts}(\mathsf{offer}_i\,\sigma) = \{i\}$, and $\mathsf{parts}(\bot) = \varnothing$ for a stutter. A spawn names only the parent $i$.
se.parts.why: A thread takes part in a step iff it is in $\mathsf{parts}$ of its event. \inmode{lf}{Weak fairness and lock freedom ask whether $t \in \mathsf{parts}(l_j)$ for some position $j$.}

args.name: ev
args.meaning: An event. $\mathsf{parts}(ev)$ is the set of identifiers of the threads that take part in the step of $ev$.

se.reach.title: Reachability $\to^{*}$
se.reach.meaning: $p \to^{*} p'$ when finitely many $\tau$ steps lead from $p$ to $p'$.
se.reach.why: A plain definition. Deadlock freedom and absence of internal divergence quantify over the $p'$ with $p \to^{*} p'$.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: Processes, $p \to^{*} p'$ iff a finite sequence of $\tau$ steps leads from $p$ to $p'$.

se.acc.title: Accessibility $\mathsf{Acc}$
se.acc.meaning: $\mathsf{Acc}\,R\,q$ holds when each $R$-chain $q = q_0\,R\,q_1\,R \cdots$ is finite, inductively, when $\mathsf{Acc}\,R\,q'$ for each $q'$ with $q\,R\,q'$.
se.acc.why: It states the absence of infinite $R$-chains from $q$ by induction, so proofs consume it by well-founded induction.
se.acc.example: If each administrative chain from $q$ has length at most $2$, then $\mathsf{Acc}\ {\to_{\mathsf{admin}}}\ q$.

args.name: R
args.meaning: A relation on $X$, instantiated with $\to_{\mathsf{admin}}$ on processes.

args.name: q
args.meaning: The start element, instantiated with a process reachable from $p$.

se.r0.title: The run starts at $p$
se.r0.meaning: $r_0$ is the configuration at position $0$ of the run, and $\mathsf{erase}(r_0) = p$ states that forgetting its thread names gives the process $p$.
se.r0.why: Lock freedom is a property of a process, and runs are sequences of configurations, so the run must start at a configuration of $p$. Each naming of the threads of $p$ is allowed.

args.name: r_0
args.meaning: The first configuration of the run, $r$ applied to $0$.

args.name: p
args.meaning: The process whose lock freedom is stated.

se.run.title: Runs $r$ and $l$
se.run.meaning: A run is a pair of sequences, $r_i$ the configuration at position $i$ and $l_i$ the event of the step from $r_i$ to $r_{i+1}$, or none when $r_{i+1} = r_i$ stutters.
se.run.why: Lock freedom quantifies over infinite runs and speaks of positions $i \leq j$ in a run.

args.name: l_i
args.meaning: The event of the step $r_i \to r_{i+1}$, or $\bot$ when $r_{i+1} = r_i$.

lbl.beta.title: $\beta$ label
lbl.beta.meaning: The label of application, unit and pair elimination, case and force.
lbl.beta.why: These steps have the same cost in each cost table, so one label covers the five.

lbl.new.title: Label $\mathsf{new}\,c$
lbl.new.meaning: It contains the name $c$ of the new channel.
lbl.new.why: The process rule reads $c$ to keep names fresh. Position and facts of $c$ are no part of the label, and the relation chooses position and facts.

args.name: c
args.meaning: The name of the new channel.

lbl.spawn.title: Label $\mathsf{spawn}\,v$
lbl.spawn.meaning: It contains the thunk $v$ that starts the child thread $v\,\ast$.
lbl.spawn.why: The relation splits the environment of the parent as $\Theta = \Theta_c \uplus \Theta_r$ with $v$ in the thunk relation at $\Theta_c$. Exactness of $V$ gives $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_c = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, so the split is determined by $v$.

args.name: v
args.meaning: The thunk, the child thread is $v\,\ast$.

lbl.send.title: Send label $o!v$
lbl.send.meaning: An offer to send the value $v$ on the end $o$.
lbl.send.why: \inmode{lf}{The relation, the fuel layer and scope extrusion read the ends that leave as $\mathsf{fends}(v)$.} For $v$ in $V$ at $\Theta_v$ this set is $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_v$.
lbl.send.example: Sending the end $a$ on $o$ has the label $o!a$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

lbl.recv.title: Receive label $o?v$
lbl.recv.meaning: An offer to receive $v$ on $o$, for each value $v$.
lbl.recv.why: A receive must meet each send on the dual end, so its labels range over the values.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

args.name: v
args.meaning: The received value, one label per value.

lbl.close.title: Close label $o\,\mathsf{end}$
lbl.close.why: A plain label. Its obligation removes $o$ from the environment $\Theta$, so after a close $o \notin \mathrm{dom}\,\Theta$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

lbl.sel.title: Select label $o \lhd i$
lbl.sel.meaning: An offer to select branch $i$ on $o$.
lbl.sel.why: A plain label. Its obligation moves $o$ from $x$ to $\overline{x\cdot\kappa_i}$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

lbl.bra.title: Branch label $o \rhd i$
lbl.bra.meaning: An offer to receive the choice $i$ on $o$, for both $i$.
lbl.bra.why: A plain label. $\mathsf{branch}$ must meet either choice on the dual end, so it has a step for each $i$, and the obligation moves $o$ to $x\cdot\kappa_i$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

lbl.link.title: Link label $\leftrightarrow\{o_1, o_2\}$
lbl.link.meaning: An unordered pair $\{o_1, o_2\}$ of ends, where $o_1 = o_2$ is allowed.
lbl.link.why: The label is a set, so one process rule removes the channel of either end.

args.name: o_1, o_2
args.meaning: The linked ends, an unordered pair.

T-Act-App.title: T-Act-App
T-Act-App.why: Call by value. The argument is a value before the body runs.

T-Act-Let.title: T-Act-Let-Unit, T-Act-Let-Pair
T-Act-Let.meaning: A unit elimination of $\ast$ continues with its body, and a pair elimination of a pair of values substitutes both components.
T-Act-Let.why: The two lets sequence code. The derived one-variable $\mathsf{let}$ takes one step of each.

args.name: v_1, v_2
args.meaning: The components of the pair, values.

T-Act-Case.title: T-Act-Case-Inl, T-Act-Case-Inr
T-Act-Case.meaning: A case of an injected value continues with the branch of its side, the value substituted for the bound variable.
T-Act-Case.why: The only eliminator of sums. It consumes the result of $\mathsf{branch}$.

T-Act-Force.title: T-Act-Force
T-Act-Force.meaning: $\mathsf{force}\,(!e) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{force}} e[!e]$, so the body runs with the box for its own variable.
T-Act-Force.why: It is the only rule that unrolls a definition, so recursion and replication go through force steps.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The body of the box, substituted with the box itself.

T-Act-New.title: T-Act-New
T-Act-New.meaning: $\mathsf{new} \xrightarrow{\mathsf{new}\,c} \langle c^{+}, c^{-}\rangle$ for each $c$, and the process rule picks $c$.
T-Act-New.why: The step of a single thread cannot determine which channel names are in use. The process rule asks $c \notin C \cup \mathsf{echans}(M)$.

args.name: c
args.meaning: A channel name, restricted by the process rule.

T-Act-Spawn.title: T-Act-Spawn
T-Act-Spawn.why: The label contains $v$, so the process rule can start the thread $v\,\ast$.

T-Act-Send.title: T-Act-Send
T-Act-Send.why: The label contains the payload $v$, which the receiving thread obtains by the process rule.

T-Act-Recv.title: T-Act-Recv
T-Act-Recv.why: The step of a single thread does not depend on what the other thread sends, so it has a step for each $v$. The receive obligation quantifies only over $v$ in the value relation at the payload type.

T-Act-Close.title: T-Act-Close
T-Act-Close.why: A plain rule. The process rule pairs it with $\overline{o}\,\mathsf{end}$ in another thread.

T-Act-Select.title: T-Act-Select
T-Act-Select.meaning: $\mathsf{select}_i\,o \xrightarrow{o \lhd i} o$, returning the same end name.
T-Act-Select.why: The end keeps its name $o$, so no step reads a point.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end, returned under the same name.

T-Act-Branch.title: T-Act-Branch
T-Act-Branch.why: Either choice may arrive, so the thread has one step for each $i$.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The received choice, one step for each $i$.

T-Act-Link.title: T-Act-Link
T-Act-Link.meaning: $\mathsf{link}\,\langle o_1, o_2\rangle \xrightarrow{\leftrightarrow\{o_1, o_2\}} \ast$. The label is a set, so $\langle o_1, o_2\rangle$ and $\langle o_2, o_1\rangle$ give one label.
T-Act-Link.why: The renaming $\mathsf{csub}\,o_1\,o_2$ concerns other threads, so the process rule performs the renaming.

T-Act-Ctx.title: T-Act-Ctx
T-Act-Ctx.why: No frame has its hole under $\lambda$ or $!$, so the bodies of closures and boxes take no step before they are called.

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: The term in the hole before and after the step.

args.name: f
args.meaning: An evaluation frame whose subterms left of the hole are values.

sem.frameval.title: $\mathsf{frame\_val}$
sem.frameval.meaning: $\mathsf{frame\_val}\,f$ holds when each subterm of $f$ left of the hole is a value.
sem.frameval.why: It fixes left-to-right evaluation, so each term has at most one redex position.

args.name: f
args.meaning: A frame, $\mathsf{frame\_val}\,f$ iff each subterm of $f$ left of the hole is a value.

P-Act-Beta.title: P-Act-Beta
P-Act-Beta.meaning: If $M(i) \xrightarrow{\beta} e'$, then $(C, M) \to (C, M[i \mapsto e'])$ with event $\mathsf{solo}_i\,\beta\,\cdot$.
P-Act-Beta.why: A plain rule. A $\beta$ step changes only thread $i$.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: The configuration before the step, $C$ its restricted channels and $M$ its thread map.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The identifier of the acting thread, $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

args.name: e'
args.meaning: The term of thread $i$ after its step.

P-Act-New.title: P-Act-New
P-Act-New.meaning: If $M(i) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{new}\,c} e'$ and $c \notin C \cup \mathsf{echans}(M)$, then $(C, M) \to (C \cup \{c\}, M[i \mapsto e'])$.
P-Act-New.why: Both ends of $c$ start in thread $i$, so $c$ is internal to the process and joins $C$.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: The configuration before the step, $C$ its restricted channels and $M$ its thread map.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The identifier of the acting thread, $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

args.name: e'
args.meaning: The term of thread $i$ after its step.

sem.fresh-global.title: Global freshness
sem.fresh-global.meaning: $c \notin C \cup \mathsf{echans}(M)$, so $c$ is neither restricted nor mentioned by a thread.
sem.fresh-global.why: Channel names are global. If $c \in \mathsf{fchans}(M(j))$ for some $j$, the new channel would share its name with a channel thread $j$ uses.
sem.fresh-global.breaks: Reusing a name some thread still mentions merges two channels into one, and an action on one channel synchronizes with an action on the other.

args.name: c
args.meaning: The name of the channel being created.

args.name: C
args.meaning: The restricted channels of the configuration.

args.name: M
args.meaning: The thread map of the configuration.

P-Act-Spawn.title: P-Act-Spawn
P-Act-Spawn.meaning: If $M(i) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{spawn}\,v} e'$ and $j \notin \mathrm{dom}\,M$, then $M$ becomes $M[i \mapsto e'][j \mapsto v\,\ast]$.
P-Act-Spawn.why: The event is $\mathsf{solo}_i\,(\mathsf{spawn}\,v)\,j$, so only thread $i$ takes part.
P-Act-Spawn.example: $\mathsf{spawn}\,(\lambda u.\,e)$ adds a thread $j$ running $(\lambda u.\,e)\,\ast$.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: The configuration before the step, $C$ its restricted channels and $M$ its thread map.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The identifier of the acting thread, $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

args.name: e'
args.meaning: The term of thread $i$ after its step.

args.name: j
args.meaning: The identifier of the new thread, $j \notin \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

P-Act-Msg.title: P-Act-Msg
P-Act-Msg.meaning: $M(i) \xrightarrow{o!v} e'$, $M(j) \xrightarrow{\overline{o}?v} f'$, $i \neq j$ give $M[i \mapsto e'][j \mapsto f']$, with no condition on $C$.
P-Act-Msg.why: In a typed process both ends of a channel are held inside only when the channel is restricted, so a condition $\mathsf{ech}\,o \in C$ would add nothing for typed processes.
P-Act-Msg.example: The client sends on $a$ and the server receives on $a'$.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: The configuration before the step, $C$ its restricted channels and $M$ its thread map.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The identifier of the acting thread, $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

args.name: j
args.meaning: The identifier of the other thread, $j \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$ with $j \neq i$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end of the sender, the receiver acts on $\overline{o}$.

args.name: v
args.meaning: The payload, the same value in both labels.

args.name: e'
args.meaning: The term of thread $i$ after its step.

args.name: f'
args.meaning: The term of thread $j$ after its step.

P-Act-Close.title: P-Act-Close
P-Act-Close.meaning: If $M(i) \xrightarrow{o\,\mathsf{end}} e'$, $M(j) \xrightarrow{\overline{o}\,\mathsf{end}} f'$ and $\mathsf{ech}\,o \in C$, then $C$ becomes $C \setminus \{\mathsf{ech}\,o\}$.
P-Act-Close.why: After both closes no thread holds an end of $\mathsf{ech}\,o$, so the channel leaves $C$.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: The configuration before the step, $C$ its restricted channels and $M$ its thread map.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The identifier of the acting thread, $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

args.name: j
args.meaning: The identifier of the other thread, $j \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$ with $j \neq i$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end closed by $i$, with $\mathsf{ech}\,o \in C$.

args.name: e'
args.meaning: The term of thread $i$ after its step.

args.name: f'
args.meaning: The term of thread $j$ after its step.

P-Act-Choice.title: P-Act-Choice
P-Act-Choice.meaning: If $M(i) \xrightarrow{o \lhd b} e'$ and $M(j) \xrightarrow{\overline{o} \rhd b} f'$ with the same $b$, then $M$ becomes $M[i \mapsto e'][j \mapsto f']$.
P-Act-Choice.why: Requiring the same $b$ passes the choice of thread $i$ to thread $j$.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: The configuration before the step, $C$ its restricted channels and $M$ its thread map.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The identifier of the acting thread, $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

args.name: j
args.meaning: The identifier of the other thread, $j \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$ with $j \neq i$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The selecting end, the other thread branches on $\overline{o}$.

args.name: b
args.meaning: The choice, the same in both labels.

args.name: e'
args.meaning: The term of thread $i$ after its step.

args.name: f'
args.meaning: The term of thread $j$ after its step.

P-Act-Link.title: P-Act-Link
P-Act-Link.meaning: If $M(i) \xrightarrow{\leftrightarrow\{o_1, o_2\}} e'$ and $\mathsf{ech}\,o_1 \in C$, then $C$ loses $\mathsf{ech}\,o_1$ and each thread of $M[i \mapsto e']$ is renamed by $\mathsf{csub}\,o_1\,o_2$.
P-Act-Link.why: The label is unordered, so the rule applies with either end as $o_1$ and removes the channel of either end.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: The configuration before the step, $C$ its restricted channels and $M$ its thread map.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The identifier of the acting thread, $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

args.name: e'
args.meaning: The term of thread $i$ after its step.

P-Act-Session.title: P-Act-Session
P-Act-Session.meaning: If $M(i) \xrightarrow{\sigma} e'$ and $\mathsf{subj}\,\sigma \cap C = \varnothing$, then $(C, M) \to (C \setminus \mathsf{sentc}\,\sigma, M[i \mapsto e'])$, an offer to the environment.
P-Act-Session.why: A send of $v$ to the environment moves the ends $\mathsf{fends}(v)$, so their channels leave $C$. The process and the relation compute the extruded channels from the same $v$.
P-Act-Session.example: An external send of a restricted $d^{+}$ removes $d$ from $C$.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: The configuration before the step, $C$ its restricted channels and $M$ its thread map.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The identifier of the acting thread, $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

args.name: \sigma
args.meaning: A session label with $\mathsf{subj}\,\sigma \cap C = \varnothing$, an offer to the environment.

args.name: e'
args.meaning: The term of thread $i$ after its step.

sem.sentc.title: $\mathsf{sentc}$
sem.sentc.why: These are the channels a message to the environment moves out of the process.

ev.event.title: Event
ev.event.meaning: $\mathsf{solo}_i\,\alpha\,k$ is a step of thread $i$ alone with thread label $\alpha$. $\mathsf{sync}_{i,j}\,\sigma$ is a step in which thread $i$ takes the send, close or select $\sigma$ on an end $o$ and thread $j$ the matching receive, close or branch on $\overline{o}$. $\mathsf{offer}_i\,\sigma$ is an offer of thread $i$ to the environment.
ev.event.why: \inmode{lf}{Weak fairness asks of each thread $t$ that $t \in \mathsf{parts}(l_j)$ for some $j$, so each step names its threads.}

args.name: \alpha
args.meaning: The thread label of a solo step.

args.name: k
args.meaning: The pick of a solo step.

args.name: \sigma
args.meaning: The session label of thread $i$, in a synchronization or an offer to the environment.

deviations.reason: The constructors `EvSolo`, `EvSync` and `EvOffer` of `event` are shown as $\mathsf{solo}$, $\mathsf{sync}$ and $\mathsf{offer}$.

ev.pick.title: Pick $k$
ev.pick.meaning: What a process rule chooses beyond the thread label. $k = j$ names the new thread of a spawn. $k = (o_1, o_2)$ orders the ends of a link, so the channel of $o_1$ goes and the thread with $\overline{o_1}$ then holds $o_2$. Each other solo step has $k = \cdot$.
ev.pick.why: The thread label of a link is the unordered set $\{o_1, o_2\}$, and the thread label of a spawn names no thread, so the event records the choice the rule makes.

args.name: j
args.meaning: The identifier of a spawned thread.

args.name: o_1, o_2
args.meaning: The ends of a link, the channel of $o_1$ goes.

ev.admin.title: Administrative events
ev.admin.meaning: $\mathsf{admin}$ is the set of solo events $\mathsf{solo}_i\,\alpha\,k$, the steps by $\beta$, $\mathsf{force}$, $\mathsf{new}$, $\mathsf{spawn}$ and $\mathsf{link}$.\inmode{lf}{ Each of them but a force costs $0$ in $\kappa_L$.}
ev.admin.why: They act on no protocol. \inmode{lf}{Absence of internal divergence states that each chain of them is finite.}
ev.admin.example: An unbounded chain of spawns takes only administrative steps.

ev.tau.title: $\tau$ events
ev.tau.meaning: Each event except $\mathsf{offer}_i\,\sigma$, an offer to the environment.
ev.tau.why: A closed configuration has no environment, so each of its steps is a $\tau$ step.

deviations.reason: `ev_tau` holds of the events whose process label is `PTau`, shown as a set of events. $\mathsf{Event}$ is the type `event`.

prop.terminated.title: $\mathsf{terminated}$
prop.terminated.meaning: $\mathsf{terminated}\,p$ iff $p = (\varnothing, \{\!|v|\!\} \uplus E)$ with $v$ a value and $e = \ast$ for each $e \in E$.
prop.terminated.why: At the end $C = \varnothing$, so each channel is used up, and only the main thread returns a value.

args.name: v
args.meaning: The result of the main thread, a value.

args.name: E
args.meaning: The multiset of the other threads, each equal to $\ast$.

prop.df.title: $\mathsf{deadlock\_free}$
prop.df.meaning: $\mathsf{deadlock\_free}\,p$ iff for each $p'$ with $p \to^{*} p'$, $\mathsf{terminated}\,p'$ or $p' \to p''$ for some $p''$.
prop.df.why: It is the safety property the deadlock-free results prove of closed typed processes. A stuck configuration is one that has not terminated and cannot step.

args.name: p'
args.meaning: Ranges over the processes with $p \to^{*} p'$.

prop.notau.title: $\mathsf{no\_tau\_divergence}$
prop.notau.meaning: For each $q$ with $p \to^{*} q$, $\mathsf{Acc}\ {\to_{\mathsf{admin}}}\ q$, so no infinite chain of administrative steps starts at $q$.
prop.notau.why: A thread that loops on internal steps never takes part in a session step. Typing no longer gives this property, because a loop of forces that holds no end types, and [[th-adeq|thread progress]] takes it as a hypothesis.

args.name: q
args.meaning: Ranges over the processes with $p \to^{*} q$.

prop.padmin.title: Administrative step
prop.padmin.meaning: $q \to_{\mathsf{admin}} q'$ when $q \to q'$ with an administrative event.
prop.padmin.why: It is the relation that absence of internal divergence asks to be well-founded.

args.name: q, q'
args.meaning: Processes with $q \to q'$ by an event in $\mathsf{admin}$.

prop.lf.title: $\mathsf{lock\_free}$
prop.lf.meaning: For each run $(r, l)$ with $\mathsf{erase}(r_0) = p$ that is maximal and weakly fair, each thread $t$ pending at a position $i$ has $t \in \mathsf{parts}(l_j)$ for some $j \geq i$.
prop.lf.why: Deadlock freedom allows a thread to wait forever while other threads step. Lock freedom excludes it, and its definition mentions no type.
prop.lf.breaks: A server that serves one client forever while a second client waits is deadlock free and not lock free.

args.name: (r, l)
args.meaning: A run, $r_i \in \mathsf{Config}$ the configuration and $l_i$ the event or stutter at position $i \in \mathbb{N}$.

args.name: j
args.meaning: A position with $j \ge i$, existentially quantified.

prop.maximal.title: Maximal run
prop.maximal.meaning: For each $i$, either $r_i \to r_{i+1}$ by a $\tau$ event $l_i$, or $r_i$ has no $\tau$ step and $r_{i+1} = r_i$.
prop.maximal.why: A run that stutters while a step is possible would satisfy lock freedom vacuously, so the definition quantifies over maximal runs only.
prop.maximal.example: A run that stutters at $r_i$ while $r_i$ has a $\tau$ step is not maximal.

args.name: (r, l)
args.meaning: A run, $r_i \in \mathsf{Config}$ the configuration and $l_i$ the event or stutter at position $i \in \mathbb{N}$.

args.name: i
args.meaning: Ranges over the positions of the run.

prop.wfair.title: Weak fairness
prop.wfair.meaning: For each position $i$ and thread $t$, there is $j \geq i$ with $t \in \mathsf{parts}(l_j)$ or $t$ disabled at $r_j$.
prop.wfair.why: Without fairness a scheduler may never run an enabled thread $t$, and no program with two threads is lock free.
prop.wfair.example: A run that never schedules an enabled thread is not weakly fair.

args.name: (r, l)
args.meaning: A run, $r_i \in \mathsf{Config}$ the configuration and $l_i$ the event or stutter at position $i \in \mathbb{N}$.

args.name: i
args.meaning: Ranges over the positions of the run.

args.name: j
args.meaning: A position with $j \ge i$, existentially quantified.

prop.pend.title: Pending thread
prop.pend.meaning: $\mathsf{pend}(q, t)$ holds when thread $t$ of $q$ has a session label as its next step, so it waits for another thread or for the environment.
prop.pend.why: Lock freedom guarantees progress exactly to the pending threads.

prop.lfrun.title: $\mathsf{lf\_run}$
prop.lfrun.meaning: For each $i$ and $t$, $\mathsf{pend}(r_i, t)$ implies $t \in \mathsf{parts}(l_j)$ for some $j \geq i$.
prop.lfrun.why: It is the condition on one run, and $\mathsf{lock\_free}\,p$ asks it of each maximal weakly fair run from $p$.
prop.lfrun.example: Each message the client sends is received by the server at a later position.

args.name: (r, l)
args.meaning: A run, $r_i \in \mathsf{Config}$ the configuration and $l_i$ the event or stutter at position $i \in \mathbb{N}$.

args.name: i, t
args.meaning: Range over the positions of the run and the thread identifiers.

args.name: j
args.meaning: A position with $j \ge i$, existentially quantified.

ty.unit.title: Unit type $\ast$
ty.unit.meaning: The type of $\ast$, with $V\llbracket\Theta \vdash \ast\rrbracket = \{\ast\}$ at $\Theta = \varnothing$ and empty otherwise.
ty.unit.why: A plain type. $\mathsf{close}$, $\mathsf{link}$ and $\mathsf{spawn}$ return $\ast$, and a spawned thread returns $\ast$.

ty.arrow.title: Arrow
ty.arrow.meaning: $T \multimap^{u}_{l} U$ is a closure type with upper point $u$ and lower point $l$. \inmode{lf}{In the lock-free view it is $(T \multimap^{u}_{l}[c]\,U)\inmode{lf}{^{a}}$ with a cost $c$\inmode{lf}{ and a credit} $a$.} \inmode{lf}{The body is typed with each captured end at its own credit minus $a$.}
ty.arrow.why: A call runs code that may block and holds the ends of the closure. The type bounds where the call blocks by $u$ and where the held ends are by $l$.
ty.arrow.example: $\ast \multimap \ast$ is the type of a spawned thunk.

args.name: a
args.meaning: The credit of the closure, a lower bound on its captured counters and what they lose before a call.

args.name: u
args.meaning: The upper point, a point, $\bot$ or $\top$.

args.name: l
args.meaning: The lower point, $\top$ iff the closure holds no end and $\bot$ when it gives no bound for its ends.

ty.ubound.title: Upper point $u$
ty.ubound.meaning: $u = x$ bounds the points where a call may wait, $u = \bot$ asks nothing of the caller, because $\bot$ lies below each point, and $u = \top$ admits only the empty future.
ty.ubound.why: With $u = \top$ the body runs as the last code of its thread. A spawned abstraction is such a closure, so E-Abs at $u = \top$ and $l = \bot$ followed by E-Spawn types it, and V-Arrow at $(\top, \bot)$ is the predicate of a spawned thunk.

deviations.reason: `UNone` is $\bot$, `UPt x` is $x$ and `UTop` is $\top$.

ty.arrow.ub.title: Upper point $u$
ty.arrow.ub.meaning: The body is in $E$ under each future $F$ with $u \prec F$, which the caller must establish.
ty.arrow.ub.why: The type of a closure does not show its body. The condition $u \prec F$ places the later actions of the caller above the points where the body may block.
ty.arrow.ub.breaks: Without $u$, a closure that blocks at $x$ with $y \prec x$ for some later action $y$ of the caller could be called first, and the thread waits on its own later action.
ty.arrow.ub.example: A function that blocks on an end at $\kappa$ has $u = \kappa$.

args.name: u
args.meaning: A point, $\bot$ or $\top$. The body is in $E$ under each future $F$ that $u$ lies below.

ty.arrow.lb.title: Lower point $l$
ty.arrow.lb.meaning: $l \preccurlyeq \mathsf{ap}(\Theta)$ for the captured ends $\Theta$. A point $l$ lies at or below each of their dual points, $l = \top$ asks that the closure captures no end, and $l = \bot$ asks nothing.
ty.arrow.lb.why: A closure is a held value. A thread blocked at $x$ while holding it needs $x \prec y$ for each dual point $y$ of the captured ends, and $x \prec l$ implies these facts.
ty.arrow.lb.breaks: Without $l$, a thread blocks at $x$ while it holds a closure with a captured end at $v$ and $x \not\prec \overline{v}$, so the thread holding the dual end may wait on the first thread.

args.name: l
args.meaning: A point with $l \preccurlyeq y$ for each dual point $y$ of the captured ends, $\top$ iff the closure captures no end, or $\bot$ for no bound.

ty.arrow.cost.title: Arrow cost $c$
ty.arrow.cost.meaning: A call performs at most $c \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ channel actions before it returns.
ty.arrow.cost.why: A thread that holds an end $o$ while a call runs delays $o$ by at most $c$ actions. Aging subtracts $c$ from the credit of $o$.
ty.arrow.cost.breaks: A thread that holds an end across a call that never returns keeps the thread holding the dual end waiting forever. With $c = \infty$ the held end has credit $a - \infty$, which fails $c \leq a$ at finite counter bound.
ty.arrow.cost.example: A loop body that never returns has $c = \infty$.

args.name: c
args.meaning: An upper bound on the channel actions of one call before it returns.

ty.credit.title: Credit $a$
ty.credit.meaning: $a \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ on an end type $S_x^{a,m}$ is a lower bound on the counter of that end. On a closure type $(T \multimap [c]\, U)^{a}$ each captured end that is not idle has counter at least $a$.
ty.credit.why: A counter bounds how many actions of other ends an end may still wait through. Only ends and closures hold ends of their own. A pair, a sum or an existential holds the ends of its parts, and their types have the credits.
ty.credit.breaks: A send of an end whose counter may be $0$ lets the end be sent on forever while the thread holding its dual end waits.
ty.credit.example: A fresh end with $m$ tickets has type $S_{\rho}\inmode{lf}{^{m,m}}$, credit $m$ and tickets $m$. A closure keeps its credit in the superscript, $(T \multimap [c]\, U)\inmode{lf}{^{a}}$.

args.name: a
args.meaning: A lower bound on the counter of an end, or of the ends a closure captured.

ty.prod.title: Product
ty.prod.meaning: $T \otimes U$. Its value relation splits $\Theta = \Theta_1 \uplus \Theta_2$ between the components.
ty.prod.why: A plain type. $\mathsf{send}$ takes a pair and $\mathsf{recv}$ returns one.
ty.prod.example: $S_{\iota} \otimes {S'}_{\kappa}$ for two ends of a client.

ty.sum.title: Sum
ty.sum.meaning: $T \oplus U$, the type of $\mathsf{inj}_1\,v$ with $v : T$ and of $\mathsf{inj}_2\,v$ with $v : U$.
ty.sum.why: A plain type. $\mathsf{branch}$ returns a sum whose injection records the choice.

args.name: T, U
args.meaning: The types of the two injections.

ty.sess.title: End type $S_x\inmode{lf}{^{a,m}}$
ty.sess.meaning: An end that runs the protocol $S$ and acts next at the point $x$. The point is the subscript, and a decorated point reads $S_{x^{+}}$ or $S_{\overline{x}}$. \inmode{lf}{In the lock-free view the superscript holds the credit $a$ and then the tickets $m$, and the deadlock-free view writes $S_x$.} A protocol that is not a single letter is parenthesized, as in $(!\ast.\mathsf{Close})_{\rho}$.
ty.sess.why: The points order the next actions of the ends, and readiness compares them to exclude circular waiting.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of its next action.

args.name: a
args.meaning: Its credit, a lower bound on its counter.

args.name: m
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{Its tickets, an upper bound on its counter, with $a \leq m$.}

ty.box.title: Box type
ty.box.meaning: $\Box(\forall\bar\iota\,\bar\alpha.\ C.\ \ast \multimap^{u} U)$ is a replicable thunk, usable at each point instance $\bar x$ with $C[\bar x]$ and each session instance $\bar s$.
ty.box.why: A loop needs fresh points in each round. Quantifying over $\bar\iota$ under $\Box$ gives each call its own instance.
ty.box.example: A client loop has type $\Box\forall\iota\,\kappa\,\zeta.\ C.\ \ast \multimap (S_{\iota} \otimes {S'}_{\kappa} \multimap^{\zeta} \ast)$.

args.name: \bar\iota
args.meaning: $m$ point variables, instantiated at each $\mathsf{force}$ by points $\bar x$ with $C[\bar x]$.

args.name: C
args.meaning: The constraint over $\bar\iota$ and outer points.

args.name: u
args.meaning: The upper point of the thunk.

ty.box.svars.title: Session variables $\bar\alpha$
