E-Send.heads.why: A thread waiting at $x$ while it holds a value of $T$ does not offer the ends in $T$, so readiness asks $x$ below the dual point of each. Ends behind the lower point $\bot$ have no known dual point, so a thread holding them may not wait.
E-Send.heads.breaks: Without $\bot$ in the active points, $\mathsf{send}\,\langle p, o\rangle$ with the unopened pair $p$ of a $\mathsf{new}$ types, and the sender waits while holding ends at points nothing orders.
E-Send.heads.example: The growing ring needs $Y \prec \overline{Y\cdot 0}$ for the payload $a$ of the send on $y$ at $Y$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: the point of the end the action is on

args.name: T
args.meaning: a held value, in E-Send the payload $T[x\cdot i]$

deviations.reason: `below_ty` asks `hbot T = false` and $x$ below each point of `heads T`, which is $x \prec \mathsf{ap}(T)$ with $\bot \in \mathsf{ap}(T)$ for `hbot`.

E-Send.floor.title: The sent value fits the payload type
E-Send.floor.meaning: $T'\inmode{lf}{ - 1} \leq T[x\cdot i]$. The type $T'$ of the sent value\inmode{lf}{, aged by one transfer,} is a subtype of the payload type at the fields of $x$. \inmode{lf}{The payload value aged by one transfer still has the credits the protocol guarantees.}
E-Send.floor.why: The receiver reads the payload at the type the protocol states, so the sent value must fit that type. \inmode{lf}{A transferred end loses $1$ of its counter at the send. Asking the promised credits after the loss bounds how often one end may be transferred.}
E-Send.floor.breaks: \inmode{lf}{Without the loss of $1$, an end is transferred forever, and the thread holding its dual end waits forever.}
E-Send.floor.example: A value of type $\exists^{\bot}\iota.\,C.\,S_\iota$ fits a payload $!(\iota.\,S_\iota)$ at $x$ only through the field $x\cdot 0$, so a created channel to be sent is placed at that field. \inmode{lf}{An end at credit $3$ fits a payload that asks credit $2$.}

args.name: T'
args.meaning: the type of the payload value

args.name: T[x\cdot i]
args.meaning: the payload type of the protocol at the fields of $x$

E-Recv.unfold.title: Receive head
E-Recv.unfold.why: Rules read the first action of $S$ after unfolding, so recursive protocols need no rule of their own.

args.name: S
args.meaning: the session type of the end before the action, and $S'$, $S''$ its continuations

args.name: \mathsf{unfold}
args.meaning: the head normal form, which unfolds $\mu$ and removes leading $\mathsf{Skip}$

E-Close.unfold.title: Close head
E-Close.unfold.why: Rules read the first action of $S$ after unfolding.

args.name: S
args.meaning: the session type of the end before the action, and $S'$, $S''$ its continuations

args.name: \mathsf{unfold}
args.meaning: the head normal form, which unfolds $\mu$ and removes leading $\mathsf{Skip}$

E-Select.unfold.title: Select head
E-Select.unfold.why: Rules read the first action of $S$ after unfolding.

args.name: S
args.meaning: the session type of the end before the action, and $S'$, $S''$ its continuations

args.name: \mathsf{unfold}
args.meaning: the head normal form, which unfolds $\mu$ and removes leading $\mathsf{Skip}$

E-Branch.unfold.title: Branch head
E-Branch.unfold.why: Rules read the first action of $S$ after unfolding.

args.name: S
args.meaning: the session type of the end before the action, and $S'$, $S''$ its continuations

args.name: \mathsf{unfold}
args.meaning: the head normal form, which unfolds $\mu$ and removes leading $\mathsf{Skip}$

E-Link.tickets.title: $a_1 + m_2 > N$ and $a_2 + m_1 > N$
E-Link.tickets.meaning: The credit of each linked end exceeds $N - m$ for the tickets $m$ of the other linked end, the bound on the tickets of the dual end of that end.
E-Link.tickets.why: After the link the thread holding $\overline{o_1}$ faces $\overline{o_2}$, whose counter is at most $N - m_2 < a_1$, and $a_1$ bounds the counter of $o_1$ from below. The new dual end a waiting thread faces therefore has a lower counter than the old one, and the invariant on the tickets of a channel holds for the new pair.
E-Link.tickets.breaks: Without the premise a thread relinks the dual end of a waiting end to a new end with a full counter in each round, and the wait never ends.
E-Link.tickets.example: At $N = 4$ ends at $S_x\inmode{lf}{^{3,3}}$ and $\overline{S}_{\overline{x}}\inmode{lf}{^{3,3}}$ can be linked, and ends at credit $1$ cannot.
E-Link.tickets.signature: a_1 + m_2 > N \land a_2 + m_1 > N

args.name: a_1, a_2
args.meaning: the credits of the two linked ends

args.name: N
args.meaning: the bound on the tickets of a channel

E-Link.dual.title: Linked ends dual
E-Link.dual.meaning: $e$ returns $S_x \otimes \overline{S}_{\overline{x}}$, two ends at dual types and dual points.
E-Link.dual.why: After the link the dual ends of the two ends form one channel. They are a well-typed pair only when the linked ends are exactly dual at dual points.

args.name: \overline{S}_{\overline{x}}
args.meaning: the second, at the dual type and dual point

E-Chan.crtk.title: Credit at most tickets, $a \leq m$
E-Chan.crtk.meaning: The end that E-Chan reads has credit at most its tickets.
E-Chan.crtk.why: Each end of a context is typed by E-Chan or aged, and both ask $a \leq m$. So each context that types a term has $a \leq m$ on each end, and [[th-terms|fuel from cost typing]] may start each end at its tickets.
E-Chan.crtk.breaks: Without it $o : S_x^{5,2} \vdash o : S_x^{5,2}$ types, and no counter lies between the credit $5$ and the tickets $2$.

E-New.bot.title: Lower bound $\bot$
E-New.bot.meaning: The pair is at a fresh base $\rho$, and no fact of $\Gamma$ mentions a point of its tree.
E-New.bot.why: $\exists^{\bot}$ records that the ends of the value are at points without a known lower bound. $\bot$ enters the active points of the value, so a thread that holds it may not wait.

args.name: \bot
args.meaning: the lower bound of the existential, no point of the context lies below its ends

E-New.facts.title: The constraint $C$
E-New.facts.meaning: A set of facts, which may be infinite, over the fresh base $\rho$, its shifts and fields, and points of $\Gamma$.
E-New.facts.why: The derivation chooses the facts the new channel needs, and an interval $l \prec \rho \prec u$ is the simplest case. Opening the existential adds $C$ to $\Gamma$.
E-New.facts.breaks: With facts limited to finitely many bounds by held ends, a client and server loop that orders the points of its infinitely many rounds at once has no typing.

args.name: C
args.meaning: the facts of the creation, chosen by the derivation

E-New.wf.title: $\inmodeplain{df}{\mathsf{acyc\_new}}\inmode{lf}{\mathsf{new\_ok}_N}\,\Gamma\,\rho\,C$
E-New.wf.meaning: The facts $C$ of a creation at a fresh base meet $\mathsf{acyc\_new}$\inmode{lf}{ at $N = \infty$ and $\mathsf{gen\_new}$ at a finite bound}.
E-New.wf.why: The fundamental theorem grows the world by the new tree. \inmode{lf}{A strict world stays strict under $\mathsf{acyc\_new}$, and a ranked world finds ranks for the tree under $\mathsf{gen\_new}$.}
E-New.wf.breaks: A fact from the tree down to a context point with nothing below it in $\Gamma$, or a cycle through the tree, would leave no world that satisfies $C$.

E-New.field.title: A field $x\cdot\kappa$
E-New.field.meaning: The field case of E-New places the new channel at a field $x\cdot\kappa$ of a point $x$ and its dual, with the constraint $\top$ and no bound point.
E-New.field.why: The order around a field was fixed with its base, so a field creation adds no fact and abstracts no point. A field may be used by more than one creation. \inmode{lf}{Its ranks in a ranked world were chosen when the base was created.}
E-New.field.breaks: A field creation that stated a new fact could contradict the facts fixed with the base of $x$.\inmode{lf}{ It could also ask a rank that the base left no room for.}
E-New.field.example: The example with a channel between two box arguments creates $d$ at $\iota\cdot 0$.

E-New.dual.title: Dual pair
E-New.dual.meaning: $c^{+}$ has type $S_{p}\inmode{lf}{^{m_1,m_1}}$ and $c^{-}$ type $\overline{S}_{\overline{p}}\inmode{lf}{^{m_2,m_2}}$ for the position $p$, the fresh base or the field. \inmode{lf}{Each end starts at credit equal to its tickets.}
E-New.dual.why: \inmode{lf}{Fuel starts each counter of a new channel at the tickets of its end\inmode{lf}{, and the credits} are lower bounds on these counters.}

args.name: S
args.meaning: the protocol, chosen by the derivation

args.name: p
args.meaning: the position, the fresh base $\rho$ or the field $x\cdot\kappa$

args.name: m_1, m_2
args.meaning: the tickets of the two ends, chosen by the derivation

E-New.tickets.title: $m_1 + m_2 \leq N$
E-New.tickets.meaning: The creation picks the tickets of the two new ends with sum at most $N$.
E-New.tickets.why: The bound on the tickets of a channel then holds for each new channel, so E-Link can read the bound on the tickets of the dual end off the type of an end.
E-New.tickets.breaks: Tickets above the bound break the premise of E-Link, which compares a credit with $N - m$.

args.name: m_1, m_2
args.meaning: the tickets of the new ends

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, $N \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$}

E-Sub.cost.title: Effects may rise
E-Sub.cost.why: The cost is an upper bound, so a larger bound is also correct. The branches of a case and closures passed to one parameter have different effects, and the larger bound covers both.

E-Weak.drop.title: Weakening
E-Weak.drop.meaning: $\Delta'$ arises from $\Delta$ by emptying entries of unlimited type only.
E-Weak.drop.why: A linear entry may hold ends that must be used, so only entries of unlimited type are dropped.

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the context of the conclusion, with additional unlimited entries

E-Pack.lb.title: Lower bound of a pack
E-Pack.lb.meaning: $l \preccurlyeq T[\bar x]$, each head of the packed value lies at or above $l$. $l = \bot$ asks nothing of the ends, and $l = \top$ asks that $T[\bar x]$ holds no end.
E-Pack.lb.why: After packing, a holding thread refers to the ends only through $l$, so $l$ must bound the active points of the packed value from below. The value relation at an existential states exactly this bound.

args.name: l
args.meaning: the lower bound of the existential

E-Pack.wf.title: Well-formed existential
E-Pack.wf.meaning: Under $\Gamma$ and $C$ at the bound variables $\bar\iota$, the lower bound satisfies $l \preccurlyeq T$. Each head of $T$ lies at or above $l$, and $l = \top$ asks that $T$ holds no end.
E-Pack.wf.why: The condition reads the type alone. It makes opening at the binder complete for each lower bound, so the algorithmic system can open eagerly.
E-Pack.wf.breaks: Without it an existential at a point lower bound may be packed at one instance and need a later instance to be repacked, and no single place to open it is best.

args.name: l
args.meaning: the lower bound of the existential

args.name: C
args.meaning: the constraint at the bound variables

E-Open.entry.title: Opened entry
E-Open.entry.why: Opening replaces entry $i$ in place, and the entry stays linear. Each linear variable of a typed term occurs in the term, and a linear existential opened to an unlimited body could otherwise be dropped unused.

args.name: i
args.meaning: the de Bruijn index of the opened variable

E-Open.body.title: Body after opening
E-Open.body.meaning: $e$ is typed with $C(\bar\iota)$ added to $\Gamma$ and entry $i$ replaced by $T$, under the same future and result.
E-Open.body.why: The fresh variables stand for the unknown witness, and $C$ is the only hypothesis about the witness in the scope. Freshness keeps them out of $F$ and $U$.

args.name: \bar\iota
args.meaning: the fresh point variables of the existential

args.name: U
args.meaning: the result type, which mentions no $\bar\iota$

E-Open.cons.title: Conservativity $\mathsf{conserv}_{\Gamma}(\bar\iota, C)$
E-Open.cons.meaning: Each fact $z \prec y$ between points outside $\mathsf{tree}(\bar\iota)$ that $\Gamma, C(\bar\iota)$ derives, $\Gamma$ derives already. Opening adds facts about the $m$ fresh points $\bar\iota$ and none between old points.
E-Open.cons.why: A dead arm or an uncalled abstraction receives no value, so the type of its binder may state arbitrary facts. Without the premise opening such a binder supplies the arm with an order fact that no world holds. The premise reads only the static order. E-New asks the same condition at one base, so each existential it creates satisfies the premise.
E-Open.cons.breaks: Without it the flag variant types. Its dead arm opens a binder whose constraint states $y \prec \overline{x}$, and the running arm asks only $x \prec \overline{y}$ of the world.
E-Open.cons.example: Opening $\exists^{\top}.\,\{y \prec \overline{x}\}.\,\ast$ in a world with only $x \prec \overline{y}$ fails the premise. Its one fact orders two old points, and the world does not derive $y \prec \overline{x}$.
E-Open.cons.signature: \mathsf{conserv}_{\Gamma}(\bar\iota, C) \iff \forall z, y \notin \mathsf{tree}(\bar\iota).\ \Gamma, C(\bar\iota) \vdash z \prec y \Rightarrow \Gamma \vdash z \prec y

args.name: \Gamma
args.meaning: the fact context before the opening

args.name: \bar\iota
args.meaning: the $m$ fresh point variables of the existential

args.name: C
args.meaning: the constraint of the opened existential

args.name: z, y
args.meaning: old points, outside the tree of $\bar\iota$

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{conserv}_{\Gamma}(\bar\iota, C)$ is `conserv W Γ m C`, stated over the points of $\Gamma$ shifted past the $m$ binders, which are the points outside the tree. The typing rules check the finite form `cons_open W Γ m C`. It asks $\Gamma$ to derive $z \prec y$ for each path `bridge_at` from an old point $z$ to an old point $y$. Such a path uses one fact of $C$, or it enters the tree by a fact of $C$, follows facts of $C$ and program order inside the tree and leaves by a fact of $C$. `cons_open_iff` proves `cons_open` and `conserv` equivalent for a world whose facts lie at constant bases.

pfree.title: $\mathsf{pfree}\,\Sigma$
pfree.why: P-Term puts each channel whose two ends the thread holds into $C_0$. Hence an interface never holds both ends of a channel, which the semantic P-Connect needs.
pfree.breaks: No program is lost, because such a channel always moves into $C_0$.
pfree.example: $\Sigma = \{c^{+}, c^{-}\}$ is rejected, and $(\{c\}, \ldots)$ with $\Sigma = \varnothing$ types instead.

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S_x$

P-Term.C0.title: $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_B = \mathsf{ends}(C_0)$
P-Term.C0.meaning: $o \in \mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_B$ iff the channel of $o$ is in $C_0$.
P-Term.C0.why: Each end of the thread is an interface end or an end of a restricted channel, and the second kind is exactly $\Theta_B$.

args.name: \Theta_B
args.meaning: the entries of the restricted ends

args.name: C_0
args.meaning: the restricted channels of the thread

P-Term.disj.title: $\mathsf{chans}\,\Sigma \cap C_0 = \varnothing$
P-Term.disj.meaning: No channel of the interface is restricted.
P-Term.disj.why: Then each end of $\Sigma\inmode{lf}{^{N}} \cup \Theta_B$ lies in exactly one part, and the interface is the environment restricted to the channels outside $C_0$.

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S_x$

P-Term.pairs.title: Restricted pairs dual
P-Term.pairs.meaning: For each $c \in C_0$ there are $S$ and $x$\inmode{lf}{, and tickets $m$ and $m'$,} with $\Theta_B(c^{+}) = S_x\inmode{lf}{^{m,m}}$, $\Theta_B(c^{-}) = \overline{S}_{\overline{x}}\inmode{lf}{^{m',m'}}$\inmode{lf}{ and $m + m' \leq N$}.
P-Term.pairs.why: A restricted channel has both ends inside the process. \inmode{lf}{They synchronize with each other only, so they need dual types at dual points, and their tickets meet the bound of each channel.}
P-Term.pairs.signature: \forall c \in C_0.\ \exists S\,x\inmode{lf}{\,m\,m'}.\ \Theta_B(c^{+}) = S_x\inmode{lf}{^{m,m}} \land \Theta_B(c^{-}) = \overline{S}_{\overline{x}}\inmode{lf}{^{m',m'}}\inmode{lf}{ \land m + m' \leq N}

args.name: S, x
args.meaning: the type and point of its positive end

args.name: m, m'
args.meaning: the tickets of its two ends

P-Term.typed.title: Thread typing
P-Term.typed.meaning: $t$ is typed under no facts, the interface ends and $\Theta_B$, and the empty future.
P-Term.typed.why: The process judgment has static premises only. Its semantic content comes from the fundamental theorems.

args.name: \Sigma\inmode{lf}{^{\eta}}
args.meaning: the interface as a context of ends\inmode{lf}{, each end $o$ at $\eta(o)$}

P-Term.future.title: Empty future
P-Term.future.meaning: A thread at top level runs under the empty future $\varnothing$.
P-Term.future.why: A thread has no context, so no point lies in its future.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future of a top-level thread

lf.N.title: $N \in \mathbb{N}$
lf.N.meaning: The bound of lock-free typing is a natural number.
lf.N.why: Lock freedom ranks waiting threads by counters as natural numbers, and at $N = \infty$ each counter is $\infty$.

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, $N \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$}

P-Connect.left.title: Left component
P-Connect.left.meaning: $(C_1, E_1)$ is typed over $\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_C$ in $W_1$ at result $T$.
P-Connect.left.why: The main thread lies on the left, so the left side has the result $T$ and the right side returns $\ast$.

args.name: \Sigma_C
args.meaning: the cut, the ends connected to the right component

P-Connect.right.title: Right component at $\ast$
P-Connect.right.meaning: $(C_2, E_2)$ is typed over $\Sigma_2 \cup \overline{\Sigma_C}$ in $W_2$ at result $\ast$.
P-Connect.right.why: Only the main thread returns a value, and each other thread returns $\ast$.

args.name: \overline{\Sigma_C}
args.meaning: the dual ends of the cut

P-Connect.cut.title: Exact dual cut $\overline{\Sigma_C}$
P-Connect.cut.meaning: $\overline{\Sigma_C}$ maps $\overline{o}$ to $\overline{S}_{\overline{x}}$ for each $o \mapsto S_x$ in $\Sigma_C$.
P-Connect.cut.why: The rule pairs each end of the cut with the exact dual of its type and point. \inmode{lf}{After composition the two ends of each cut channel are restricted, and lock freedom asks their protocols dual up to annotations, which the exact dual gives.}
P-Connect.cut.breaks: \inmode{lf}{An annotation mismatch on a cut channel breaks the payload credit of a later message.}

P-Connect.disj.title: Disjoint channels
P-Connect.disj.meaning: The channel sets of $\Sigma_1$, $\Sigma_2$, $\Sigma_C$ are pairwise disjoint, $C_1 \cap C_2 = \varnothing$, and each $C_i$ is disjoint from the channels of $\Sigma_1$, $\Sigma_2$, $\Sigma_C$.
P-Connect.disj.why: Each channel then belongs to one side. The cut $\Sigma_C$ is the only channel set both sides use, so composition merges no two channels. Disjoint domains of $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_C$, and of $\Sigma_2$ and $\overline{\Sigma_C}$, follow from disjoint channel sets.
P-Connect.disj.example: Two closes cut at $c$ with $\Sigma_1 = \Sigma_2 = \varnothing$ and $C_1 = C_2 = \varnothing$.

args.name: C_1, C_2
args.meaning: the restricted channels of the components

P-Connect.wf.title: The join of the two worlds is checked
P-Connect.wf.meaning: $\mathsf{cons}(W_1 \sqcup W_2)$\inmode{lf}{ at $N = \infty$ and $\mathsf{wf}(W_1 \sqcup W_2)$ at a finite bound}, where $W_1$ and $W_2$ are the worlds of the two components.
P-Connect.wf.why: The check reads only the two component worlds. Two components may pick the same private constant for unrelated points. The join then has more facts, and the check reads each such fact. If they order that constant oppositely, the join has a cycle. A bijection on constants that fixes the interface of one component then renames its derivation, and the two worlds share only constants of both interfaces. The condition is not pairwise. The [[ex-ring3|ring of three threads]] is consistent two components at a time and inconsistent as a whole. The composite therefore keeps the joined order for the next P-Connect, and the ring is rejected.
P-Connect.wf.breaks: If $W_1$ derives $\rho \prec \overline{\tau}$ and $W_2$ derives $\overline{\tau} \prec \rho$ for interface points, the join has a cycle and two threads each wait on the other although each side alone is ready.
P-Connect.wf.example: Two components over an empty interface whose worlds share the constant $0$ compose when their join is consistent.

deviations.reason: The rule asks `wok N (W1 ⊔ W2)` only. The join of the two component worlds is well formed by `ptyped_wf`, so the folded $\mathsf{cons}$ and $\mathsf{wf}$ of the join ask nothing more.

P-Term.wf.title: $\inmodeplain{df}{\mathsf{cons}}\inmode{lf}{\mathsf{ok}_N}\,W$
P-Term.wf.meaning: The world of a single thread is consistent\inmode{lf}{ at $N = \infty$ and well-founded at a finite bound}, well-formedness included.
P-Term.wf.why: The world of each process derivation then has an extension of the right kind.
P-Term.wf.breaks: Without it P-Connect would have to check the whole join, and a thread world with a cycle would make the semantic judgment vacuous.

deviations.reason: `p_term` asks `sworld_wf W ∧ wok N W`. The map folds `sworld_wf` into $\mathsf{cons}$ and $\mathsf{ok}_N$.

P-Connect.n.title: The n-ary connect, admissible
P-Connect.n.meaning: Components $p_1, \ldots, p_n$ at worlds $W_1, \ldots, W_n$. Component $i \geq 2$ connects over the cut $\Sigma_{C,i}$ to the composite of the components before it, with the side conditions of P-Connect. One premise reads the worlds, $\mathsf{ok}_N(W_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup W_n)$, and the composite types at that join.
P-Connect.n.why: The rule folds the binary P-Connect. The world of each partial composite is the join of its component worlds, so the one check gives each binary check. The condition is no conjunction of pairwise conditions.
P-Connect.n.breaks: Three threads that each close one end and then the next end round a ring meet each condition but the world check. Their worlds are consistent in pairs and hold a cycle together, and the ring deadlocks.
P-Connect.n.example: The ring whose third thread closes its two ends in the other order types and is deadlock free.

args.name: \Sigma_{C,i}
args.meaning: the cut of component $i$ against the composite of the components before it

deviations.reason: `p_connect_n` concludes a derivation at some world $W$ with $W \sqsubseteq W_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup W_n$ and $W_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup W_n \sqsubseteq W$, the join `sw_joins` of the list, because the binary joins of the fold nest to the left. Both have the same bases and the same facts, and the map writes the join.

P-Connect.join.title: Result at the join
P-Connect.join.meaning: The composite is typed in $W_1 \sqcup W_2$.
P-Connect.join.why: The join keeps the facts of both components, so a later P-Connect checks each of them against the worlds of further components.
P-Connect.join.example: Two closes cut at $c$ type in the world with no constants.

tp.iface.title: $\mathsf{I}(\Sigma, T)$
tp.iface.meaning: The constants that occur in the points and session types of $\Sigma$ and in $T$.
tp.iface.why: These are the constants a renaming must fix to leave the interface alone. They contain the bases of the points of $\Sigma$.

tp.Sigma.title: The interface $\Sigma$
tp.Sigma.meaning: $\Sigma$ is a finite map from the ends a process offers to its environment to pairs $S_x$ of a session type and a point.
tp.Sigma.why: A process is typed against its interface, and composition cuts interface ends against each other.

args.name: o
args.meaning: an end offered to the environment

tp.pjudg.title: $\Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N,\eta}}_{W} p : T$
tp.pjudg.meaning: The process $p$ is typed over $\Sigma$ in $W$\inmode{lf}{ at bound $N$}\inmode{lf}{ with interface annotations $\eta$} with result $T$, derived by P-Term and P-Connect. A component is typed by the pair of $\Sigma$ and $W$.
tp.pjudg.why: \inmode{lf}{One judgment serves deadlock freedom at $N = \infty$ and lock freedom at finite $N$.} Its soundness reads each component at the world $W$ of its derivation.

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S_x$

args.name: W
args.meaning: the world whose order $\prec_W$ the rule reads

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, $N \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$}

args.name: \eta
args.meaning: the interface annotations, a credit and tickets for each end

args.name: p
args.meaning: the process $(C, E)$, restricted channels $C$ and a multiset $E$ of threads

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

tp.lfjudg.title: $\Sigma \Vdash^{N,\eta}_{W} p : T$
tp.lfjudg.meaning: $\Sigma \Vdash^{N,\eta}_{W} p : T$ iff $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N,\eta}}_{W} p : T$.
tp.lfjudg.why: Lock freedom needs finite counters. A loop is charged at each force, so no separate check on terms is needed.
tp.lfjudg.example: Two threads closing $c^{+}$ and $c^{-}$, at each $N \in \mathbb{N}$.

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S_x$

args.name: W
args.meaning: the world whose order $\prec_W$ the rule reads

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, $N \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$}

args.name: p
args.meaning: the process $(C, E)$, restricted channels $C$ and a multiset $E$ of threads

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

tp.chans.title: $\mathsf{chans}\,\Sigma$
tp.chans.meaning: The set of channels of the ends in $\mathrm{dom}\,\Sigma$.
tp.chans.why: Restricted sets are sets of channels, so disjointness is stated on channels.

tp.ends.title: $\mathsf{ends}(C)$
tp.ends.why: A restricted channel contributes both its ends.

tp.lift.title: The interface as a context of ends
tp.lift.meaning: $\Sigma$ as a context of ends\inmode{lf}{, each end $o$ at the credit and tickets $\eta(o)$}.
tp.lift.why: The dual end of an interface end belongs to another component. \inmode{lf}{The annotations of the two ends of a cut channel meet the bound $N$ by the premise of P-Connect.}

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S_x$

args.name: \eta
args.meaning: the interface annotations, a credit and tickets for each end

E-Box.fresh.title: $\bar\iota$ fresh
E-Box.fresh.meaning: The bound point variables $\bar\iota$ occur nowhere in $\Gamma$, $\Delta$, $F$ or the result type.
E-Box.fresh.why: They stand for points chosen later, at each force or for the unknown witness of an existential, so nothing in scope may mention these variables. The Rocq uses de Bruijn indices and shifts the context instead.
E-Box.fresh.example: Opening $\exists^{\bot}\iota.\,C.\,T$ under a context that mentions $\rho$ picks $\iota \neq \rho$.

tp.pinst.title: Point instance $T[\bar x]$
tp.pinst.meaning: Replaces the point variables $\bar\iota$ of $T$ by the points $\bar x$.
tp.pinst.why: Forcing and packing choose concrete points for the bound variables.

args.name: T
args.meaning: a type over the bound point variables $\bar\iota$

tp.sinst.title: Session instance $U[\bar s]$
tp.sinst.meaning: Replaces the session variables of $U$ by the session types $\bar s$.
tp.sinst.why: A box is polymorphic in its session variables, and each force chooses an instance.

args.name: U
args.meaning: a type over the session variables $\bar\alpha$

tp.sinsts.title: Allowed session instances $\mathsf{sinsts}\,\bar s$
tp.sinsts.meaning: The session types a session variable of a box may stand for. Each $s \in \bar s$ is contractive, and no payload of $s$ mentions a point free below its binder. \inmode{lf}{At $N = \infty$ each $s$ also has no finite credit.}
tp.sinsts.why: The rules read the first action of a protocol after unfolding, and a contractive instance keeps a contractive type contractive and keeps $\inmodeplain{df}{\approx}\inmodeplain{lf}{\simeq}$. \inmode{lf}{At $N = \infty$ each annotation in a derivation is $\infty$, and an instance with a finite credit inside its payloads would bring one in.}
tp.sinsts.breaks: Without contractivity a box with a variable $\alpha$ could be forced at $\mu\alpha.\alpha$, and an end of type $\mu\alpha.\alpha$ would be stuck with no action to perform.
tp.sinsts.example: $\mu\alpha.\,!\ast.\alpha$ and $\mathsf{Close}$ are allowed, $\mu\alpha.\alpha$ and $\mu\alpha.\,\mathsf{Skip}.\alpha$ are not.

args.name: N
args.meaning: the bound on the tickets of a channel, $N \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

tp.max.title: $\max(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2)$
tp.max.meaning: The larger of two costs, $\max(c_1, c_2)$.
tp.max.why: Only one branch of a case runs, so its effect is bounded by the larger of the two.

args.name: \varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2
args.meaning: the effects of the two branches

tp.vdash.title: The term turnstile $\vdash$
tp.vdash.meaning: The least relation closed under E-Unit to E-Open. \inmode{lf}{The deadlock-free judgment $\Gamma ; \Delta \vdash^{F} t : T$ is the instance $N = \infty$ with each annotation $\infty$.}
tp.vdash.why: \inmode{lf}{One relation has the session type, the points and, in the lock-free mode, the\inmode{lf}{ credits and }the effect of $e$, so each mode reads its premises off one derivation.}

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the linear context, ends $o$ with end types and de Bruijn indices with types

args.name: H
args.meaning: the entries the thread holds while $e$ runs, a context or a type

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, the points at which the context acts after the term

tp.msunion.title: Multiset union $E_1 \uplus E_2$
tp.msunion.meaning: $E_1 \uplus E_2$, the multiset sum, counts each thread as often as $E_1$ and $E_2$ together.
tp.msunion.why: A composite process runs the threads of both components side by side.

args.name: E_1, E_2
args.meaning: the thread multisets of the two components

ord.ord.title: Ordinals
ord.ord.meaning: Brouwer trees, built from $0$, the successor $\alpha + 1$ and the supremum of a family $f$ indexed by a type $X$.
ord.ord.why: The relation is indexed by ordinals. \inmode{lf}{A limit index lets a choice made at each index, such as the annotated configuration of the lock-free judgment, be fixed once and used at each index.}
ord.ord.breaks: At the finite indices alone, $\forall n.\ \exists a$ does not give $\exists a.\ \forall n$ for an infinite space of choices.

args.name: X
args.meaning: the index type of a limit

ord.lt.title: Order of ordinals
ord.lt.meaning: $\beta < \alpha$ when $\beta + 1 \leq \alpha$, with $\leq$ defined by structural recursion on the trees.
ord.lt.why: The relation reads a successor at each smaller index the cost of a step allows.

ord.wf.title: Well-founded order
ord.wf.meaning: Each descending sequence of ordinals is finite.
ord.wf.why: The relation is defined by recursion on the index, which needs a well-founded order.

ord.add.title: $\beta + c$
ord.add.meaning: The $c$-fold successor of $\beta$ for a natural number $c$, the cost of a step.
ord.add.why: A step of cost $c > 0$ at index $\alpha$ reads its successor at each $\beta$ with $\beta + c \leq \alpha$, which lies strictly below $\alpha$.

ord.fix.title: $\mathsf{osfix}$
ord.fix.meaning: The family defined by well-founded recursion on the index, where $F$ reads the family only strictly below $\alpha$.
ord.fix.why: $V$, $E$ and $P$ together are one such family, unfolded up to pointwise equivalence.\inmode{lf}{ Fuel is a second one.}

ord.exprop.title: The existential property
ord.exprop.meaning: Under excluded middle and functional choice, a family $P\,x\,\alpha$ closed downwards in $\alpha$ with a witness at each index has one witness that serves each index.
ord.exprop.why: The lock-free judgment chooses an annotated configuration at each index, and lock-free soundness needs one that holds at each index. The proof takes a failing index for each witness and the supremum of these indices.
ord.exprop.breaks: At finite indices a choice of $n$ at each index $n$ has no common witness.
ord.exprop.example: $\forall \alpha.\ \exists a.\ a \in S_\alpha$ gives $\exists a.\ \forall \alpha.\ a \in S_\alpha$.

args.name: P
args.meaning: a family down-closed in the index

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{EM}$ and $\mathsf{FC}$ abbreviate `excluded_middle` and `functional_choice` of `FairRun.v`.

sj.sw.title: Semantic judgment at a world
sj.sw.meaning: $\Sigma \vDash_W p : T$ holds when $p \in P^{W'}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma \vdash T\rrbracket$ for each ordinal index $\alpha$ and each consistent extension $W'$ of $W$\inmode{lf}{ that is strict}.
sj.sw.why: A typing derivation fixes a world over the constants of its interface, and the relation reads worlds that hold the bases of a run. The semantic judgment at $W$ reads each consistent extension of $W$, and semantic P-Connect composes two components at one consistent extension of the join.

deviations.reason: The Rocq quantifies over the Rocq worlds of type `world` that `wmodels` relates to $W$, and the map writes them as consistent extensions. At each of them it reads `sem_ptyped`, whose Rocq notation is $\Sigma \vDash_W p : T$. The map writes that judgment out as $\forall \alpha.\ p \in P^{W'}_{\alpha}\llbracket \Sigma \vdash T \rrbracket$, so that $\vDash_W$ names this judgment alone.
At $\kappa_L$ the Rocq writes `⊫`. The map writes $\vDash[\kappa_L]$, the instance of the family $\vDash[\kappa]$, as for terms.

ct.table.title: Cost table $\kappa$
ct.table.meaning: A tuple $\kappa \in \mathbb{N}^7$ of costs, one per kind of step.
ct.table.why: One relation parametric in $\kappa$ yields both the relation at $\kappa_{DF}$ and the relation at $\kappa_L$, so each compatibility proof is done once and holds at each $\kappa$.

args.name: \kappa_\beta, \ldots, \kappa_{\mathrm{take}}
args.meaning: the costs of $\beta$, force, creation, spawn, link, give and take

ct.take-pos.title: $1 \leq \kappa_{\mathrm{take}}$
ct.take-pos.meaning: Receive and branch cost at least one level.
ct.take-pos.why: A receive reads $V$ of its payload negatively at the level of its continuation, so that level is $\beta < \alpha$ and $V_\alpha$ is well defined.
ct.take-pos.breaks: With $\kappa_{\mathrm{take}} = 0$, $V_\alpha$ would quantify negatively over $V_\alpha$ and the fixpoint would not exist.

ct.give-pos.title: $\kappa_\beta = 0 \Rightarrow 1 \leq \kappa_{\mathrm{give}}$
ct.give-pos.meaning: If $\beta$ is free, a give costs at least one level.
ct.give-pos.why: For $\kappa_\beta = 0$, $V_\alpha$ and $E_\alpha$ are defined together by recursion on the size of the type, and a free send would read $V_\alpha$ at a payload type of unbounded size.

ct.give-take.title: $\kappa_{\mathrm{give}} \leq \kappa_{\mathrm{take}}$
ct.give-take.meaning: A give costs at most a take.
ct.give-take.why: A synchronization costs $\kappa_{\mathrm{give}} + \kappa_{\mathrm{take}}$, and composing two components counts a synchronization as two gives, which needs $2\kappa_{\mathrm{give}} \leq \kappa_{\mathrm{give}} + \kappa_{\mathrm{take}}$.

ct.DF.title: $\kappa_{DF}$, the step index
ct.DF.meaning: The table $(1,1,1,1,0,0,1)$. It is the ordinary step index of a logical relation. Each step but a send, select, close or link costs one level.
ct.DF.why: A step index lets $V$ and $E$ refer to themselves at lower levels, which recursion and received closures need. A link and the give actions cost nothing, and their successor is checked at the same level. A send therefore passes its payload on at the level of the continuation.
ct.DF.example: $\beta$ and $\mathsf{recv}$ cost one level, $\mathsf{send}$ costs none.

ct.L.title: $\kappa_L$, the lock-free table
ct.L.meaning: The table $(0,1,0,0,0,1,1)$. The free steps, $\beta$, $\mathsf{new}$, $\mathsf{spawn}$ and $\mathsf{link}$, cost nothing. A force and the session actions cost a level.
ct.L.why: A free step is checked inside the least fixpoint of the current level, and a least fixpoint admits only finitely many steps in a row. So a term in the relation at $\kappa_L$ cannot take infinitely many free steps in a row, which is absence of divergence by free steps. A loop goes through a force, and a force costs a level.
ct.L.breaks: With a free force, $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$ steps forever inside one level and is in no relation.
ct.L.example: Under $\kappa_L$ a synchronization costs $2$, one level for each side.

ct.beta.title: Cost $\kappa_\beta$
ct.beta.meaning: The cost of application, pair and unit elimination and case.
ct.beta.why: An arrow reads its body at each $\beta < \alpha$ under $\kappa_{DF}$. \inmode{lf}{Under a general table it reads the levels $\beta$ with $\beta + \kappa_\beta \leq \alpha$, which for $\kappa_L$ include $\alpha$ itself.}

ct.new.title: Cost $\kappa_{\mathrm{new}}$
ct.new.why: \inmode{lf}{Creation synchronizes with nobody, so $\kappa_L$ counts it as an internal step.}

ct.spawn.title: Cost $\kappa_{\mathrm{spawn}}$
ct.spawn.why: For $\kappa_{\mathrm{spawn}} = 0$ the child thunk is read inside the least fixpoint of the parent, so an infinite chain of spawns is in no $E_\alpha$.

ct.link.title: Cost $\kappa_{\mathrm{link}}$
ct.link.meaning: The cost of $\mathsf{link}$, $0$ in $\kappa_{DF}$. \inmode{lf}{It is $0$ in $\kappa_L$ as well.}
ct.link.why: A link acts alone and synchronizes with nobody, so it is an internal step.
ct.link.breaks: \inmode{lf}{Under $\kappa_L$ a loop that creates and links forever is an infinite sequence of internal steps and lies in no $E_\alpha$.}
ct.link.example: $!(f = \mathsf{let}\ \langle a, b\rangle = \mathsf{new}\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{let}\ \ast = \mathsf{link}\,\langle a, b\rangle\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{force}\,f)$ diverges internally.

ct.give.title: Cost $\kappa_{\mathrm{give}}$
ct.give.why: The obligation of a give reads the continuation at the levels $\beta$ with $\beta + \kappa_{\mathrm{give}} \leq \alpha$.

deviations.reason: The cost field `c_give` applies to $\mathsf{send}$, $\mathsf{select}$ and $\mathsf{close}$, which the formula names by their keywords.

ct.takek.title: Cost $\kappa_{\mathrm{take}}$
ct.takek.meaning: The cost of $\mathsf{recv}$ and $\mathsf{branch}$, $1$ in $\kappa_{DF}$. \inmode{lf}{It is $1$ in $\kappa_L$ as well.}
ct.takek.why: The obligation of a take reads each incoming value at the levels $\beta$ with $\beta + \kappa_{\mathrm{take}} \leq \alpha$, so $\beta < \alpha$.

deviations.reason: The cost field `c_take` applies to $\mathsf{recv}$ and $\mathsf{branch}$, which the formula names by their keywords.

ct.sync.title: Cost of an event $\kappa(ev)$
ct.sync.meaning: $\kappa(ev)$ is the cost of the step kind of $ev$, and $\kappa_{\mathrm{give}} + \kappa_{\mathrm{take}}$ for a synchronization.
ct.sync.why: Both threads of a synchronization step at once, so the step of the process costs the sum of both costs.
ct.sync.example: A message costs $1$ under $\kappa_{DF}$\inmode{lf}{ and $2$ under $\kappa_L$}.

args.name: ev
args.meaning: an event of the instrumented semantics

rel.atcost.title: $e'$ at $\Theta'$
rel.atcost.meaning: Take a step $\ell$ of cost $c = \kappa(\ell)$ at the ordinal index $\alpha$. Its successor is read in the fixpoint $X$ if $c = 0$, and in $E_\beta$ for each ordinal $\beta$ with $\beta + c \leq \alpha$ if $c > 0$, with $\beta + c$ the $c$-fold successor of $\beta$.
rel.atcost.why: Stated as two implications, $X$ occurs strictly positively and the inductive definition is admissible. At a successor $\alpha = \gamma + c$ the second case is the index $\gamma$, and at a limit $\lambda$ it is each $\beta < \lambda$, the later modality of transfinite step indexing.
rel.atcost.example: \inmode{lf}{Under $\kappa_L$ a $\beta$ step stays at index $\alpha$, and at the limit $\omega$ a step of cost $2$ obliges the successor at each finite index.}

args.name: c = \kappa(\ell)
args.meaning: the cost of the step label $\ell$

args.name: X
args.meaning: the least fixpoint under construction at index $\alpha$

rel.lfp.title: Least fixpoint $X$
rel.lfp.meaning: $E_\alpha$ and $P_\alpha$ are the least fixpoints of their clauses over steps of cost $0$.
rel.lfp.why: \inmode{lf}{A least fixpoint admits only finite sequences of cost-$0$ steps, so under $\kappa_L$ no term in $E_\alpha$ diverges internally.}
rel.lfp.breaks: A greatest fixpoint would admit $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$, which takes only $\beta$ steps.
rel.lfp.example: Induction on $E_\alpha$ is induction on cost-$0$ steps.

args.name: X
args.meaning: the least relation closed under the clauses of index $\alpha$

deviations.reason: $(\mathsf{lfp})$ marks the least fixpoints, the inductive types `Eind` and `Pind`.

V-Unit.title: $V$ at $\ast$
V-Unit.why: A finished thread has result type $T$ or $\ast$, and $\Theta = \varnothing$ shows that a thread holding a value of type $\ast$ holds no end.
V-Unit.breaks: Without $\Theta = \varnothing$, a thread could end as $\ast$ while owning an end on which the thread holding the dual end waits forever.

V-Sess.title: $V$ at $S_x$
V-Sess.meaning: $v \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash S_x\rrbracket \iff \exists o, S'.\ v = o \land \Theta = \{o \mapsto {S'}_x\} \land S' \approx S$.
V-Sess.why: \inmode{lf}{$\Theta$ keeps its annotations for the fuel layer, and $V$ compares session types erased.}

args.name: S'
args.meaning: the session type of $o$ in $\Theta$\inmode{lf}{, with annotations}

V-Sess.exact.title: $\Theta = \{o \mapsto {S'}_x\}$
V-Sess.exact.meaning: The environment of an end value is the singleton of its own entry at the point $x$ of the type.
V-Sess.exact.why: Exact environments make $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$ for each $v \in V$, which fixes ownership at sends and spawns.

args.name: {S'}_x
args.meaning: the entry of $o$, at the point $x$ of the type

V-Prod.title: $V$ at $\otimes$
V-Prod.meaning: $\langle v_1, v_2\rangle \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash T_1 \otimes T_2\rrbracket \iff \exists \Theta_1, \Theta_2.\ \Theta = \Theta_1 \uplus \Theta_2 \land \forall i.\ v_i \in V\llbracket\Theta_i \vdash T_i\rrbracket$.
V-Prod.why: The clause mirrors E-Pair, and the disjoint split keeps environments exact through pairs.

args.name: \Theta_1, \Theta_2
args.meaning: the disjoint parts owned by $v_1$ and $v_2$

V-Prod.split.title: $\Theta = \Theta_1 \uplus \Theta_2$
V-Prod.split.meaning: The components own disjoint parts of $\Theta$.
V-Prod.split.why: An end is owned by exactly one component, so no renaming can move a held end into a box inside a pair.

V-Sum.title: $V$ at $\oplus$
V-Sum.meaning: $\mathsf{inj}_i\,v \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash T_1 \oplus T_2\rrbracket \iff v \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash T_i\rrbracket$.
V-Sum.why: The clause mirrors E-Inj and E-Case, and branch returns its end in an injection.

V-Arrow.exact.title: $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(e)$
V-Arrow.exact.meaning: A closure owns exactly the ends its body mentions.
V-Arrow.exact.why: With it, each $v \in V$ satisfies $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, so the ends a send or spawn passes on are $\mathsf{fends}$ of the value.
V-Arrow.exact.breaks: $\lambda\_.\,\mathsf{let}\ \ast = \Omega\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{close}\,q^{+}$ owns nothing and is in $V$ at each level, and then a send of it next to $q^{+}$ fails E-Send.

V-Arrow.lb.title: $l \preccurlyeq \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta$
V-Arrow.lb.meaning: $\forall z \in \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta.\ l \preccurlyeq z$ in the order of $W$, with $\bot$ below and $\top$ above each bound. So $l = \bot$ asks nothing, and $l = \top$ asks $\mathsf{ap}\,\Theta = \varnothing$.
V-Arrow.lb.why: The thread holding a closure reads its active points through $l$, which bounds the active points of the values it holds.
V-Arrow.lb.example: A closure over $a$ at $\rho$ has $\mathsf{ap}\,\Theta = \{\overline{\rho}\}$ and $l = \overline{\rho}$.

args.name: l
args.meaning: the lower point of the arrow, a point, $\bot$ or $\top$

V-Arrow.kripke.title: $\forall W' \sqsupseteq W$
V-Arrow.kripke.meaning: The body is in $E$ in each extension $W'$ of $W$.
V-Arrow.kripke.why: A closure may be called after composition has extended the world, so $V$ is monotone in $W$.
V-Arrow.kripke.example: A received closure is called in $W \sqcup W'$.

V-Arrow.level.title: Level of the body
V-Arrow.level.meaning: The body is read at each level $\beta < \alpha$, \inmode{lf}{and under a general table at the levels $\beta$ with $\beta + \kappa_{\mathrm{beta}} \leq \alpha$.}
V-Arrow.level.why: A $\beta$-step costs one level in the deadlock-free relation. \inmode{lf}{Under $\kappa_L$, where $\beta$ is free, the body is read at the levels $\beta \leq \alpha$.}
V-Arrow.level.example: The body of a closure in $V_3$ is read at levels $0$ to $2$.

args.name: \beta
args.meaning: the level at which the body is read

V-Arrow.ub.title: $W' \vdash u \prec F$
V-Arrow.ub.meaning: The body is in $E$ under each future $F$ that $u$ lies below, $\forall y \in F.\ W' \vdash u \prec y$ with $\bot$ below and $\top$ above each point. So $u = \bot$ admits each $F$, and $u = \top$ only $F = \varnothing$.
V-Arrow.ub.why: A closure may block up to $u$, so its caller must still act only above $u$.
V-Arrow.ub.example: The body of $\mathsf{between}$ runs under each $F$ above $\kappa$.

args.name: u
args.meaning: the upper point of the arrow, a point, $\bot$ or $\top$

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future of the call, a set of points above $u$

V-Arrow.body.title: Body in $E$
V-Arrow.body.meaning: $e[w] \in E^{W'}_{\beta}\llbracket\Theta \cup \Theta' \vdash U\rrbracket^{F}$ for each argument $w \in V^{W'}_{\beta}\llbracket\Theta' \vdash T\rrbracket$ with $\Theta' \mathbin{\#} \Theta$.
V-Arrow.body.why: The call owns the closure's ends and the argument's ends, which are disjoint, and the compatibility of E-App feeds exactly this union to the body.
V-Arrow.body.example: $\mathsf{cli}$ applied to $\langle a, b\rangle$ runs at $\{a, b\}$.

args.name: \Theta'
args.meaning: the ends of the argument, disjoint from $\Theta$

FV-Arrow.call.title: $\Phi' \geq \Phi - a$
FV-Arrow.call.meaning: At the call each captured end has the protocol it had at creation and a counter at least its counter at creation minus $a$.
FV-Arrow.call.why: Aging a closure by $c \leq a$ lowers $a$ and the counters by $c$ together, so the difference stays, and the body was typed at each credit minus $a$.
FV-Arrow.call.example: A closure at credit $1$ created with counter $3$ on $o$ is called with counter $2$ or more on $o$.
FV-Arrow.call.signature: \forall o.\ \Phi(o) = S^{f} \Rightarrow \Phi'(o) = S^{f'} \land f' \geq f - a

args.name: \Phi'
args.meaning: the captured ends at the call

V-Box.empty.title: $\Theta = \varnothing$
V-Box.empty.meaning: A box value owns no end.
V-Box.empty.why: Each value in $V$ satisfies $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, and at a box this is $\Theta = \varnothing$.
V-Box.empty.breaks: Without it, a box could be copied together with an end it owns.

V-Box.noends.title: $\mathsf{fends}(e) = \varnothing$
V-Box.noends.meaning: The body of a box mentions no end.
V-Box.noends.why: A box is unlimited, so it must be copyable, and an end mentioned inside would be copied with the box.
V-Box.noends.breaks: A box that captures an end under an empty environment could be forced twice and act on the end twice.

V-Box.kripke.title: $\forall W' \sqsupseteq W$
V-Box.kripke.meaning: The body is in $E$ in each extension $W'$ of $W$.
V-Box.kripke.why: $V$ is monotone in $W$, and at a box the extension cannot be pushed into the body clause, because the instances $\bar x$ range over points ordered only in $W'$.
V-Box.kripke.breaks: Without it, a box received after composition could not be forced at an instance whose constraint holds only in the joined world.
V-Box.kripke.example: Forcing a received box in $W \sqcup W'$.

V-Box.inst.title: $W' \vdash C[\bar x]$
V-Box.inst.meaning: The body is in $E$ at each instance $\bar x \in \mathsf{Point}^m$ with $\forall (y \prec z) \in C.\ W' \vdash y[\bar x] \prec z[\bar x]$.
V-Box.inst.why: E-Force asks $\Gamma \vdash C[\bar x]$ at its instance, so the box must work at each instance meeting $C$ and at no other.

args.name: C
args.meaning: the box constraint over $m$ point variables

V-Box.hc.title: Contractive and scoped instances
V-Box.hc.meaning: The body is in $E$ at each list $\bar s$ of $k$ session types that are hereditarily contractive and point-scoped.
V-Box.hc.why: Session instances must unfold to a head, which hereditary contractiveness guarantees. A payload of an instance must mention no point free below its binder, which scoping guarantees, as E-Send and E-Recv ask.

V-Ex.lb.title: $l \preccurlyeq \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta$
V-Ex.lb.meaning: $\forall z \in \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta.\ l \preccurlyeq z$ in the order of $W$, with $\bot$ below and $\top$ above each bound. So $l = \bot$ asks nothing, and $l = \top$ asks $\mathsf{ap}\,\Theta = \varnothing$.
V-Ex.lb.why: It lets a holding thread bound the actual active points of a packed value by its static active points, which the readiness of a send carrying a packed payload and the compatibility of E-Pack use.
V-Ex.lb.breaks: Without it, a sender holding a packed payload could not show its offered end below the dual points of the payload ends.
V-Ex.lb.example: $l = \bot$ for the existential that E-New returns, which asks nothing.

args.name: l
args.meaning: the lower bound, a point, $\bot$ or $\top$

V-Ex.witness.title: A witness in $W$
V-Ex.witness.meaning: $\exists \bar x \in \mathsf{Point}^m.\ W \vdash C[\bar x] \land v \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash T[\bar x]\rrbracket$.
V-Ex.witness.why: Opening an existential substitutes fresh point variables and adds $C$ to $\Gamma$, and the compatibility of E-Open instantiates them with this witness.
V-Ex.witness.example: The fresh base $a$ with the facts $C$ of its creation.
V-Ex.witness.signature: \exists \bar x \in \mathsf{Point}^{m}.\ W \vdash C[\bar x] \land v \in V^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \Theta \vdash T[\bar x] \rrbracket

args.name: T[\bar x]
args.meaning: the body type at the witness

rel.vsize.title: Recursion on $(\alpha, \mathsf{size}\,T)$
rel.vsize.meaning: $V_{\alpha}$ is defined by well-founded recursion on the ordinal $\alpha$ and, inside a level, on the size of the type, with the levels built by one fixpoint $\mathsf{osfix}$. The size counts the constructors of a type, with a box as $3 + \mathsf{size}\,U$ and its thunk $\ast \multimap^{u} U$ as $2 + \mathsf{size}\,U$, so that the box clause reads the thunk at the same level.
rel.vsize.why: Under $\kappa_{DF}$, $V_{\alpha}$ reads $V$ and $E$ at lower levels for closures and boxes, and at smaller types within the level for products, sums and existentials, whose instantiation preserves size. \inmode{lf}{Under $\kappa_L$, $V_{\alpha}$ reads $E_{\beta}$ and $V_{\beta}$ at the levels $\beta \leq \alpha$ and at smaller types, and instantiation preserves size.}

deviations.reason: The Rocq builds the levels with `osfix` in `RelA` and measures types with `tsize`, written $\mathsf{size}$. `Vtop` unfolds `Vbody` with the fuel $\mathsf{size}\,T + 1$, which is the recursion on the size within a level.

P.zero.title: Index $0$
P.zero.why: At an index with nothing below it no step of a process can be read, so the clauses start at $\alpha > 0$. The term relation has no such case, because a term at index $0$ still meets its stop and ready clauses and its steps of cost $0$.

E.kripke.title: $\forall W' \sqsupseteq W$
E.kripke.meaning: Each unfolding of $E$ holds in each extension $W'$ of $W$.
E.kripke.why: $E$ is monotone in $W$ by definition, so no clause needs its own world quantifier.

args.name: W'
args.meaning: an extension of $W$, the world at which the clauses are read

E.stop.title: (stop)
E.stop.why: A term that takes no step must be a value in $V$, so a stuck term is in no $E_\alpha$ for $\alpha > 0$ and adequacy reads termination off $V$.
E.stop.breaks: A stuck non-value would count as well typed, and adequacy would fail.

deviations.reason: $(\mathsf{stop})$ labels the first clause of `Ebody`.

E.ready.title: (ready)
E.ready.why: Readiness excludes circular waiting between threads.
E.ready.breaks: Two threads each waiting on the dual end of the other's second end deadlock.

deviations.reason: $(\mathsf{ready})$ labels the second clause of `Ebody`, and $\mathsf{irred}$ is the Rocq predicate `irred`.

E.step.title: (step)
E.step.why: One conjunct per kind of label keeps $X$ strictly positive.

deviations.reason: $(\mathsf{step})$ labels the clause that `Esteps` and `Eobl` state.

O-Beta.title: O-Beta
O-Beta.why: A $\beta$ step changes no end, and the compatibility of each elimination rule discharges it by reading the redex at the same environment.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-New.title: O-New
O-New.meaning: For a fresh name $c$ some $S$, position $\pi$ and world $W' \sqsupseteq W$ place $c^{+}$ at $S_{\pi}$ and $c^{-}$ at $\overline{S}_{\overline{\pi}}$, and the successor runs in $W'$.
O-New.why: It is the semantic counterpart of E-New. The creation picks the point and grows the world by the bases it needs. For a fresh base the fundamental theorem adds the base and the facts of $C$ to the world. \inmode{lf}{In a ranked world it ranks the new tree above each context point below the tree, and the existential property of ordinal indices fixes the choice once per creation.}

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-New.cfresh.title: $c^{\pm} \notin \mathrm{dom}\,\Theta$
O-New.cfresh.meaning: The new name is no end of $\Theta$.
O-New.cfresh.why: The process rule picks $c$ globally fresh, so the term obligation may assume freshness.

O-New.grow.title: Position and world
O-New.grow.meaning: $\exists S, \pi, W'.\ W \sqsubseteq W'$. The obligation picks the point $\pi$ freely, and $W'$ extends $W$\inmode{lf}{, with the same kind and each rank kept}.
O-New.grow.why: E-New at a fresh base picks a constant $a$ that is no base of $W$ and adds it with the facts $C[a]$ to $W'$. \inmode{lf}{A ranked world also ranks the tree.} E-New at a field picks $x\cdot\kappa$ and keeps $W$. No order is lost\inmode{lf}{ and no rank changes}, so the worlds of a run form a chain.
O-New.grow.breaks: A world that lost a fact would not extend $W$, and the obligation reads its successor only at extensions.\inmode{lf}{ If a creation could change a rank, the measure of a waiting thread could rise.}
O-New.grow.example: At $\pi = \rho$ with $C = \{\rho \prec \overline{\rho\cdot 0},\ \overline{\rho} \prec \rho\cdot 0\}$ the world $W'$ adds the base $\rho$ and the facts $C$\inmode{lf}{, and a ranked $W'$ adds the ranks $\varrho(\rho) = 0$ and $\varrho(\rho\cdot 0) = 1$}.

args.name: W'
args.meaning: an extension of $W$\inmode{lf}{ that keeps each rank of $W$}

O-New.dual.title: Dual placement
O-New.dual.why: \inmode{lf}{It is the static result of E-New at the witness $\pi$, and duality of the pair is what the lock-free process relation asks of restricted channels.}

O-Spawn.title: O-Spawn
O-Spawn.meaning: $\Theta$ splits into a part $\Theta_M$ for the thunk, which is in $V^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Theta_M \vdash \ast \multimap^{\top}_{\bot} \ast\rrbracket$, and a rest $\Theta_r$ for the continuation.
O-Spawn.why: Exactness of $V$ fixes $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_M = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, so the split is the same at each level.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

args.name: \Theta_M, \Theta_r
args.meaning: the parts of the child and of the parent

O-Spawn.split.title: $\Theta = \Theta_M \uplus \Theta_r$
O-Spawn.split.meaning: The child and the parent own disjoint parts of $\Theta$.
O-Spawn.split.why: \inmode{lf}{The fundamental theorem builds the split from E-Spawn's split of the context, and the lock-free process relation moves exactly $\Theta_M$ to the new thread.}

O-Spawn.thunk.title: $v \in V^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Theta_M \vdash \ast \multimap^{\top}_{\bot} \ast\rrbracket$
O-Spawn.thunk.meaning: The thunk is a closure at upper point $\top$ and lower point $\bot$, in $V$ at the parent's index $\alpha$. At $u = \top$ its body is read at the empty future.
O-Spawn.thunk.why: For $\kappa_{\mathrm{spawn}} = 0$ the child is read inside the parent's least fixpoint, so an infinite chain of spawns is in no $E_\alpha$.

O-Send.title: O-Send
O-Send.meaning: The subject is at a send head, $\Theta \setminus o$ splits into the payload part $\Theta_M$ and the rest, the payload is in $V$, and the continuation runs at the rest with $o$ at $S_{x^{+}}$.
O-Send.example: $\mathsf{send}\,\langle a, y\rangle$ in the growing ring.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

args.name: S, S'
args.meaning: the session type of the subject and its continuation after the head

args.name: m, U, b
args.meaning: the number of point variables, the type\inmode{lf}{ and the credit} of the payload

O-Send.split.title: $\Theta \setminus o = \Theta_M \uplus \Theta_r$
O-Send.split.meaning: The payload owns no copy of the subject $o$.
O-Send.split.why: A send gives away held ends other than its subject.
O-Send.split.breaks: A term that sends its own subject would leave the continuation acting on an end it gave away.

sr.head.title: Head of an end $\Theta(o) \doteq H_x$
sr.head.meaning: $\Theta(o) \doteq H_x$ states $\Theta(o) = S_x$ for some $S$ with $\mathsf{unfold}\,S = H$.
sr.head.why: Each obligation reads the first action of the subject end after unfolding, so the notation states it once.

args.name: H
args.meaning: the head form of its protocol

O-Send.payload.title: Payload level
O-Send.payload.meaning: $w \in V_{\alpha}\llbracket\Theta_M \vdash U[x\cdot\bar\imath]\rrbracket$, \inmode{lf}{and $V_{\beta}$ for $\beta + \kappa_{\mathrm{give}} \leq \alpha$ and for $\beta = 0$ under a general table.}
O-Send.payload.why: The payload is read at the level of the continuation, because a send costs no level in the deadlock-free relation. \inmode{lf}{Under $\kappa_L$ it costs one.}
O-Send.payload.example: The payload $a$ of $\mathsf{send}\,\langle a, y\rangle$ at $Y\cdot 0$.

args.name: U[x\cdot\bar\imath]
args.meaning: the payload type with its point variables at the fields $x\cdot i$

O-Send.shift.title: $o : S_{x^{+}}$
O-Send.shift.meaning: The subject continues at $S$ and the next point $x^{+}$.
O-Send.shift.why: $x \prec x^{+}$ holds in each world, so successive actions on one end are ordered.

O-Recv.title: O-Recv
O-Recv.meaning: For each $\beta < \alpha$ and each incoming $w \in V_{\beta}$ with ends disjoint from $\Theta$, the continuation is in $E_{\beta}$ with those ends added.
O-Recv.why: The value that arrives is unknown when the receiver is typed, so it continues for each value its type admits, and the compatibility of E-Recv pairs this with the sender's O-Send.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

args.name: S, S'
args.meaning: the session type of the subject and its continuation after the head

O-Recv.forall.title: Each incoming value
O-Recv.forall.why: This negative occurrence of $V$ is at a lower level, so $V$ is well defined. \inmode{lf}{Under a general table the bound is $\beta + \kappa_{\mathrm{take}} \leq \alpha$, and $1 \leq \kappa_{\mathrm{take}}$ keeps $\beta < \alpha$.}

args.name: \beta
args.meaning: the level of the incoming value

O-Recv.level.title: Continuation at level $\beta$
O-Recv.level.why: The continuation owns the old ends with $o$ advanced and the received ends, and is read at the level of the value it received.

args.name: \beta
args.meaning: the level of the incoming value

O-Close.title: O-Close
O-Close.why: After the close nobody holds $o$, which matches the restriction removed by the process rule.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-Select.title: O-Select
O-Select.meaning: At a head $\oplus(S', S'')$, $e'$ at $\Theta[o \mapsto {S'}_{\overline{x\cdot\kappa_{\mathsf{false}}}}]$ for $i = \mathsf{false}$ and at $\Theta[o \mapsto {S''}_{\overline{x\cdot\kappa_{\mathsf{true}}}}]$ for $i = \mathsf{true}$.
O-Select.why: The selecting end keeps its name and moves to the dual side of the field of choice $i$, where E-Select places the end.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-Branch.title: O-Branch
O-Branch.meaning: For the choice $i$ the step took, $e'$ at $\Theta[o \mapsto {S'}_{x\cdot\kappa_{\mathsf{false}}}]$ or $\Theta[o \mapsto {S''}_{x\cdot\kappa_{\mathsf{true}}}]$, one level later.
O-Branch.why: The branching end moves to the field of choice $i$, the dual point of the selecting side.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-Link.title: O-Link
O-Link.meaning: Two distinct ends at $x$ and $\overline{x}$ with dual types leave $\Theta$.
O-Link.why: After the link $\overline{o_1}$ and $\overline{o_2}$ form one channel, which is well typed only if $o_1$ and $o_2$ were dual.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-Link.distinct.title: $o_1 \neq o_2$
O-Link.distinct.meaning: A link of an end with itself is rejected.
O-Link.distinct.why: The link label is a set and may be degenerate.

O-Link.dual.title: Dual at dual points
O-Link.dual.why: \inmode{lf}{E-Link types the two ends exactly dual at dual points, and the lock-free process relation keeps restricted pairs dual, which the renaming of the link preserves only under this condition.}

args.name: S, S'
args.meaning: the session types of the linked ends

rd.stable.title: $\mathsf{stable}\,t$
rd.stable.meaning: $\forall \alpha, t'.\ t \xrightarrow{\alpha} t' \Rightarrow \alpha \text{ is a session label}$.
rd.stable.why: Readiness constrains only terms that wait for another thread.

rd.offered.title: $\mathsf{offered}\,t$
rd.offered.meaning: The ends $o$ with $t \xrightarrow{\sigma} t'$ for some label $\sigma$ whose subject contains $o$. For a process, the same with $p$.
rd.offered.why: Each end has its own entry, so the offered ends are read off the labels.

deviations.reason: `offered_t`$\,\Theta\,t\,o$ also asks $o \in \mathrm{dom}\,\Theta$. The map writes it as $o \in \mathsf{offered}\,t$ and takes the restriction to $\Theta$ in $\Theta|_{\mathsf{offered}\,t}$ and $\Theta \setminus \mathsf{offered}\,t$.

rd.value.title: $\Theta|_{\mathsf{offered}\,t} = \varnothing \Rightarrow t \in \mathsf{Val}$
rd.value.meaning: A stable term that offers no end it holds is a value.
rd.value.why: A stable term offering only ends it does not hold would be stuck.

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{Val}$ is the set of terms that `is_val` accepts, and $\Theta|_{\mathsf{offered}\,t} = \varnothing$ stands for $\forall o.\ \neg$`offered_t`$\,\Theta\,t\,o$.

rd.link.title: $\mathsf{link}\,t$
rd.link.meaning: $\exists os, t'.\ t \xrightarrow{\leftrightarrow os} t'$, and a term at a link is ready.
rd.link.why: A link step at process level needs no other thread, so a link never waits and readiness need not order the link.
rd.link.breaks: Asking the order of a link would reject each link next to an end held at an unrelated point, and E-Link has no order premise.

args.name: os
args.meaning: the linked ends of the step

rd.below-rest.title: $\mathsf{below\_rest}$
rd.below-rest.meaning: $\Theta|_{\mathsf{offered}\,t} \prec_W \overline{\Theta \setminus \mathsf{offered}\,t} \cup F$. Each offered end lies below the dual point of each end kept but not offered and below each point of $F$.
rd.below-rest.why: It excludes circular waiting, because a waiting thread's offer is minimal among what it holds and what its context still does.
rd.below-rest.breaks: Client and server each blocked on their second channel while holding the first, under a cyclic order.
rd.below-rest.example: Closing $c$ at $\rho$ while $d$ is held at $\rho\cdot 0$ needs $\rho \prec \overline{\rho\cdot 0}$.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

deviations.reason: $\Theta|_{\mathsf{offered}\,t} \prec_W \overline{\Theta \setminus \mathsf{offered}\,t} \cup F$ writes `below_rest` with sets of points in place of its two quantified clauses.

rd.below-held.title: $\overline{\Theta \setminus \mathsf{offered}\,t}$
rd.below-held.meaning: The dual points of the ends held but not offered.
rd.below-held.why: The dual end of a held end acts at $\overline{x'}$, so the offered end is served before anyone waits on the held ends.

args.name: x
args.meaning: the point of an offered end

args.name: o', x'
args.meaning: a held end that is not offered and its point

rd.below-future.title: The future $F$
rd.below-future.meaning: The points at which the context acts after the term returns. Each offered end lies below each point of $F$.
rd.below-future.why: The context acts at the points of $F$ after the term returns.
rd.below-future.example: $\kappa \prec y$ for each $y$ above the upper point in $\mathsf{between}$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: the point of an offered end

rd.p-stable.title: $\mathsf{stable}\,p$
rd.p-stable.why: A process with an internal step is not waiting, and readiness speaks only of waiting processes.

rd.p-term.title: $\Sigma|_{\mathsf{offered}\,p} = \varnothing \Rightarrow \mathsf{terminated}\,p$
rd.p-term.meaning: A stable process that offers no interface end has terminated.
rd.p-term.why: A stable process that offers nothing to its environment must be finished, which is the deadlock-freedom statement at the process level.
rd.p-term.breaks: Without it, a stable process blocked on internal ends would satisfy P-Ready.

deviations.reason: $\Sigma|_{\mathsf{offered}\,p} = \varnothing$ stands for $\forall o.\ \neg$`offered_p`$\,\Sigma\,p\,o$.

rd.above-offered.title: $\mathsf{above\_offered}$
rd.above-offered.meaning: $\forall y \in \overline{\Sigma \setminus \mathsf{offered}\,p}.\ \exists x \in \Sigma|_{\mathsf{offered}\,p}.\ W \vdash x \prec y$. Each interface end kept but not offered has an offered end below its dual point.
rd.above-offered.why: The environment can always serve some offered end first, so composing two ready processes over one world keeps one of them able to move.

args.name: o, x
args.meaning: an interface end that is not offered and its point

args.name: o', x'
args.meaning: an offered end and its point

deviations.reason: The map quantifies over the dual points $\overline{\Sigma \setminus \mathsf{offered}\,p}$ and the points $\Sigma|_{\mathsf{offered}\,p}$, where `above_offered` quantifies over the ends.

P.strict.title: Later worlds
P.strict.meaning: Each unfolding of $P$ holds in each world $W' \sqsupseteq W$.
P.strict.why: Composition places a process into a larger world. \inmode{lf}{A ranked world has no cycle, so no strictness premise remains.}

P.clauses.title: $\mathsf{clauses}_{W'}(\Sigma', p')$
P.clauses.meaning: The stop, ready and step clauses of $p'$ at the interface $\Sigma'$ in the world $W'$.
P.clauses.why: $P$ asks them after each fusion, and a term asks the same three of itself.
P.clauses.example: A finished process $(\varnothing, \{v\})$ meets them when $v \in V$.

P.fuse.title: Closed under fusions
P.fuse.meaning: Each unfolding holds at $(h, D)\cdot\Sigma$ and $(h, D)\cdot p$ for each $(h, D) \in \mathsf{Fus}(\Sigma, p)$.
P.fuse.why: Renaming, internalizing a pair of interface ends and the renaming done by a link are fusions, and closure by definition makes each of them a projection.
P.fuse.breaks: With renamings alone, a link could join two unrelated interface ends into one channel and composition would fail.

P-Stop.title: P-Stop
P-Stop.meaning: $\mathsf{pirred}\,p' \Rightarrow \exists v, E.\ p' = (\varnothing, \{v\} \uplus E) \land v \in V\llbracket\Sigma' \vdash T\rrbracket \land \forall e \in E.\ e = \ast$.
P-Stop.why: An irreducible process in $P$ has no restricted channel left, its main thread returned a value in $V$ and each other thread returned $\ast$, which is the definition of terminated.
P-Stop.breaks: Without it, a process stuck with restricted channels would be in $P$, and adequacy would fail.

deviations.reason: $(\mathsf{stop})$ labels the first clause of `Pclauses`.

P-Ready.title: P-Ready
P-Ready.why: Readiness of processes excludes circular waiting across the interface.

deviations.reason: $(\mathsf{ready})$ labels the second clause of `Pclauses`, and $\mathsf{pirred}$ is the Rocq predicate `pirred`.

P-Step.title: P-Step
P-Step.meaning: Each step $p' \xrightarrow{ev} p''$ meets $\mathsf{Pobl}_{ev}$. A process steps when some numbering of its threads steps, $p \xrightarrow{ev} p' \iff \exists q, q'.\ \mathsf{erase}\,q = p \land q \xrightarrow{ev} q' \land \mathsf{erase}\,q' = p'$.
P-Step.why: The obligations read the event and the result, and no thread number. \inmode{lf}{Thread numbers matter only to the lock-free process relation, which records the thread holding each end.}
P-Step.example: A message between two threads meets Q-Tau.

deviations.reason: $(\mathsf{step})$ labels the clause that `Psteps` states.

fuse.dcomm.title: $h$ commutes with duality
fuse.dcomm.why: Restricted channels and the dual ends added by Q-Send and Q-Recv enter $P$ as pairs, which $h$ must map to pairs.

fuse.inj.title: Injective on held ends
fuse.inj.meaning: $\forall o_1, o_2 \in \mathsf{held}.\ h(o_1) = h(o_2) \Rightarrow o_1 = o_2$.
fuse.inj.why: $\mathsf{csub}$ of a link identifies $\overline{o_1}$ and $o_2$, so $h$ is no bijection, but it is injective on the held ends of the other component.
fuse.inj.example: $\mathsf{csub}$ is injective on the other side's held ends.
fuse.inj.signature: \forall o_1, o_2 \in \mathsf{held}.\ h(o_1) = h(o_2) \Rightarrow o_1 = o_2

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{held}$ is the set of ends that `pheld` accepts in `fuse_ok`.

fuse.partners.title: New dual pairs only on $D$
fuse.partners.why: Two held ends become the two ends of one channel only if they were or their channel is restricted by the fusion.
fuse.partners.breaks: Without it, $h$ joins unrelated interface ends into one channel, and composition fails.

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{held}$ is the set of ends that `pheld` accepts in `fuse_ok`.

fuse.D.title: $D \cap \mathsf{gch}_h[C] = \varnothing$
fuse.D.meaning: The channels restricted by the fusion are not images of channels already restricted.
fuse.D.why: Composition splits a fused process into its two sides, and this condition keeps the two restricted sets $\mathsf{gch}_h[C_i] \cup D_i$ disjoint from each other and from the interface.
fuse.D.breaks: Without it, a restricted channel could be restricted again as a new pair, and the split of the fused composite fails.

fuse.dpairs.title: $\mathsf{dpairs}\,D\,\Sigma$
fuse.dpairs.meaning: Both ends of each channel of $D$ are in $\Sigma$, at dual points and dual types.
fuse.dpairs.why: They become restricted, and restricted channels are dual pairs.

Q-Tau.title: Q-Tau
Q-Tau.meaning: An internal step that restricts no interface channel keeps $\Sigma$, costs the levels of its kind of step and continues in some world $W' \sqsupseteq W$.
Q-Tau.why: Administrative steps and internal synchronizations are one clause. A creation among them may grow the world.
Q-Tau.example: A message between two threads costs one level\inmode{lf}{, and $\kappa_{\mathrm{give}} + \kappa_{\mathrm{take}}$ under a general table}.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: the process before and after the step, $p = (C, E)$ and $p' = (C', E')$

Q-Send.title: Q-Send
Q-Send.meaning: An external send. The interface part $\Sigma_v$ and the restricted part $\Theta_e$ of the payload leave, and the dual ends $\Sigma_e$ left behind join the interface.
Q-Send.why: It is O-Send at the process level, and the compatibility of P-Term discharges it from O-Send of the thread.
Q-Send.example: Sending a restricted end $d^{+}$ puts $d^{-}$ into the interface.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: the process before and after the step, $p = (C, E)$ and $p' = (C', E')$

args.name: \Sigma_v, \Sigma_r
args.meaning: the interface ends of the payload and the rest

args.name: \Theta_e, \Sigma_e
args.meaning: the restricted ends that leave and their dual ends that stay

Q-Send.theta-e.title: Extruded ends $\Theta_e$
Q-Send.theta-e.why: $\Theta_e$ is exactly the restricted part of the ends of $w$. Exactness of $V$ at the payload gives $\mathsf{fends}(w) = \mathrm{dom}\,\Sigma_v \cup \mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_e$, so the payload has $\mathsf{fends}(w)$ and nothing else.

args.name: \Theta_e
args.meaning: the restricted ends of the payload

args.name: \Sigma_v
args.meaning: the interface ends of the payload

Q-Send.split.title: $\mathsf{send\_split}$
Q-Send.split.meaning: The extruded ends are no interface ends, and $\Sigma_e$ holds the dual ends of extruded ends that stay, at dual types and points.
Q-Send.split.why: The dual end of an extruded end becomes an interface end, and the interface must record its type and point.
Q-Send.split.breaks: Without it, the process would keep an end its interface does not mention, and P-Stop could not hold.

args.name: \Sigma_e
args.meaning: the dual ends that join the interface

Q-Send.sigma-e.title: $\Sigma_e$ joins the interface
Q-Send.sigma-e.meaning: The dual ends of extruded ends become interface ends.

args.name: \Sigma_e
args.meaning: the dual ends of extruded ends

Q-Recv.title: Q-Recv
Q-Recv.meaning: For each incoming environment and value, the process continues with the received ends added and the channels both of whose ends it now holds restricted.
Q-Recv.why: It is O-Recv at the process level, and composition feeds one component's Q-Send into the other's Q-Recv.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: the process before and after the step, $p = (C, E)$ and $p' = (C', E')$

Q-Recv.ok.title: $\mathsf{recv\_ok}$
Q-Recv.ok.meaning: Incoming ends are new to $\Sigma$, and each incoming end whose dual end is held or received is at the dual point with the dual type.
Q-Recv.ok.why: Composition delivers one component's payload only under this condition, and it is what makes a newly restricted pair dual.
Q-Recv.ok.breaks: Without the duality conjunct, receiving the dual end of a held end at a mismatched type would restrict an ill-typed channel.

Q-Recv.back.title: $\mathsf{recv\_back}$
Q-Recv.back.meaning: The channels of incoming ends whose dual end is held or received along.
Q-Recv.back.why: Both ends of such a channel are now in the process, so it is restricted, as the interface holds no two dual ends.

Q-Recv.env.title: $\mathsf{recv\_env}$
Q-Recv.env.meaning: The interface after the receive, without the ends that became internal.
Q-Recv.env.why: Internal ends leave the interface, and the rest of $\Theta_2$ joins the interface.

Q-Link.title: Q-Close, Q-Select, Q-Branch, Q-Link
Q-Link.meaning: The term obligations O-Close, O-Select, O-Branch and O-Link with $\Sigma$ for $\Theta$ and $P$ for $E$.
Q-Link.why: An external close, choice or link acts on interface ends exactly as a thread acts on its own ends.
Q-Link.example: Q-Link removes both linked ends from $\Sigma$.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: the process before and after the step, $p = (C, E)$ and $p' = (C', E')$

deviations.reason: Q-Close, Q-Select, Q-Branch and Q-Link are the clauses `q_close`, `q_select`, `q_branch` and `q_link`, shown as the term obligations they repeat.

sj.at.title: Judgment at a set of points $X$
sj.at.meaning: For each level, later world, environment $\Theta'$ disjoint from the ends $|\Delta|$ and grounding $\gamma$ of the variables of $\Delta$ in $\Theta'$, $\gamma(e) \in E_\alpha\llbracket|\Delta| \cup \Theta' \vdash T\rrbracket^{X}$, over each ordinal index $\alpha$.
sj.at.why: It quantifies over everything a context may supply, so it composes by the compatibility lemmas.

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the linear context of the typing judgment, its ends erased to $|\Delta|$

args.name: X
args.meaning: a set of points read as the future

args.name: \alpha, W', \Theta', \gamma
args.meaning: each ordinal index, extension, environment of the grounding and grounding

sj.grel.title: Grounding $\gamma \in G\llbracket\Theta \vdash \Delta\rrbracket$
sj.grel.meaning: $\gamma$ substitutes for each entry $T^a$ of $\Delta$ a value in $V\llbracket\Theta_i \vdash T\rrbracket$, with $\Theta = \biguplus_i \Theta_i$.
sj.grel.why: Variables of $\Delta$ stand for values, and the ends of those values split $\Theta$ disjointly.

args.name: \gamma
args.meaning: a substitution $\mathbb{N} \to \mathsf{Expr}$ for the variables of $\Delta$

sj.den.title: $\mathsf{den}_{Y}(F)$
sj.den.meaning: $\mathsf{den}_{Y}(X \cup {\vartriangle}v) = (X \cap \mathsf{Point}) \cup Y$ for a finite set $Y$ of points with $v \prec y$ for each $y \in Y$. For $v = \top$ the set $Y$ is empty, and for $v = \bot$ it is an arbitrary finite set. For $\bot \in X$ the set $Y$ is an arbitrary finite set as well. The bounds $\bot$ and $\top$ in $X$ denote no point.
sj.den.why: The rest stands for an unknown set of points, so the judgment holds at each choice of this set.

deviations.reason: `sf_den Y F` adds $Y$ when $F$ has a rest, and `rest_ok` asks each point of $Y$ above $u$ for the rest `RAbove u`. With no rest the Rocq still quantifies over $Y$ and adds nothing, which the map writes as $Y = \varnothing$. The Rocq future has no bounds in its set. A future with $\bot \in X$ is the Rocq future with the rest `RAll`, for which `rest_ok` asks nothing of $Y$, as [[t-contexts]] states.

sj.term.title: $\Delta \vDash^{F}_W e : T$
sj.term.meaning: $\forall Y.\ \Delta \vDash^{\mathsf{den}_{Y}(F)}_W e : T$, with the same context $\Delta$ as the typing judgment.
sj.term.why: It is the conclusion of the fundamental theorem for terms. \inmode{lf}{The judgment at $\kappa_L$, written $\vDash[\kappa_L]$, reads the relation at the table $\kappa_L$.}

deviations.reason: The Rocq writes the judgment at $\kappa_L$ with a turnstile of its own, `⊫`, for `sem_typed κ_L` and `sem_ptyped κ_L`. The map writes $\vDash[\kappa_L]$, the instance of the family $\vDash[\kappa]$ at $\kappa_L$, so that one symbol serves each cost table.

sj.proc.title: The process relation at each index
sj.proc.meaning: $\forall \alpha.\ p \in P^W_\alpha\llbracket\Sigma \vdash T\rrbracket$ at a consistent world $W$, over each ordinal index $\alpha$.
sj.proc.why: Adequacy turns it into deadlock freedom. \inmode{lf}{With $\kappa_L$ it also gives absence of divergence by free steps.}

deviations.reason: The Rocq calls it `sem_ptyped`, with the notation $\Sigma \vDash_W p : T$. The map writes the quantifier out and keeps $\Sigma \vDash_W p : T$ for the judgment at each consistent extension of [[sj-all]].

fu.rty.title: Result $\sigma$
fu.rty.meaning: $\sigma$ is a credited type $T^a$ of the returned value, or $\mathsf{thread}$, whose value holds no end.
fu.rty.why: A spawned thread returns $\ast$ and keeps no end, which $\mathsf{thread}$ states without a type.
fu.rty.example: $\mathsf{thread}$ for a lock-free process relation thread.

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{thread}$ is the constructor `RThread` of `rty`.

fu.frame.title: Frame $d$
fu.frame.meaning: $d \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ bounds the channel actions the term performs before it returns.
