fu.frame.why: Each action asks $1 \leq d$ and lowers $d$ by one, so the frame bounds how often the context decrements its own ends during the term.

fu.Phi.title: Held ends $\Phi$
fu.Phi.meaning: $\Phi$ maps each end the thread holds to its protocol $S$, a session type with annotations, its counter $f$ and its tickets $m \geq f$, written $o \mapsto S^{f,m}$.
fu.Phi.why: The counter bounds how many actions of the thread holding it may pass before the end acts again, and an action sets it back to $m$. The protocol says when the end is idle and what it sends and receives. Where the relation gives an end a point, fuel gives it a counter and tickets.

args.name: S^{f,m}
args.meaning: the protocol $S$, counter $f$ and tickets $m$ of an end, $f \leq m$

deviations.reason: The Rocq keeps the protocols in a map `penv` and the counters and tickets in a map `cenv`, and the formula shows both in one map $\Phi$ from $\mathsf{End}$ to $\mathsf{STy} \times \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$.

fu.tick.title: $\Phi{\downarrow}$
fu.tick.meaning: Each counter of $\Phi$ lowered by one, truncated at $0$, with the tickets kept.
fu.tick.why: An action decrements the counters of the other ends of the thread holding it, and a send passes the counters of its payload on one lower. Both use this operation.
fu.tick.example: $\{a \mapsto S^{3,3}, b \mapsto S'^{1,2}\}{\downarrow} = \{a \mapsto S^{2,3}, b \mapsto S'^{0,2}\}$.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f,m}$ from ends to a protocol, a counter $f$ and tickets $m \geq f$

fu.rename.title: Injective renamings
fu.rename.meaning: Fuel holds for each renaming $g$ of ends injective on $\mathrm{dom}\,\Phi$.
fu.rename.why: A link renames the dual end of a removed end in another thread, so fuel must remain renaming.
fu.rename.breaks: A renaming that merges two held ends would merge their counters.

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{injective}(g|_{\mathrm{dom}\,\Phi})$ is `kinj g φ`, and `renk` renames the map.

fu.val.title: (val)
fu.val.why: A returning term gives its context a value whose counters meet its credits, which the bind lemma of fuel consumes.

deviations.reason: $(\mathsf{stop})$ labels the value clause of `Fdef`, and $\mathsf{Val}$ is the set of terms that `is_val` accepts.

fu.step.title: (step)
fu.step.meaning: $\forall \ell, e'.\ g(e) \xrightarrow{\ell} e' \Rightarrow \mathsf{Fobl}\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_\ell(e')$ at each ordinal $\beta < \alpha$.
fu.step.why: Each step updates the state by one index-free rule, which the lock-free process relation follows along a run. At a limit $\alpha$ the obligation holds at each smaller index.

args.name: \ell, e'
args.meaning: the step label and the successor

deviations.reason: $(\mathsf{step})$ labels the step clause of `Fdef`, stated through `Fobl`.

F-Wait.title: F-Wait
F-Wait.meaning: $\Phi(o) = S^{f}$ with $S$ not idle, so the end is held and can act.
F-Wait.why: An idle end is exempt from the checks $\geq 1$, so it must not act either.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f,m}$ from ends to a protocol, a counter $f$ and tickets $m \geq f$

F-Tick.title: F-Count
F-Tick.meaning: $\mathsf{positive}(\Phi \setminus o)$, each other end that is not idle has counter at least $1$.
F-Tick.why: Each action decrements the counters of the other ends, so an end can wait only as many actions of the thread holding it as its counter allows.
F-Tick.breaks: A thread that holds an end and loops on other ends forever while the thread holding the dual end waits.
F-Tick.example: At $\Phi = \{a \mapsto S^{2}, b \mapsto S'\inmode{lf}{^{0}}\}$ no action on $a$ is allowed unless $b$ is idle.

args.name: \Phi

F-Tick.frame.title: $1 \leq d$
F-Tick.frame.meaning: The frame has a unit for the action.
F-Tick.frame.why: The frame bounds the decrements of the context's ends during the term.

fu.idle.title: $\mathsf{idle}$
fu.idle.why: Idleness removes the checks $\geq 1$ and never changes how a counter evolves, so counters stay index-free. The typing ages idle ends by truncation at $0$, matching counters that decrement down to $0$.
fu.idle.breaks: An idle end whose credit stayed fixed while its counter decrements would exceed its counter.

F-Beta.title: F-Beta
F-Beta.why: A $\beta$ step changes no counter and costs one index.

F-New.why: A new channel starts each end at its tickets, the credit E-New gives to the new ends.

args.meaning: the tickets of the two ends

F-New.fresh.title: Fresh against the thread
F-New.fresh.why: Without it, a new channel could reuse a held name and overwrite its counter.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f,m}$ from ends to a protocol, a counter $f$ and tickets $m \geq f$

F-New.cnew.title: New ends at their tickets
F-New.cnew.why: An action sets the counter of an end back to its tickets, and a new end starts there too.

args.name: m_1, m_2
args.meaning: the tickets of the new ends, $m_1 + m_2 \leq N$

F-Spawn.title: F-Spawn
F-Spawn.meaning: The child takes $\Phi|_M$ for $M = \mathsf{fends}(v)$ and runs as a thread, the parent keeps $\Phi \setminus M$.
F-Spawn.why: The split is a function of $v$, so it is the same at each index. A spawn is no action, so no counter falls. The call clause of [[fv|FV-Arrow]] accepts the current counters at each credit, which makes F-Spawn hold for each closure value.
F-Spawn.example: The thunk takes $d'$ at $1$ in the cycle.

F-Spawn.held.title: $M \subseteq \mathrm{dom}\,\Phi$
F-Spawn.held.why: A child mentioning an end the parent does not hold would act on an end without a counter.
F-Spawn.held.breaks: A box mentioning channel constants would pass on ends nobody holds.

fu.fspare.title: $\mathsf{positive}$
fu.fspare.meaning: $\mathsf{positive}(\Phi) \iff$ each end of $\Phi$ that is not idle has counter at least $1$.
fu.fspare.why: An action decrements the other counters and a send passes the counters of its payload on minus one, so a non-idle end must have a positive counter. A spawn lowers no counter and asks nothing.
fu.fspare.breaks: A transfer at counter $0$ under truncation passes $0$ again and an end is passed on forever.

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{positive}$ is the Rocq predicate `fspare`, and $\mathsf{idle}$ is `idle_at`.

F-Spawn.child.title: The child
F-Spawn.child.why: The child is a new thread of the lock-free process relation, so it must have thread fuel at exactly the ends and counters the lock-free process relation moves to the child.

F-Send.title: F-Send
F-Send.meaning: An action on $o$ that passes on $M = \mathsf{fends}(w)$ one lower, the payload in $FV$, and the continuation with $o$ back at its tickets $m$.
F-Send.why: A send is an action, so F-Count applies, and a transfer, so $\mathsf{positive}$ applies.
F-Send.example: $\mathsf{send}\,\langle a, y\rangle$ in the growing ring.

F-Send.notsubj.title: $o \notin M \subseteq \mathrm{dom}\,\Phi$
F-Send.notsubj.meaning: A send gives away held ends other than its subject.
F-Send.notsubj.why: The continuation keeps acting on $o$, so $o$ cannot leave.
F-Send.notsubj.breaks: A term that sends its own subject or an end its context holds.

F-Send.payload.title: Payload in $FV$
F-Send.payload.meaning: $w \in FV^N_{\alpha}\llbracket\Phi|_M{\downarrow} \vdash T\rrbracket$, with each transferred counter lowered by one transfer.
F-Send.payload.why: $FV$ reads no point, so the raw payload type and its placed form agree.
F-Send.payload.example: $FV^N_{\alpha}\llbracket \{a \mapsto S^{2}\} \vdash S_x^{2}\rrbracket$ for a payload end promised at credit $2$.

F-Recv.title: F-Recv
F-Recv.meaning: An action on $o$ that continues for each incoming value in $FV$ at each index $\gamma \leq \beta$ with ends disjoint from $\Phi$.
F-Recv.why: The receiver continues for each value its type admits, and the lock-free process relation supplies the sender's transferred ends.

args.name: \beta, \Phi_i
args.meaning: its level and the ends it brings

F-Recv.forall.title: Each incoming value
F-Recv.forall.why: Each value in $FV$ is exact, so incoming closures hold exactly what they mention.
F-Recv.forall.breaks: Without exactness, a received closure owning nothing but mentioning an end could not be spawned.

args.name: \Phi_i
args.meaning: the ends of the received value, disjoint from $\Phi$

F-Close.title: F-Close, F-Select, F-Branch
F-Close.meaning: Actions that drop $o$ and decrement the rest at a close, or advance the protocol of $o$ to the chosen continuation and set it back to its tickets $m$ at a choice.
F-Close.why: They are the fuel forms of O-Close, O-Select and O-Branch, and each is an action, so F-Count applies.

args.name: i
args.meaning: the choice, for select and branch

F-Link.title: F-Link
F-Link.meaning: Two distinct held ends at dual protocols leave, and the counter of each exceeds $N - m$ for the tickets $m$ of the other.
F-Link.why: The link lowers no counter. Its premise gives the dual end a waiting thread faces after the link a lower counter than before.
F-Link.example: $\mathsf{link}\,\langle c^{+}, d^{-}\rangle$ with counters $3$ and $3$ and tickets $3$ and $3$ at $N = 4$.

F-Link.plink.title: Dual held ends
F-Link.plink.meaning: $o_1 \neq o_2$, both held, at protocols $S$ and $S'$ with $S \sqsubseteq \overline{S'}$.
F-Link.plink.why: After the link the two dual ends form one channel. What the thread holding $\overline{o_1}$ sends at some credit, the thread holding $\overline{o_2}$ receives at a credit no higher. The protocols of the two dual ends lie below and above $S$ and $\overline{S'}$ by $\sqsubseteq$.
F-Link.plink.breaks: With $S'$ and $\overline{S}$ unrelated a thread receives a payload at a credit that its sender never guaranteed.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f,m}$ from ends to a protocol, a counter $f$ and tickets $m \geq f$

F-Link.ticket.title: $f_1 + m_2 > N$ and $f_2 + m_1 > N$
F-Link.ticket.meaning: The counter of each linked end exceeds $N - m$ for the tickets $m$ of the other linked end.
F-Link.ticket.why: The dual end $\overline{o_2}$ has at most $N - m_2$ tickets, so its counter is below $f_1$. The thread waiting on $\overline{o_1}$ then faces a lower counter after the link, and the measure of lock-free adequacy falls.
F-Link.ticket.breaks: Without it a link can give a waiting thread a new dual end with a full counter in each round.
F-Link.ticket.signature: f_1 + m_2 > N \land f_2 + m_1 > N

args.name: f_1, f_2
args.meaning: the counters of the linked ends

args.name: N
args.meaning: the bound on the tickets of a channel, $N \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

FV-Sess.title: $FV$ at $S_x$
FV-Sess.meaning: An end with protocol $S' \sqsubseteq S$, counter $f \geq a$ and the tickets $m$ of its type.
FV-Sess.why: Credits are lower bounds on counters, and the tickets of the type are those fuel resets the counter to. The protocol held at run time lies below the type by $\sqsubseteq$, so Sub-Sess keeps a value in $FV$.

args.name: S_x, a, m
args.meaning: the end type, its credit and its tickets

FV-Sess.counter.title: $a \leq f$
FV-Sess.counter.why: Typing reasons with credits and the lock-free process relation with counters, and this inequality transfers each credit bound of typing to the counters.
FV-Sess.counter.breaks: Without it, a context could age an end below its actual counter and F-Count would fail on an end whose credit typing treats as positive.

FV-Arrow.title: $FV$ at an arrow
FV-Arrow.meaning: A closure whose body has fuel at each lower level, counters at or above the counters at creation minus its credit and argument in $FV$.
FV-Arrow.why: The clause reads costs and credits, the data typing attaches to arrows.

args.name: c, h
args.meaning: the cost and floor of the arrow

FV-Arrow.exact.title: $\mathsf{fends}\,e = \mathrm{dom}\,\Phi$
FV-Arrow.exact.meaning: The closure holds exactly the ends it mentions.
FV-Arrow.exact.why: It mirrors exactness of $V$, and the cost fundamental theorem needs it to read fuel off typing.
FV-Arrow.exact.breaks: A closure mentioning an end it does not hold would be in $FV$, and a forwarder receiving that closure could not spawn the closure.

FV-Arrow.floor.title: Counters $\geq a$
FV-Arrow.floor.meaning: Each captured counter $f$ of an end that is not idle has $a \leq f$.
FV-Arrow.floor.why: The closure's credit $a$ is a lower bound on each captured counter, as the credit of an end is on its own counter.

FV-Arrow.body.title: Body fuel
FV-Arrow.body.why: The caller supplies an argument and counters lowered by at most $a$ by its own actions, and the body guarantees fuel with frame $c$.
FV-Arrow.body.example: A call of a closure of cost $1$.

args.name: c

FV-Box.title: $FV$ at a box
FV-Box.meaning: A box with no ends whose body has fuel per force at each lower level and session instance in $\mathsf{sinsts}\,N$.
FV-Box.why: A box is unlimited, so it holds no counters and works at each use.

FV-Box.noends.title: $\mathsf{fends}\,e = \varnothing$
FV-Box.noends.meaning: A box mentions no end and holds no protocol or counter.
FV-Box.noends.why: A copied box would otherwise copy ends.

FV-Box.body.title: Body per force
FV-Box.body.meaning: $e[!e] \in F^{N}_{\beta}\llbracket\varnothing \vdash U[\bar s]\ !\ c\rrbracket$ for each $\beta < \alpha$ and $\bar s \in \mathsf{sinsts}\,N$.
FV-Box.body.why: Each force unrolls the box once, at an instance the forcing context chooses.

args.name: c

FV-Thread.title: Thread result
FV-Thread.why: A finished thread holds no end.

fu.fsem.title: $\mathsf{fsem}$

sp.world.title: $W \sqsubseteq W_a$
sp.world.meaning: The ranked world $W_a$ of the configuration extends the ranked world $W$ the relation is read at.
sp.world.why: A configuration may start at an extension of $W$, and a creation grows $W_a$ along a run. Composition reads the second component at the ranked world the first one starts at, so the fresh bases of the two never collide.
sp.world.breaks: Asking $W_a = W$ would make each component start at the world of the composite, which only a common ranked world of both sides provides.
sp.world.example: $W_a = W \oplus (a, \varrho_a)$ after one creation at the fresh base $a$.

args.name: W

args.name: W_a

sp.allR.title: $\forall W' \sqsupseteq W$
sp.allR.meaning: The judgment holds at each ranked extension $W'$ of the world $W$.
sp.allR.why: Each component of P-Connect is read at the ranked extensions of its own world. A ranked extension of the join extends both worlds, so both components hold there, and only the shared constants are compared, through $\mathsf{wf}\,(W_1|_S \sqcup W_2|_S)$, which makes such a ranked world exist.
sp.allR.breaks: At one fixed ranked world per component composition fails. A ranked world orders two ranked points whenever their ranks differ, so a ranked $W_1' \sqsupseteq W_1$ may put $y \prec \overline{x}$ and a ranked $W_2' \sqsupseteq W_2$ put $\overline{x} \prec y$ for shared points that no fact relates. A thread holding an end at $x$ and waiting at $y$ is ready in $W_1'$, the other thread holding an end at $\overline{y}$ and waiting at $\overline{x}$ is ready in $W_2'$, and the two deadlock.
sp.allR.example: The client at $W_{cli}$ and the server at $W_{srv}$, which share the base $\rho$.

deviations.reason: `lf_sems` quantifies over the ranked Rocq worlds of type `world` that `wmodels` relates to $W$, which the map writes as ranked extensions.

sp.dom.meaning: $A$, $\Phi$ and $K$ describe the same held ends.
sp.dom.why: Lock-free adequacy reads the protocol of an end of $K$, and of its dual end, to decide idleness, and a synchronization updates $\Phi$ and $K$ together.
sp.dom.breaks: Without it, a held end could lack a protocol, and idleness of a waiting end would be undefined.

sp.owner.why: A thread waiting on an end needs the thread holding the dual end to be a thread of $q$, so the dependency of waiting threads is a relation on threads.
sp.owner.breaks: Without it, an end could be held by a thread that no longer exists, and the thread holding its dual end would wait forever.

sp.closed.title: Held ends restricted or interface
sp.closed.why: For $\Sigma = \varnothing$ each held end is restricted, so the lock-free process relation holds both ends of each channel it acts on. Composition splits held ends along this condition.
sp.closed.breaks: Without it, a closed process could hold an end whose dual end nobody holds, and the thread holding it would wait forever.

sp.pair.title: Dual ends of restricted channels held
sp.pair.why: The dual end of an internal end is held by some thread.
sp.pair.example: Both ends of $c$ in the pair of closes.

sp.sdual.title: Restricted pairs dual
sp.sdual.why: The two ends of an internal channel are at dual points with dual session types.

sp.pdual.title: Restricted protocols dual up to subtyping
sp.pdual.meaning: $\mathsf{ech}\,o \in C$, $\Phi(o) = P^{f}$ and $\Phi(\overline{o}) = P'^{f'}$ imply $\overline{P} \sqsubseteq P'$.
sp.pdual.why: Lock-free adequacy reads idleness from $\Phi$, and $\sqsubseteq$ and duality transfer idleness from an end to its dual end. What one end sends at some credit, the other end receives at a credit no higher.

args.name: P, P'

sp.sig.title: Interface entries in $A$
sp.sig.why: Restricting a cut makes its channels internal, and their dual entries in $A$ come from $\Sigma$ through this condition.
sp.sig.breaks: Without it, a channel restricted at composition could have non-dual entries in $A$.

sp.psig.title: Interface protocols in $\Phi$
sp.psig.meaning: $\Sigma(o) = S_x$ implies $\Phi(o) = S^{f}$ for some counter $f$.
sp.psig.why: At composition the protocols of the cut come from $\Sigma$, which typing makes dual.

sp.fin.title: Finite counters
sp.fin.why: The termination measure reads each counter as a natural number.

sp.lfsem.title: $\Sigma \Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_W p : T$
sp.lfsem.meaning: $\forall W' \sqsupseteq W.\ \mathsf{ranked}\,W' \Rightarrow \forall \alpha.\ \exists a.\ \mathsf{erase}(q_a) = p \land a \in S^{N,W'}_\alpha\llbracket\Sigma \vdash T\rrbracket$, at each ranked extension $W'$ of the world $W$ and each ordinal index $\alpha$.
sp.lfsem.why: The lock-free process relation alone suffices, and absence of divergence by free steps of the lock-free process relation gives what a process conjunct would.
sp.lfsem.example: The lock-free fundamental theorem concludes this judgment.

The map writes it out and keeps $\Sigma \Vvdash^{N}_W p : T$ for `lf_sems`, the judgment at each ranked extension. `lf_sems` reads `lf_semk`, the judgment at the annotations $\eta$ of the interface. The map leaves $\eta$ implicit here and in the theorem rows, because it is fixed with the interface.

sp.exists-before-forall.title: $\forall \alpha$ before $\exists a$
sp.exists-before-forall.meaning: The bound $N$ is a parameter of the judgment, and the annotated configuration $a$ is an ordinary existential at each ordinal index $\alpha$. The creation of a channel chooses its position, facts and tickets inside O-New.
sp.exists-before-forall.why: The relation holds at each ordinal of a universe above the space of creation choices. The existential property, proved from excluded middle and choice, turns $\forall \alpha.\ \exists a$ into $\exists a.\ \forall \alpha$, so along a run each choice holds at each index.
sp.exists-before-forall.breaks: At the finite indices alone the existential property fails for an infinite space of choices, the example $\exists n.\ \triangleright^{n}\bot$ of transfinite step indexing.

sp.next.title: $\mathsf{lf\_next}$
sp.next.meaning: $\mathsf{lf\_next}\,N\,(q, K)\,ev\,(q', K')$ holds when $K'$ is one of the ownership maps $\mathsf{own\_next}\,N\,ev\,K$ allows.
sp.next.why: A creation places the new ends at a position, with facts and with tickets of sum at most $N$, each counter at its tickets. An action moves its end to the next point and resets its counter to its tickets. A transfer moves the ends to the receiving thread and decrements their counters. A link renames. None of these depends on the index, and the choices of a creation come from O-New and F-New.
sp.next.example: One step of the lock-free process relation along an event.

sp.cap.title: $f \leq m$
sp.cap.meaning: Each counter recorded in $K$ is at most the tickets of its end.
sp.cap.why: The bound $N - m$ read off an end bounds the counter of its dual end only through this inequality, which E-Link and F-Link use.
sp.cap.breaks: A counter above its tickets would let the new dual end after a link have a counter above the bound the link premise checks.

args.name: f, m

sp.tsum.title: $m + m' \leq N$ on internal channels
sp.tsum.meaning: For an internal channel the tickets of its two ends, read from $K$, sum to at most $N$.
sp.tsum.why: It is the invariant $\mathsf{tk}(o) + \mathsf{tk}(\overline{o}) \leq N$ of typing, kept along a run. A creation chooses tickets with that sum, an action keeps the tickets, and a link joins two ends whose tickets meet it by the premise of F-Link. Lock-free adequacy measures a wait by the counter of the dual end, and this invariant bounds the counter of a new dual end after a link.
sp.tsum.breaks: Without it the measure need not fall at a link.
sp.tsum.signature: \mathsf{ech}\,o \in C \land K(o) = (\_, \_, \_, m) \land K(\overline{o}) = (\_, \_, \_, m') \Rightarrow m + m' \leq N

sp.own.title: $\mathsf{consistent}(a, A, \Phi)$
sp.own.meaning: The ownership map $K$ of the annotated configuration agrees with $A$ and $\Phi$. Each held end is held by one thread of the configuration and is internal or in the interface. Both ends of an internal channel are held, at dual types, points and protocols. Interface entries come from $\Sigma$, counters are finite and at most the tickets, and the tickets of the two ends of an internal channel sum to at most $N$.
sp.own.why: Lock-free adequacy reads the thread holding an end, its point and its counter from $K$, and concludes that the dual end of an internal end is held by some thread at the dual protocol.
sp.own.breaks: Without it a thread could wait on an end whose dual end no thread holds, and the chain of waits in the proof of adequacy would break off.
sp.own.example: Two threads closing $c^{+}$ and $c^{-}$, each holding one end, with $C = \{c\}$.

th.adequacy.title: Adequacy
th.adequacy.meaning: If $W$ is consistent and $p \in P^W_\alpha\llbracket\varnothing \vdash T\rrbracket$ for each ordinal index $\alpha$, then $p$ is deadlock free.
th.adequacy.why: It turns the semantic judgment into the safety property. A stuck closed process has finitely many waiting threads, and readiness puts each wait below the dual points of the waiting thread in the strict order of $W$. At a minimal wait the thread holding the dual end can act.
th.adequacy.breaks: With a cyclic order the premise would hold for two threads that wait on each other.
th.adequacy.example: Two threads closing the two ends of $c$ are deadlock free.

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

deviations.reason: The Rocq states the premise as `sem_ptyped`, with the notation $\varnothing \vDash_W p : T$, at a world of the relation, which is consistent by its type.

th.lf-adequacy.title: Lock-free adequacy
th.lf-adequacy.meaning: If $W$ is ranked and each ordinal index $\alpha$ has an annotated configuration $a \in S^{N,W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\varnothing \vdash T\rrbracket$ with $\mathsf{erase}(q_a) = p$, then $p$ is lock free.
th.lf-adequacy.why: A pending thread waits for the thread holding the dual end of its end. The proof follows this chain of waiting threads and shows it is finite. Its measure ranks a waiting thread by the ordinal $\varrho(x)$ of the point $x$ of the end $o$ it waits on and then by the counter of the dual end. Ranks never change along a run, so the chain is finite, and a link gives a waiting end a dual end with a lower counter.
th.lf-adequacy.breaks: Without ranks an infinite descending chain of points lets a thread wait forever along an infinite chain of holding threads.
th.lf-adequacy.example: Two threads closing the two ends of $c$ are lock free.

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, a natural number for lock freedom}

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.lf-thread-progress.title: Thread progress
th.lf-thread-progress.meaning: Under the premises of lock-free adequacy and $\mathsf{no\_tau\_divergence}\,p$, each run $(r, l)$ with $\mathsf{erase}(r\,0) = p$, $\mathsf{maximal}\,(r, l)$ and $\mathsf{wfair}\,(r, l)$ satisfies $\mathsf{thread\_progress\_run}\,(r, l)$.
th.lf-thread-progress.why: Each thread eventually returns a value or takes part in a session step. Typing no longer excludes a loop of forces that holds no end, so the absence of internal divergence is a hypothesis.

args.name: (r, l)
args.meaning: a run, $r\,i$ the configuration and $l\,i$ the event at position $i$

th.fundamental.title: Fundamental theorem
th.fundamental.meaning: If $W$ is well formed and $\varnothing ; \Delta \vdash^{F}_{W} t : T$, then $\Delta \vDash^{F}_{W'} t : T$ at each consistent extension $W'$ of $W$\inmode{lf}{ that is strict}.
th.fundamental.why: Each typing rule has a semantic counterpart that holds at each index, and the theorem is the induction on the derivation. A creation grows the world by a fresh base and the facts of $C$. \inmode{lf}{No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.}
th.fundamental.example: The main thread of the [[ex-cycle|cycle]] satisfies the semantic judgment.
th.fundamental.signature: \mathsf{world\_wf}\,W \land \varnothing ; \Delta \vdash^{F}_{W} t : T \land W \sqsubseteq W' \land \mathsf{cons}\,W'\inmode{lf}{ \land \mathsf{strict}\,W'} \Rightarrow \Delta \vDash^{F}_{W'} t : T

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the linear context of ends and variables

th.fundamental-typed.title: Fundamental theorem for annotated typing
th.fundamental-typed.meaning: For each $N$, the annotated typing judgment implies the semantic judgment at $\Delta_{df}$ and $T_{df}$, at each strict consistent extension of $W$.
th.fundamental-typed.why: Erasing the annotations of an annotated derivation gives a deadlock-free derivation, to which the fundamental theorem applies. No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.
th.fundamental-typed.example: The client and server main at $N = \infty$.
th.fundamental-typed.signature: \mathsf{world\_wf}\,W \land \varnothing ; \Delta \vdash^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} t : T\ !\ \varepsilon \land W \sqsubseteq W' \land \mathsf{cons}\,W' \land \mathsf{strict}\,W' \Rightarrow \Delta_{df} \vDash^{F}_{W'} t : T_{df}

th.live-fundamental.title: Fundamental theorem at $\kappa_L$
th.live-fundamental.meaning: $\varnothing ; \Delta \vdash^{F}_{W} t : T$ implies $\Delta \mathrel{\vDash[\kappa_L]}^{F}_{W'} t : T$ at each strict consistent extension $W'$ of $W$.
th.live-fundamental.why: A force costs one level at $\kappa_L$, so a box reads its body below its own level, as in the deadlock-free proof. No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.
th.live-fundamental.breaks: With a free force the statement is false, because $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$ types and satisfies no semantic judgment at $\kappa_L$.
th.live-fundamental.signature: \mathsf{world\_wf}\,W \land \varnothing ; \Delta \vdash^{F}_{W} t : T \land W \sqsubseteq W' \land \mathsf{cons}\,W' \land \mathsf{strict}\,W' \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrel{\vDash[\kappa_L]}^{F}_{W'} t : T

th.live-fundamental-typed.title: Fundamental theorem at $\kappa_L$ for annotated typing
th.live-fundamental-typed.meaning: The annotated typing judgment implies the semantic judgment at $\kappa_L$ at erased environments and type, at each strict consistent extension of $W$.
th.live-fundamental-typed.why: It is the fundamental theorem at $\kappa_L$ after erasure. No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.
th.live-fundamental-typed.example: A thread typed by P-Term at finite $N$.

th.fundamental-proc.title: Fundamental theorem for processes
th.fundamental-proc.meaning: $\Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{\infty}}_{W} p : T$ implies $\Sigma \vDash_{W} p : T$, the semantic judgment at the world of the derivation.
th.fundamental-proc.why: One induction on the derivation. The case of P-Term is the fundamental theorem for terms, the case of P-Connect the semantic P-Connect at the join of the two component worlds. \inmode{lf}{No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.}
th.fundamental-proc.example: Two threads closing the two ends of $c$.

th.lf-fundamental.title: Lock-free fundamental theorem
th.lf-fundamental.meaning: Under excluded middle, $\Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W} p : T$ at a finite $N$ implies $\Sigma \Vvdash^{N}_{W} p : T$, the lock-free judgment at each ranked extension of $W$.
th.lf-fundamental.why: The fuel of each thread comes from its cost typing at finite $N$, and its relation at $\kappa_L$ from its typing, read at ranked worlds. Excluded middle enters through the creations under $\mathsf{gen\_new}$, which choose the largest of finitely many ranks.

th.sem-p-term.title: Semantic P-Term
th.sem-p-term.meaning: If $\mathsf{tfree}\,T$, $\mathsf{sth}\,\Theta\,\Sigma\,\Theta_B\,C$ and $t \in E[\kappa]^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Theta \vdash T\rrbracket^{\varnothing}$, then $(C, \{t\}) \in P[\kappa]^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma \vdash T\rrbracket$.
th.sem-p-term.why: It is P-Term in the relation. When $t$ spawns $v$, the child receives exactly the ends $\mathsf{fends}(v)$, which $V$ fixes by $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, and the proof composes parent and child as P-Connect does.

th.sth.title: $\mathsf{sth}\,\Theta\,\Sigma\,\Theta_B\,C$
th.sth.meaning: $\Theta = \Sigma \cup \Theta_B$, $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_B = \mathsf{ends}(C)$, $\mathsf{chans}\,\Sigma \cap C = \varnothing$, $\mathsf{pfree}\,\Sigma$, and for each $c \in C$ the two entries of $\Theta_B$ are dual at dual points.
th.sth.why: These are the environment premises of P-Term, as the semantic proof uses these premises.

th.sem-p-connect.title: Semantic P-Connect
th.sem-p-connect.meaning: If $\mathsf{tfree}\,T$, $\mathsf{conn}$, $p_1 \in P^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_C \vdash T\rrbracket$ and $p_2 \in P^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma_2 \cup \Sigma_D \vdash \ast\rrbracket$, then $p_1 \parallel_{\Sigma_C} p_2 \in P^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2 \vdash T\rrbracket$, with both components at one world $W$.
th.sem-p-connect.why: It is P-Connect in the relation, for each index and each cost table. Both components are read at one world, so two orders are never reconciled, and a fresh base of either side is fresh for that world.
th.sem-p-connect.example: Two threads closing $c^{+}$ and $c^{-}$, cut at $c$.
th.sem-p-connect.signature: \mathsf{tfree}\,T \land \mathsf{conn} \land p_1 \in P^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_C \vdash T\rrbracket \land p_2 \in P^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma_2 \cup \Sigma_D \vdash \ast\rrbracket \Rightarrow p_1 \parallel_{\Sigma_C} p_2 \in P^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2 \vdash T\rrbracket

args.name: \Sigma_C, \Sigma_D
args.meaning: the cut and its dual ends

th.lf-p-connect.title: P-Connect in the lock-free judgment
th.lf-p-connect.meaning: If $\mathsf{conn}$, $\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_C \Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_1} p_1 : T$ and $\Sigma_2 \cup \Sigma_D \Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_2} p_2 : \ast$, then $\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2 \Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_1 \sqcup W_2} p_1 \parallel_{\Sigma_C} p_2 : T$. With $\mathsf{wf}\,W_1$, $\mathsf{wf}\,W_2$ and $\mathsf{wf}\,(W_1|_S \sqcup W_2|_S)$ a closed composite is lock free. The fundamental theorem for processes applies it at the worlds of the two components.
th.lf-p-connect.why: Each component is read at the ranked extensions of its own world. A ranked extension $W'$ of the join extends both. The first component starts at some extension of $W'$, and the second is read there and starts at a further extension $W''$. The first moves up to $W''$ because the relation is monotone in the world. A ranked extension of the join exists exactly when the join is well-founded, which the condition on the shared bases gives. Its ranks come from the order of the join, never from the ranks of a component.
th.lf-p-connect.breaks: Two components at fixed ranked worlds $W_1' \sqsupseteq W_1$ and $W_2' \sqsupseteq W_2$ do not compose, because the two rankings may order shared points that no fact relates in opposite directions.
th.lf-p-connect.example: The client at $W_{cli}$ and the server at $W_{srv}$, which share the base $\rho$, compose over the cut $\{a, b\}$.
th.lf-p-connect.signature: \mathsf{conn} \land \Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_C \Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_1} p_1 : T \land \Sigma_2 \cup \Sigma_D \Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_2} p_2 : \ast \Rightarrow \Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2 \Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_1 \sqcup W_2} p_1 \parallel_{\Sigma_C} p_2 : T

th.lf-p-term.title: P-Term in the lock-free judgment
th.lf-p-term.meaning: Under excluded middle, a thread that meets the premises of P-Term at a finite $N$ satisfies $\Sigma \Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_W (C_0, \{t\}) : T$.
th.lf-p-term.why: It is P-Term read in the lock-free process relation. The relation of the thread at each ranked world comes from the fundamental theorem at $\kappa_L$ at ranked worlds.

th.Erel-bind.title: Bind
th.Erel-bind.meaning: For each cost table, if $e \in E^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Theta_1 \vdash T\rrbracket^{F \cup \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta_2}$ and $f[v] \in E^{W'}_{\beta}\llbracket\Theta_v \cup \Theta_2 \vdash U\rrbracket^{F}$ for each $W' \sqsupseteq W$, $\beta \leq \alpha$ and $v \in V^{W'}_{\beta}\llbracket\Theta_v \vdash T\rrbracket$, then $f[e] \in E^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Theta_1 \cup \Theta_2 \vdash U\rrbracket^{F}$.
th.Erel-bind.why: Each rule with a subterm runs the subterm first. The frame holds $\Theta_2$ while the hole runs, so the hole must not wait above $\mathsf{ap}\,\Theta_2$.
th.Erel-bind.signature: e \in E^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Theta_1 \vdash T\rrbracket^{F \cup \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta_2} \land (\forall W' \sqsupseteq W, \beta \leq \alpha, v.\ \ldots) \Rightarrow f[e] \in E^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Theta_1 \cup \Theta_2 \vdash U\rrbracket^{F}

th.soundness.meaning: $\varnothing \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{\infty}}_{W} p : T$ implies that $p$ is deadlock free.
th.soundness.why: The fundamental theorem for processes at the world of the derivation, which is consistent, followed by adequacy. \inmode{lf}{No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.}

th.lf-soundness.title: Lock-free soundness
th.lf-soundness.meaning: Under excluded middle and functional choice, $\varnothing \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W} p : T$ at a finite $N$ implies that $p$ is lock free.
th.lf-soundness.why: The lock-free fundamental theorem, a ranked extension of the world of the derivation, and lock-free adequacy. The choice fixes one annotated configuration that serves each index. With dependent choice the run form adds a weakly fair maximal run of the process.

th.lf-soundness-source.title: Lock-free soundness for source terms
th.lf-soundness-source.meaning: Under excluded middle and functional choice, for a well-formed well-founded $W$, $N \in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathsf{tfree}\,T$, a typing $\varnothing ; \varnothing \vdash^{\varnothing}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} t : T\ !\ c$, the process $(\varnothing, \{t\})$ is lock free.
th.lf-soundness-source.why: The premises are those of P-Term at finite $N$ with $\Sigma = \varnothing$ and $C_0 = \varnothing$.

th.lf-padovani.title: Lock freedom in reachability form
th.lf-padovani.meaning: Assume excluded middle and dependent choice. If $p$ is lock free, $\mathsf{erase}\,q_0 = p$, $q_0 \to^{*} q$ and thread $t$ is pending in $q$, then there are $q_1$ and a step $q_1 \to q_2$ with event $ev$ such that $q \to^{*} q_1$ and $t \in \mathsf{parts}(ev)$.
th.lf-padovani.why: It is the reachability form of lock freedom, stated per thread. A maximal weakly fair run from $q$, prefixed with the steps from $q_0$, is a run from $p$, and lock freedom of that run makes $t$ take part in a later step.
th.lf-padovani.signature: \mathsf{EM} \land \mathsf{DC} \land \mathsf{lock\_free}\,p \land \mathsf{erase}\,q_0 = p \land q_0 \to^{*} q \land \mathsf{pend}(q, t) \Rightarrow \exists q_1\,ev\,q_2.\ q \to^{*} q_1 \xrightarrow{ev} q_2 \land t \in \mathsf{parts}(ev)

args.name: \mathsf{EM}
args.meaning: excluded middle, $P \lor \lnot P$ for each proposition $P$, a hypothesis and no axiom

args.name: \mathsf{DC}
args.meaning: dependent choice, a total relation on a type has an infinite chain from each element, a hypothesis and no axiom

args.name: t
args.meaning: a thread pending in the reachable configuration $q$

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{EM}$ and $\mathsf{DC}$ abbreviate the hypotheses `excluded_middle` and `dependent_choice`.

th.conservative.title: Conservativity
th.conservative.meaning: The annotated typing judgment at $N = \infty$ derives some $T_{df}\ !\ \varepsilon$ iff the deadlock-free judgment derives $T_{df}$, at erased contexts.
th.conservative.why: Deadlock-free typing is the annotated typing judgment with credits, costs and tickets ignored, so one set of rules serves both.

th.typed-dftyped.title: Erasure to deadlock-free typing
th.typed-dftyped.meaning: For each $N$, erasing the annotations of an annotated derivation gives a deadlock-free derivation.
th.typed-dftyped.why: Hence each lock-free typing is also a deadlock-free typing.
th.typed-dftyped.example: The cycle at $N = 2$ erases to its deadlock-free typing.

th.cost-fundamental.title: Cost fundamental theorem
th.cost-fundamental.meaning: The annotated typing judgment implies the semantic cost judgment $\Delta \vDash^{N} e : T\ !\ \varepsilon$.
th.cost-fundamental.why: It is the cost half of the annotated typing judgment, proved rule by rule.

args.name: N
args.meaning: the bound on the tickets of a channel

th.fsem-of-cost.title: Fuel from cost typing
th.fsem-of-cost.meaning: If $\varnothing ; \Delta \vdash^{\varnothing}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} e : T\ !\ c$ and $\mathsf{tfree}\,T$, then $\mathsf{fsem}\,N\,\Delta\inmode{lf}{^{N}}\,e$.
th.fsem-of-cost.why: Typing keeps the credit of each end of $\Delta$ at most its tickets, so each end may start at its tickets, and the cost judgment yields the per-thread fuel that lock freedom needs.
th.fsem-of-cost.breaks: If a closure could mention an end it does not own, the forwarder could receive a closure that owns nothing and would have no fuel after spawning the closure.

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the ends of the thread with their credits and tickets

th.Prel.title: The process relation $P$
th.Prel.meaning: $P\inmode{lf}{[\kappa]}^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma \vdash T\rrbracket$, the processes in the relation at the world $W$, ordinal index $\alpha$, interface $\Sigma$ and result $T$\inmode{lf}{, at the cost table $\kappa$}.
th.Prel.why: The semantic process judgment asks membership at each index.
th.Prel.example: Two threads closing $c^{+}$ and $c^{-}$ lie in $P^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\varnothing \vdash \ast\rrbracket$ for each $\alpha$.

args.name: \kappa
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{a cost table, $\kappa_{DF}$ for deadlock freedom and $\kappa_L$ for lock freedom}

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.Erel.title: The term relation $E$
th.Erel.meaning: $E\inmode{lf}{[\kappa]}^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Theta \vdash T\rrbracket^{F}$ is the set of terms in the relation at the world $W$ and ordinal index $\alpha$, for ends $\Theta$, result $T$ and future $F$\inmode{lf}{, at the cost table $\kappa$}.
th.Erel.why: The semantic term judgment asks membership at each index and for each grounding of the variables.

args.name: \kappa
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{a cost table, $\kappa_{DF}$ for deadlock freedom and $\kappa_L$ for lock freedom}

args.name: \Theta
args.meaning: the ends held by the term

th.Vrel.title: The value relation $V$
th.Vrel.meaning: $V^{W}_{\beta}\llbracket\Theta \vdash T\rrbracket$ is the set of values in the relation at world $W$ and ordinal index $\beta$, for ends $\Theta$ and type $T$.
th.Vrel.why: A term in $E$ that is irreducible is a value in $V$.

args.name: \Theta
args.meaning: the ends held by the term

th.soup.title: The lock-free process relation $S^{N,W}_{\alpha}$
th.soup.meaning: $a \in S^{N,W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma \vdash T\rrbracket$ holds of an annotated configuration $a$ when each thread of $a$ is in the relation at $\kappa_L$ and has fuel at the ordinal index $\alpha$. Ownership, points, counters and tickets are those that $a$ records.
th.soup.why: The lock-free judgment chooses $a$ at each index, and the existential property gives one $a$ for each index.
th.soup.example: The state of two threads closing $c^{+}$ and $c^{-}$.

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, a natural number for lock freedom}

args.name: W
args.meaning: a ranked world, which the world of each configuration extends

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.qa.title: $q_a$
th.qa.meaning: The configuration of the annotated configuration $a$.
th.qa.why: An annotated configuration is a configuration together with ownership, counters and tickets.

th.em.title: Excluded middle $\mathsf{EM}$
th.em.meaning: Each proposition holds or fails, $\forall P.\ P \lor \neg P$, as an explicit hypothesis and no axiom.
th.em.why: It is a hypothesis of the lock-free results only. The existential property of ordinal indices is proved by contradiction, and a creation under $\mathsf{gen\_new}$ takes the largest of finitely many ranks. The deadlock-free soundness results, binary and n-ary, take no excluded middle, and neither does soundness at $\kappa_L$.
th.em.breaks: Without it a creation at a ranked world cannot pick a rank at or above two given ranks, and the annotated configuration chosen at each index does not give one that serves each index.
th.em.example: Transfinite Iris assumes it in its model.

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{EM}$ abbreviates `excluded_middle`.

th.ac.title: Functional choice $\mathsf{FC}$
th.ac.meaning: A total relation contains a function, as an explicit hypothesis and no axiom.
th.ac.why: The existential property picks one failing index per witness, and the run picks one creation choice per state and position, from which a recursion builds the states of the run.
th.ac.breaks: Without it the states chosen per index do not form one sequence along the run.
th.ac.example: One creation choice per position of a run of the lock-free process relation.
th.ac.signature: \mathsf{FC} := \forall X\,Y\,(R : X \to Y \to \mathsf{Prop}).\ (\forall x.\ \exists y.\ R\,x\,y) \Rightarrow \exists f.\ \forall x.\ R\,x\,(f\,x)

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{FC}$ abbreviates `functional_choice`.

th.conn.title: $\mathsf{conn}$
th.conn.meaning: The side conditions of P-Connect, with $\Sigma_D$ the dual ends of $\Sigma_C$ dual up to $\approx$ at dual points.
th.conn.why: They make the composite a process in which each channel belongs to one side.

args.name: \Sigma_C, \Sigma_D
args.meaning: the cut and its dual ends

args.name: C_1, C_2
args.meaning: the restricted channels of the two sides

th.par.title: $p_1 \parallel_{\Sigma_C} p_2$
th.par.meaning: The composite $(C_1 \cup C_2 \cup \mathsf{chans}\,\Sigma_C, E_1 \uplus E_2)$ of $p_1 = (C_1, E_1)$ and $p_2 = (C_2, E_2)$.
th.par.why: After composition the two sides communicate on the cut, which no outside process holds.

th.df.title: Erasure $X_{df}$
th.df.meaning: $\Delta_{df}$ and $T_{df}$ drop each credit, ticket and cost and keep session types, points and facts.
th.df.why: Deadlock-free typing and the relations read no annotation.

args.name: X
args.meaning: an end environment, a variable context or a type

th.styof.title: $\Delta\inmode{lf}{^{N}}$
th.styof.meaning: The held ends of $\Delta$ for fuel, each counter at its tickets. An entry $o \mapsto S_x\inmode{lf}{^{a,m}}$ of $\Delta$ becomes $o \mapsto S^{m,m}$.
th.styof.why: Fuel reads protocols, counters and tickets and ignores points and credits. A thread starts with each counter at its tickets.

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the linear context of ends and variables

th.adequacy-h.title: Adequacy at a world of typing
th.adequacy-h.meaning: If $W$ is well formed and consistent and $\varnothing \vDash_W p : T$, then $p$ is deadlock free.
th.adequacy-h.why: A well-formed consistent world is its own consistent extension, and adequacy applies there.
th.adequacy-h.example: The two closes over the empty interface.

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.lf-sems-adequacy.title: Lock-free adequacy at a world of typing
th.lf-sems-adequacy.meaning: Under excluded middle and functional choice, if $W$ is well formed and well-founded and $\varnothing \Vvdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_W p : T$, then $p$ is lock free.
th.lf-sems-adequacy.why: A well-founded world has a ranked extension, at which lock-free adequacy applies.
th.lf-sems-adequacy.example: The split client and server program, two components at their own worlds.

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, a natural number for lock freedom}

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.live-fundamental-ranked.title: Fundamental theorem at $\kappa_L$ at ranked worlds
th.live-fundamental-ranked.meaning: Under excluded middle, a derivation at a finite bound $N$ gives the semantic judgment at $\kappa_L$ at erased environments and type, at each consistent extension $W'$ of $W$ of either kind.
th.live-fundamental-ranked.why: The lock-free process relation reads each thread at a ranked world. At a finite bound the creations meet $\mathsf{gen\_new}$, which finds ranks for the new tree.
th.live-fundamental-ranked.example: Each thread of a lock-free example.
th.live-fundamental-ranked.signature: \mathsf{EM} \land \mathsf{world\_wf}\,W \land \varnothing ; \Delta \vdash^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} t : T\ !\ c \land W \sqsubseteq W' \land \mathsf{cons}\,W' \Rightarrow \Delta_{df} \mathrel{\vDash[\kappa_L]}^{F}_{W'} t : T_{df}

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, a natural number for lock freedom}

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the linear context of ends and variables

th.live-fundamental-proc.title: Fundamental theorem at $\kappa_L$ for processes
th.live-fundamental-proc.meaning: $\Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{\infty}}_{W} p : T$ implies $\Sigma \mathrel{\vDash[\kappa_L]}_{W} p : T$, the semantic judgment at $\kappa_L$.
th.live-fundamental-proc.why: The fundamental theorem for processes read at $\kappa_L$. No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.sem-p-connect-sw.title: Semantic P-Connect at the worlds of typing
th.sem-p-connect-sw.meaning: If $\mathsf{tfree}\,T$, $\mathsf{conn}$, $\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_C \vDash_{W_1} p_1 : T$ and $\Sigma_2 \cup \Sigma_D \vDash_{W_2} p_2 : \ast$, then the composite is in the semantic judgment at $W_1 \sqcup W_2$.
th.sem-p-connect-sw.why: A consistent extension of the join extends both worlds, so both components hold there and semantic P-Connect applies at that one world. The fundamental theorem for processes applies it at the worlds of the two components.
th.sem-p-connect-sw.signature: \mathsf{tfree}\,T \land \mathsf{conn} \land \Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_C \vDash_{W_1} p_1 : T \land \Sigma_2 \cup \Sigma_D \vDash_{W_2} p_2 : \ast \Rightarrow \Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2 \vDash_{W_1 \sqcup W_2} p_1 \parallel_{\Sigma_C} p_2 : T

th.connect-n.title: Soundness of the n-ary connect
th.connect-n.meaning: If the components $\bar W, p, T$ of the n-ary connect\inmode{lf}{ at $N = \infty$} are closed and the join of their worlds is consistent, then $p$ is deadlock free.
th.connect-n.why: It folds the binary P-Connect through the admissible n-ary rule and applies soundness. \inmode{lf}{No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.}
th.connect-n.example: The consistent variant of the ring of three threads.

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.live-soundness.title: Soundness without divergence by free steps
th.live-soundness.meaning: $\varnothing \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{\infty}}_{W} p : T$ implies that $p$ is deadlock free and has no divergence by free steps.
th.live-soundness.why: The fundamental theorem for processes at $\kappa_L$ followed by adequacy at $\kappa_L$. No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.lf-connect-n.title: Lock-free soundness of the n-ary connect
th.lf-connect-n.meaning: Under excluded middle and functional choice, closed components at a finite $N$ whose worlds join to a well-founded world compose to a lock-free process.
th.lf-connect-n.why: The n-ary rule followed by lock-free soundness.
th.lf-connect-n.example: Three components typed at a finite bound.

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, a natural number for lock freedom}

th.dc.title: Dependent choice $\mathsf{DC}$
th.dc.meaning: A total relation has an infinite path from each start, as an explicit hypothesis and no axiom.
th.dc.why: A maximal weakly fair run picks one step at each position, which dependent choice provides.
th.dc.example: Round robin over threads picks the next step.
th.dc.signature: \mathsf{DC} := \forall A\,(R : A \to A \to \mathsf{Prop}).\ (\forall x.\ \exists y.\ R\,x\,y) \Rightarrow \forall x_0.\ \exists f.\ f\,0 = x_0 \land \forall n.\ R\,(f\,n)\,(f\,(n{+}1))

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{DC}$ abbreviates `dependent_choice`.

th.pcomps.title: Components $\mathsf{comps}_N(\bar W, p, T)$
th.pcomps.meaning: Components $p_1, \ldots, p_n$ typed at worlds $\bar W = W_1, \ldots, W_n$\inmode{lf}{ at the bound $N$}, each connected over a cut to the composite of the ones before it, with the side conditions of P-Connect and no condition on worlds.
th.pcomps.why: It collects the premises of the n-ary connect. The one condition on worlds is checked once, on the join.
th.pcomps.example: The three threads of the ring.

args.name: N
args.meaning: the bound on the tickets of a channel, a natural number for lock freedom

th.ptermprem.title: $\mathsf{pterm}_N(\Sigma, C_0, t, T)$
th.ptermprem.meaning: The premises of P-Term at the bound $N$ for the thread $t$ over the interface $\Sigma$ with restricted channels $C_0$ and result $T$, except the conditions on the world, of which it keeps $\mathsf{world\_wf}\,W$.
th.ptermprem.why: The lock-free judgment reads the thread at each ranked extension, so the world needs no condition here.
th.ptermprem.example: One thread closing its end $c^{+}$ with $C_0 = \varnothing$.

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.live-sub-df.title: The relation at $\kappa_L$ implies the relation at $\kappa_{DF}$
th.live-sub-df.meaning: Under excluded middle and functional choice, a closed process in the process relation at $\kappa_L$ at each index at a world $W$ is in the process relation at $\kappa_{DF}$ at each index at $W$. Its result type must hold no end and no box.
th.live-sub-df.why: The relation at $\kappa_L$ reads internal steps at cost $0$ and the relation at $\kappa_{DF}$ at cost $1$. A run of internal steps is finite at $\kappa_L$, and choice fixes one world for each level after a creation.
th.live-sub-df.example: Each process in the semantic judgment at $\kappa_L$.
th.live-sub-df.signature: \mathsf{EM} \land \mathsf{FC} \land \mathsf{tfree}\,T \land \mathsf{boxfree}\,T \land (\forall \alpha.\ p \in P[\kappa_L]^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \varnothing \vdash T \rrbracket) \Rightarrow \forall \alpha.\ p \in P[\kappa_{DF}]^{W}_{\alpha}\llbracket \varnothing \vdash T \rrbracket

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.boxfree.title: $\mathsf{boxfree}$
th.boxfree.meaning: $\mathsf{boxfree}\,T$ when no box type occurs in $T$ outside arrows and end types, through products and sums.
th.boxfree.why: It restricts the result type in the comparison of the relations at $\kappa_L$ and at $\kappa_{DF}$.

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

th.lf-tp-gen.title: Thread progress from lock freedom
th.lf-tp-gen.meaning: A lock-free process without internal divergence, whose links each restrict a channel, makes each thread progress on each maximal weakly fair run.
th.lf-tp-gen.why: It is the step from lock freedom to progress of each thread, pending or not. For a process in the lock-free judgment at a ranked world, lock-free adequacy gives lock freedom and the lock-free process relation gives restricted links. No internal divergence stays a hypothesis, because a loop of forces that holds no end is in the relation.

th.linksr.title: $\mathsf{links\_restricted}$
th.linksr.meaning: In each reachable process a link acts on at least one end of a restricted channel.
th.linksr.why: A link between two interface ends would leave no thread in the process to serve either side, and thread progress would fail for reasons outside the process.
th.linksr.example: A link of two ends of channels the process created.

th.wfit.title: Worlds the fundamental theorem reads
th.wfit.meaning: \inmode{lf}{$\mathsf{fit}_N\,W$ holds when $W$ is strict, or, under excluded middle, when $W$ is ranked and the bound $N$ is finite.}
th.wfit.why: \inmode{lf}{The induction behind the fundamental theorems reads each consistent extension $W'$ of $W$ that fits the bound. A creation grows a strict world under $\mathsf{acyc\_new}$. A ranked world needs $\mathsf{gen\_new}$, which holds only at a finite bound, and the choice of the largest of finitely many ranks.}
th.wfit.breaks: \inmode{lf}{At $N = \infty$ a ranked world could meet a creation under $\mathsf{acyc\_new}$ that has no ranks.}
th.wfit.example: \inmode{lf}{The deadlock-free theorems use strict worlds, the lock-free ones ranked worlds at a finite bound.}

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, a natural number for lock freedom}

th.typed-ren.title: Renaming constants
th.typed-ren.meaning: A bijection $\pi$ on constants maps a derivation\inmode{lf}{ at each bound and cost} to a derivation of the renamed judgment.
th.typed-ren.why: The P-Term case of the fundamental theorem renames the typing of the thread, and the renaming of a process derivation uses it at each thread. The program does not change, because no term mentions a point.
th.typed-ren.example: Renaming the private constant $0$ of one copy of $P(c, d)$ to $1$.
th.typed-ren.signature: \Gamma ; \Delta \vdash^{F}_{W} e : T \Rightarrow \pi\Gamma ; \pi\Delta \vdash^{\pi F}_{\pi W} e : \pi T

th.lf-soup-term.title: Semantic P-Term in the lock-free judgment
th.lf-soup-term.meaning: Let a thread $t$ meet the channel premises of P-Term at a finite $N$, be in the relation at $\kappa_L$ and have fuel at each index. Then each ordinal index $\alpha$ has an annotated configuration $a \in S^{N,W}_{\alpha}\llbracket\Sigma \vdash T\rrbracket$ whose process is $(C_0, \{t\})$.
th.lf-soup-term.why: It is P-Term in the lock-free process relation, stated on the relation and fuel of the thread and not on its typing. A thread proved by hand composes with typed ones.

args.name: N
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the bound on the tickets of a channel, a natural number for lock freedom}

deviations.reason: The Rocq concludes `lf_semk` at the world $W$ of the relation. The map writes it out, because $\Vvdash^{N}_W$ names the judgment at each ranked extension of [[sj-all]].

th.chprem.title: $\mathsf{chan}_N(\Sigma, \Theta_B, C_0)$
th.chprem.meaning: $\Theta_B$ holds both ends of each $c \in C_0$, dual at dual points, each at credit equal to its tickets with tickets of sum at most $N$, and no channel of $\Sigma$ is in $C_0$. $\Theta$ is $\Sigma$ at the interface annotations $\eta$ together with $\Theta_B$.
th.chprem.why: These are the premises of P-Term about restricted channels.
th.chprem.example: $C_0 = \varnothing$ for a thread with no private channel.

args.name: \Theta_B
args.meaning: the ends of the restricted channels

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{chan}_N$ names the premises of `lf_soup_term` on the channels $C_0$.

th.cl2-needs.title: What two closes ask
th.cl2-needs.meaning: Each typing of $\mathsf{close}\,a$ followed by $\mathsf{close}\,b$, at each bound and context and over each world whose facts relate points at its constants, derives $\Gamma \vdash x \prec \overline{y}$ for the points $x$ of $a$ and $y$ of $b$.
th.cl2-needs.why: The first close waits at $x$ while the thread holds $b$, whose dual point is $\overline{y}$. This inversion turns a deadlock into a typing failure. Through an opening it reads the conservativity premise of E-Open over such a world. It proves the rejections of the [[ex-gennew|creations with exits]] and of the [[ex-flag|self-computed flag]], and in [[ex-forkjoin|recursive fork-join]] it asks each child point below the dual point of its parent.
th.cl2-needs.example: A thread that closes $c$ at $\rho$ and then $d$ at $\rho\cdot 0$ needs $\rho \prec \overline{\rho\cdot 0}$.

th.tpr.title: $\mathsf{thread\_progress\_run}$
th.tpr.meaning: For a run $(r, l)$, $\mathsf{thread\_progress\_run}\,(r, l)$ holds iff each thread $t$ of each position $i$ later stops or acts. That is, some $j \geq i$ exists at which $t$ is a value in $r\,j$ or takes part in the step $l\,j$ by a session action.
th.tpr.why: It states lock freedom per run for each thread, including the threads that are not pending. A thread that is neither stopped nor acting forever would be postponed without end.
th.tpr.example: In a run of two threads closing $c^{+}$ and $c^{-}$, both threads take part in the close step.

args.name: (r, l)
args.meaning: a run, $r\,i$ the configuration and $l\,i$ the event at position $i$

th.pinst.title: Point substitution
th.pinst.meaning: Instantiating the point variables of a derivation over $\Gamma$ by $\sigma$ gives a derivation over each $\Gamma'$ that derives the instance under $\sigma$ of each fact of $\Gamma$. Terms mention no point and stay. The world keeps its facts at constant bases, which $\sigma$ leaves alone.
th.pinst.why: Each premise that reads $\Gamma$ survives, and the binders of E-Box, E-Open and Sub-Ex lift $\sigma$ past their new variables. The conservativity premise of E-Open and of E-New survives the instantiation, because $\sigma$ acts only on the outer points of $C$ and leaves its facts and its tree alone.
th.pinst.breaks: Without it an opening could not be closed at the witnesses of a pack, and the use of $x$ in a let that opens its unit would stay under the constraint.
th.pinst.example: Closing an opening of $\exists\iota.\,C.\,T$ at an instance $\bar x$ where $\Gamma \vdash C[\bar x]$ gives a derivation over $\Gamma$ at $T[\bar x]$.

args.name: \sigma
args.meaning: a substitution of points for point variables

args.name: \Gamma'
args.meaning: a context that derives the instantiated facts of $\Gamma$

th.hinst.title: $\Gamma' \vdash \sigma(\Gamma)$
th.hinst.meaning: $\Gamma'$ derives $\sigma(u) \prec \sigma(v)$ for each fact $u \prec v$ of an instance in $\Gamma$.
th.hinst.why: It is the one condition point substitution puts on the new context.
th.hinst.example: $\Gamma \vdash \sigma(\Gamma, (C, \bar\iota))$ for $\sigma$ that closes $\bar\iota$ at $\bar x$, when $\Gamma \vdash C[\bar x]$.

args.name: \sigma
args.meaning: a substitution of points for point variables

th.let-var.title: A term and its let
th.let-var.meaning: If $e$ types at $T$, then $\mathsf{let}\ x = e\ \mathsf{in}\ x$ types at $T$ at the same world and contexts\inmode{lf}{, bound and cost}. The converse fails. With $f : \Box\,\exists\iota.\,\ast$ the let types at $\ast$ and $\mathsf{force}\,f$ types only at existentials. Over a well-formed world and contractive contexts with no existential entry in $\Delta$, the converse holds whenever the let binds $x$ at a type that is no existential.
th.let-var.why: E-Open opens an entry of $\Delta$, and the let puts the value of $e$ there. No rule opens the result of a term that is no variable. Over a $\Delta$ with no existential entry, a derivation of the let gives $e : T_1$ and the use of $x : T_1$ and $\ast : T_2$ that builds $T$. When $T_1$ is no existential, $e : T$ follows\inmode{lf}{ at no higher cost}. The use of $x$ is E-Var followed by E-Sub and E-Pack, and these steps apply to $e$. The use may first open $\ast : \exists\bar\iota.\,C.\,\ast$ and read $C$. The unit packs at witnesses of $C$, and point substitution closes the opening at these witnesses.
th.let-var.breaks: A rule that opens the result of $e$ would close the gap. Sub-Ex covers the case of an opening followed by a pack at the opened points with the same arity.
th.let-var.signature: \Gamma ; \Delta \vdash e : T \Rightarrow \Gamma ; \Delta \vdash \mathsf{let}\ x = e\ \mathsf{in}\ x : T

args.name: f
args.meaning: a variable bound to a box whose result is the existential $\exists\iota.\,\ast$

lbl.force.title: Label $\mathsf{force}$
lbl.force.meaning: The step $\mathsf{force}\,(!e) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{force}} e[!e]$ of a box.
lbl.force.why: A force has a label of its own, so that a cost table can charge it apart from $\beta$. A loop goes through a force, so a loop is charged at each force.
lbl.force.breaks: \inmode{lf}{With the label $\beta$ a force is free at $\kappa_L$, and $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$ is in no relation at $\kappa_L$.}

ct.force.title: $\kappa_{\mathrm{force}}$
ct.force.meaning: The cost of a force, one level in each table.
ct.force.why: The box rule reads the body of a box at a level below the level of the box, where the box itself is already in $V$. Deadlock-free typing accepts $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$, so the deadlock-free table needs this cost as well, or the box rule fails for a box that forces itself. \inmode{lf}{In $\kappa_L$ the same cost charges a loop at each round, and [[fu-obls|F-Force]] lowers the counters of the held ends.}
ct.force.breaks: At cost $0$ the body of $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$ is read at the level of the box, and the box is in no $V$.

ct.force-pos.title: $1 \leq \kappa_{\mathrm{force}}$
ct.force-pos.meaning: A cost table charges a force at least one level.
ct.force-pos.why: The box rule holds at each table with this condition, so one proof covers $\kappa_{DF}$ and $\kappa_L$.
ct.force-pos.breaks: A box that forces itself would be in no $V$.

F-Force.title: F-Force
F-Force.meaning: A force needs a positive counter on each held end that is not idle and a positive frame, and continues with each counter and the frame one lower.
F-Force.why: A loop goes through a force. A thread that loops while it holds a non-idle end exhausts the counter of that end, so the thread holding the dual end waits a finite time.
F-Force.breaks: With a free force, a thread could loop forever while the thread holding its dual end waits, and lock-free adequacy would fail.
F-Force.example: $\mathsf{force}\,f$ holding $d$ at counter $2$ continues with $d$ at counter $1$.

F-Force.spare.title: $\mathsf{positive}(\Phi) \land 1 \leq d$
F-Force.spare.meaning: Each held end that is not idle has a counter at least $1$, and so has the frame $d$.
F-Force.spare.why: The force decrements each counter, so each must be positive. Typing guarantees it, because [[r-boxes|E-Force]] charges one unit of effect, which ages the held context.
F-Force.spare.breaks: A force at counter $0$ under truncation would leave the counter at $0$ and could repeat forever.

E-Force.one.title: The force costs $1$
E-Force.one.meaning: E-Force has effect $\varepsilon_0 \cdot 1 \cdot \varepsilon$, the effect of $e$, one unit for the force and the effect of the body.
E-Force.one.why: The unit accounts for the counter decrement of [[fu-obls|F-Force]]. The rule that holds an end across the force ages the end by the effect, so a loop that holds a non-idle end has effect $\infty$ and fails the aging check at a finite bound.
E-Force.one.breaks: Without it a loop could hold a non-idle end forever, and the thread holding its dual end would wait without bound.
E-Force.one.example: $(\mathsf{force}\,f)\,\langle a, b\rangle$ ages $\langle a, b\rangle$ by one before the call.

args.name: \varepsilon
args.meaning: the effect of the box body

V-Box.body.title: The body one force below
V-Box.body.meaning: $e[!e] \in E^{W'}_{\beta}\llbracket\varnothing \vdash U[\bar s][\bar x]\rrbracket^{F}$ at each level $\beta$ with $\beta + \kappa_{\mathrm{force}} \leq \alpha$ and each future $F$ above $u[\bar x]$.
V-Box.body.why: A force steps $!e$ to $e[!e]$ at cost $\kappa_{\mathrm{force}} \geq 1$, so the body is read strictly below the level of the box. There the box itself is in $V$ by induction on the level, which makes the box rule hold at each cost table without a guard.
V-Box.body.breaks: Read at the level of the box, the body of $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$ would need the box at its own level, and a table with a free force would put no such box in $V$.
V-Box.body.example: The body of $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$ is read below the level of the box.
V-Box.body.signature: \forall \beta, F.\ \beta + \kappa_{\mathrm{force}} \leq \alpha \land u[\bar x] \prec F \Rightarrow e[!e] \in E^{W'}_{\beta}\llbracket \varnothing \vdash U[\bar s][\bar x] \rrbracket^{F}

args.name: \beta
args.meaning: a level at least a force below $\alpha$

args.name: F
args.meaning: a future above the instantiated upper point

prop.nofree.title: $\mathsf{no\_free\_divergence}$
prop.nofree.meaning: For each $q$ with $p \to^{*} q$, no infinite chain of free steps starts at $q$. A free step is an administrative step but a force.
prop.nofree.why: It is what the relation at $\kappa_L$ gives, because free steps cost nothing there. The proof of lock-free adequacy asks it of the thread that holds an awaited end.
prop.nofree.example: $\mathsf{force}\,!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$ has the property, because each of its steps is a force.

th.ptyped-ren.title: Renaming the constants of a process derivation
th.ptyped-ren.meaning: A bijection $\pi$ on constants maps a derivation $\Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_W p : T$ to a derivation of $\pi\Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{\pi W} p : \pi T$ at the renamed world.
th.ptyped-ren.why: It moves a typed component from one point to another, as in the two-sided expansion of the forwarder. The program does not change, because no term mentions a point.
th.ptyped-ren.breaks: Nothing. It is a lemma about derivations.
th.ptyped-ren.example: Swapping the constants $0$ and $1$ of the component $Q$ of the copycat.

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

sty.ssub.title: Session subtyping $\sqsubseteq$
sty.ssub.meaning: The greatest relation with $S \sqsubseteq S'$ only if $\mathsf{unfold}(S)$ and $\mathsf{unfold}(S')$ have the same first action and related continuations. A receive $?(\bar\iota.\,T)$ may become $?(\bar\iota.\,T')$ when $T \geq_{\mathrm{cr}} T'$, a send $!(\bar\iota.\,T)$ may become $!(\bar\iota.\,T')$ when $T' \geq_{\mathrm{cr}} T$, and the other annotations are equal.
sty.ssub.why: A credit is a lower bound on a counter. A payload received at some credit is also one at a lower credit, and a payload promised at a higher credit is also one at the credit the protocol asks. At annotations $\infty$ the relation is $\simeq$.
sty.ssub.breaks: Reversing either direction lets a receiver assume a counter that no sender guaranteed, and a thread acts on a payload end after its counter reached $0$.

args.name: T \geq_{\mathrm{cr}} T'
args.meaning: $T'$ is $T$ with the credit of each end and closure reached through $\otimes$, $\oplus$ and $\exists$ at most the credit at the same place in $T$, and the rest equal up to $\simeq$

E-New.pos.title: Position of a creation
E-New.pos.meaning: $(p, \bar\rho, C)$ is either $(\rho, \rho, C)$ for a fresh base $\rho$ whose facts $C$ meet the premise $\mathsf{acyc\_new}$\inmode{lf}{, and $\mathsf{new\_ok}_N$ at a finite bound}, or $(x\cdot\kappa, \cdot, \top)$ for a field $x\cdot\kappa$, with no bound point and no facts.
E-New.pos.why: A fresh base abstracts its points and states the facts the program needs about the new points. A field is an old point, whose facts were fixed with the base of $x$, so a field creation states nothing and abstracts nothing. A field may be used by more than one creation.
E-New.pos.breaks: A field creation that stated a new fact could contradict the facts fixed with the base of $x$.
E-New.pos.example: $(\rho, \rho, \{\rho \prec \overline{\rho\cdot 0}\})$ for a fresh base, $(\iota\cdot 0, \cdot, \top)$ for the field $\iota\cdot 0$.

args.name: p
args.meaning: the point of the positive end

args.name: \bar\rho
args.meaning: the bound point, $\rho$ at a fresh base and none at a field

args.name: C
args.meaning: the facts of the creation, $\top$ at a field

deviations.reason: The two constructors e_new and e_new_fld are the two cases of the triple.

E-New.vanish.title: An empty existential
E-New.vanish.meaning: $\exists^{\bot}\cdot.\ \top.\ T$ binds no point and states no fact, and it is the type $T$.
E-New.vanish.why: The field case of E-New has nothing to abstract, so its result is the product of the two ends.

deviations.reason: The Rocq types the field case at the product directly, and the map writes it as an existential with no bound point and no facts.

P-Term.ann.title: Interface annotations
P-Term.ann.meaning: $\eta$ maps each end $o$ to a credit and tickets $\eta(o) = (a, m)$. P-Term asks $m \leq N$ for each end of $\Sigma$, and the thread holds $o$ at $S_x^{a,m}$.
P-Term.ann.why: The tickets of an interface end are an upper bound on its counter, and its dual end is held by another component. Each component picks the tickets of its interface ends, and P-Connect checks the two sides of each cut against $N$.
P-Term.ann.breaks: With each interface end at $N/2$ a link of two interface ends asks $N/2 + N/2 > N$, so no forwarding component types over an interface.
P-Term.ann.example: $\eta(c^{+}) = \eta(d^{-}) = (N, N)$ and $\eta(c^{-}) = \eta(d^{+}) = (0, 0)$ for the [[ex-link|link]] closed by two threads that close the dual ends.

args.name: \eta
args.meaning: the interface annotations, a credit and tickets for each end

args.name: a, m
args.meaning: the credit and the tickets of the end $o$

P-Connect.tsum.title: Tickets at a cut
P-Connect.tsum.meaning: For each end $o$ of $\Sigma_C$ the tickets $\eta(o)_2$ of $o$ and $\eta(\overline{o})_2$ of its dual end sum to at most $N$.
P-Connect.tsum.why: P-Connect makes $o$ and $\overline{o}$ the two ends of one channel, which E-New would have created with tickets of sum at most $N$. A waiting thread then faces a dual end with counter at most $N - m$.
P-Connect.tsum.breaks: Two components that each give a cut end $N$ tickets would let one end wait on a dual end with counter up to $N$, beyond what the end bounds.
P-Connect.tsum.example: $N + 0 \leq N$ at each of the two cuts of the closed link.

args.name: \Sigma_C
args.meaning: the cut, the ends of the left component whose dual ends the right component holds

ty.up.title: The points above $v$, ${\vartriangle}v$
ty.up.meaning: ${\vartriangle}v$ stands for points that do not occur in the term, about which the rules assume only that they lie above $v$. The rules read it only through $u \prec {\vartriangle}v$, which holds iff $\Gamma \vdash u \preccurlyeq v$. So each bound lies below ${\vartriangle}\top$, a point $x$ lies below ${\vartriangle}\bot$ never, and $\bot$ always.
ty.up.why: A closure body is typed once for each call, and the body does not contain the continuation of the caller. E-App guarantees only that the caller acts above the upper point $u$ of the closure. The set of points that $\Gamma$ derives above $u$ would be the wrong condition, because the points of the caller need not occur in $\Gamma$. In the semantics ${\vartriangle}u$ stands for an arbitrary finite set of points above $u$. Readiness gets easier as the future shrinks, so the relation asks the same as $\Gamma \vdash u \preccurlyeq v$.
ty.up.example: An action at $u$ itself is allowed under ${\vartriangle}u$, because $u \preccurlyeq u$.

args.name: u
args.meaning: the bound compared with the rest, a point, $\bot$ or $\top$

deviations.reason: The Rocq writes the rest of a future as `RAbove v` for ${\vartriangle}v$, `RAll` for ${\vartriangle}\bot$ and no rest for ${\vartriangle}\top$, and compares by `rest_below`, which is $x \preccurlyeq v$, false and true in the three cases.

ctx.fl-w.title: Ord-World
ctx.fl-w.meaning: A fact of the order $\prec_W$ of the world holds under each $\Gamma$.
ctx.fl-w.why: The world states what the derivation assumes about the constants of its interface, and its order contains program order.
ctx.fl-w.breaks: Without it no derivation reads the world, and no thread holds two ends in sequence.

ctx.fl-h.title: Ord-Fact
ctx.fl-h.meaning: A fact of an instance $C[\bar x]$ in $\Gamma$ holds.
ctx.fl-h.why: A box body and the scope of an opened existential refer to their points only through these instances.
ctx.fl-h.breaks: Without it a box body could use no fact of its constraint.
ctx.fl-h.signature: C[\bar x] \in \Gamma \land (x \prec y) \in C[\bar x] \Rightarrow \Gamma \vdash x \prec y

ctx.fl-trans.title: Ord-Trans
ctx.fl-trans.why: A waiting chain combines facts of the world and of several instances.
ctx.fl-trans.signature: \Gamma \vdash x \prec y \land \Gamma \vdash y \prec z \Rightarrow \Gamma \vdash x \prec z

th.ptyped-apart.title: Renaming two components apart
th.ptyped-apart.meaning: Two derivations $\Sigma_1 \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_1} p_1 : T_1$ and $\Sigma_2 \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_2} p_2 : T_2$ have bijections $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ on constants, each the identity on the constants of its interface, such that $\Sigma_i \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{\pi_i W_i} p_i : T_i$ and the two renamed worlds share only constants of both interfaces.
th.ptyped-apart.why: P-Connect has no premise that keeps private constants apart. When two components use one private constant for unrelated points and their join is inconsistent, renaming them first gives a join with fewer facts. \inmode{lf}{No excluded middle and no choice enter the proof.}
th.ptyped-apart.breaks: Nothing. It is a lemma about derivations.
th.ptyped-apart.example: Renaming the constant $0$ of $P^{\prime}(e, f)$ to $1$ before it connects to $P(c, d)$.
th.ptyped-apart.signature: \Sigma_1 \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_1} p_1 : T_1 \land \Sigma_2 \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{W_2} p_2 : T_2 \Rightarrow \exists \pi_1, \pi_2.\ \Sigma_i \vdash\inmode{lf}{^{N}}_{\pi_i W_i} p_i : T_i \land A'_1 \cap A'_2 \subseteq \mathsf{I}(\Sigma_1, T_1) \cap \mathsf{I}(\Sigma_2, T_2)

args.name: \pi_1, \pi_2
args.meaning: bijections on constants, $\pi_i$ the identity on $\mathsf{I}(\Sigma_i, T_i)$

args.name: A'_1, A'_2
args.meaning: the bases of $\pi_1 W_1$ and of $\pi_2 W_2$

args.name: W_1, W_2
args.meaning: the worlds of the two derivations

th.lf-soundness-run.title: Lock-free soundness with a run
th.lf-soundness-run.meaning: Assume excluded middle, dependent choice and functional choice. A closed process typed at a finite bound $N$ is lock free, and a run $(r, l)$ with $\mathsf{erase}(r\,0) = p$, $\mathsf{maximal}\,(r, l)$ and $\mathsf{wfair}\,(r, l)$ exists. Such a run exists for each configuration $q$, as $r\,0 = q$, and typing plays no part in its existence.
th.lf-soundness-run.why: Lock freedom quantifies over the weakly fair maximal runs of $p$, and a statement over no run would hold of each process. The scheduler goes round robin over thread numbers and at each position takes a step of the targeted thread when that thread is enabled. Dependent choice picks the steps and excluded middle decides enabledness. So the lock-free theorems are not vacuous.
th.lf-soundness-run.example: Two threads $\ast$ and $\ast$ start a maximal weakly fair run.
th.lf-soundness-run.signature: \mathsf{EM} \land \mathsf{DC} \land \mathsf{FC} \land \varnothing \vdash^{N}_{W} p : T \land N \in \mathbb{N} \Rightarrow \mathsf{lock\_free}\,p \land \exists (r, l).\ \mathsf{erase}\,(r\,0) = p \land \mathsf{maximal}\,(r, l) \land \mathsf{wfair}\,(r, l)

args.name: \mathsf{EM}
args.meaning: excluded middle, $P \lor \lnot P$ for each proposition $P$, a hypothesis and no axiom

args.name: \mathsf{DC}
args.meaning: dependent choice, a total relation on a type has an infinite chain from each element, a hypothesis and no axiom

args.name: \mathsf{FC}
args.meaning: functional choice, a total relation contains a function, a hypothesis and no axiom

args.name: (r, l)
args.meaning: a run, $r\,i$ the configuration and $l\,i$ the event at position $i$

deviations.reason: $\mathsf{EM}$, $\mathsf{DC}$ and $\mathsf{FC}$ abbreviate the hypotheses `excluded_middle`, `dependent_choice` and `functional_choice`. The run is `fair_run_exists_proc`, which holds for each process.

examples.title: Client and server cycle
examples.lead: Two loops that call themselves forever over the same two channels are deadlock free, because one box constraint orders the points of their infinitely many rounds at once. It shows [[r-boxes|E-Box and E-Force]] with an infinite constraint, [[r-new|E-New-Field]], and [[th-sound|soundness]].
examples.meaning: A client sends on $a$ and then receives on $b$, and a server receives on $a$ and then sends on $b$, both forever. The second $\mathsf{new}$ places $b$ at the field $\rho\cdot 0$ of the base of $a$ and states the facts $C$ at $(\rho, \rho\cdot 0, \rho\cdot 1)$. Each recursive call is at the next points $(\iota^{+}, \kappa^{+}, \zeta)$, where $C$ states the same facts again.

examples.title: Cycle
examples.lead: Two threads that use two channels in the same order type, because creating the second channel states the two order facts the threads need. It is the smallest use of [[r-new|E-New]] with a constraint and of the [[t-side|side conditions]].
examples.code:
cycle = let ⟨c, c′⟩ = new in          -- c at ρ
        let ⟨d, d′⟩ = new in          -- d at ρ·0, C = {ρ ≺ (ρ·0)‾, ρ‾ ≺ ρ·0}
        let ∗ = spawn (λu. let ∗ = u in let ∗ = close c′ in close d′) in
        let ∗ = close c in close d
examples.meaning: Main closes $c$ and then $d$, and the spawned thread closes $c'$ and then $d'$. Each thread waits on one channel while it holds an end of the other. The second $\mathsf{new}$ states exactly the two facts this requires, $\rho \prec \overline{\rho\cdot 0}$ for main and $\overline{\rho} \prec \rho\cdot 0$ for the spawned thread.

examples.title: A channel between two box arguments
examples.lead: A procedure can create a channel whose point lies between the points of two channels it receives as arguments, by [[r-new|E-New-Field]] at a field of an argument point and the [[r-boxes|box constraint]].
examples.code:
between : □(∀ι κ. C. ∗ ⊸ Close_ι ⊗ Close_κ ⊸^κ ∗)
between = !(f = λp. let ⟨c, e⟩ = p in
                    let ⟨d, d′⟩ = new in        -- d at ι·0
                    let ∗ = spawn (λu. let ∗ = u in close d′) in
                    let ∗ = close c in let ∗ = close d in close e)
-- C = {ι ≺ κ, ι ≺ κ‾, ι ≺ δ‾, δ ≺ κ, δ ≺ κ‾},  δ = ι·0
main: c by new at ρ, e by new at ρ·1, force between at (ρ, ρ·1)
examples.meaning: The box creates a channel $d$ while it holds two arguments $c$ and $e$, and closes $c$, $d$ and $e$ in this order. E-New places $d$ at the field $\iota\cdot 0$ of the point of $c$. The facts of the box constraint then order $d$ between $c$ and $e$, and no point between two box points is needed.

examples.title: A channel that acts several times
examples.lead: A new channel can act several times while an older end is held, because a [[r-boxes|box constraint]] may state infinitely many facts, one per offset of the new point.
examples.code:
many = !(f = λp. let ⟨c, e⟩ = p in
                 let ⟨d, d′⟩ = new in         -- d at δ
                 let ∗ = spawn (λu. let ∗ = u in
                      let ⟨v, d′⟩ = recv d′ in let ∗ = v in
                      let ⟨w, d′⟩ = recv d′ in let ∗ = w in close d′) in
                 let ∗ = close c in
                 let ∗ = close (send ⟨∗, send ⟨∗, d⟩⟩) in close e)
